summary: Arithmetic dynamics, first pass, planned from free sources against the pinned libraries, with the two DeMarco papers whose accepted source routes name these layers covered. DY.0 builds self-maps of the projective line from coprime homogeneous forms on Mathlib's iteration and periodic points: the action on points, iterates, the binary resultant with its Nullstellensatz certificate and its behaviour under conjugation, PGL₂-conjugacy, fixed points, multipliers and critical points with multiplicity, good reduction, and the moduli spaces M_d and M_d^cm with Milnor's M₂ ≅ 𝔸² (the scheme structure waits for a GIT owner). DY.1 builds Tate's limit and the Call–Silverman canonical height for a polarised morphism, its P¹ form normalised against Mathlib's Weil height (the ClassicalArithmeticCompletion request), uniqueness, the zero-height criterion, Northcott for preperiodic points, and the comparisons with Tau Ceti's elliptic canonical height and with multiplication on abelian varieties. DY.2 builds escape rates and local canonical heights at every place with their decomposition of the global height, good reduction through the escape rate, reduction of cycles and multipliers with the residue characteristic retained, and the canonical measure with Δλ = µ − δ_∞ over the Berkovich line requested from TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic. DY.3 builds period and dynatomic polynomials with formal versus exact period and effectivity, the dynatomic curves Y₁(n), Northcott finiteness of bounded-degree preperiodic points, the rational preperiodic classification for z² + c with its computational inputs requested, certified enumeration, and the uniform boundedness conjecture as a statement only. DY.4 builds adelic measures and metrics on P¹, energies and the Arakelov–Zhang pairing, the Favre–Rivera-Letelier equidistribution theorem for small points, Yuan's theorem as a stated endpoint, dynamical equidistribution, the vanishing of the dynamical pairing and equidistribution of PCF parameters. DY.5 builds rooted-tree automorphism groups, preimage trees and the arboreal Galois representation, the discriminant and stability criteria, Stoll's maximality criterion with the fully worked x² + 1 over ℚ, Jones's ramification criterion and Odoni's theorem. DY.6 builds power maps and Lattès maps with their canonical heights, Call–Silverman specialisation and Tate's variation theorem, the critical height and Ingram's comparison with a moduli height, DeMarco–Krieger–Ye's uniform bound for common torsion images of Legendre pairs, and the proven dynamical Mordell–Lang cases, with the open conjectures stated and never consumed. Remaining work is listed per layer, with seventeen gaps and twenty-six requests to other owners.

nodes.title: The forward orbit of a point under a self-map
nodes.statement: For a type α, a self-map f : α → α and x : α, the forward orbit of x is O_f(x) = {f^n(x) : n ∈ ℕ} (with f^0(x) = x), the range of the orbit map ℕ → α, n ↦ f^[n] x (Mathlib's iterate `Nat.iterate`).
hypotheses: α any type; no structure on α is used.
n = 0 is included, so x ∈ O_f(x).
proofSteps: Define O_f(x) as Set.range (n ↦ f^[n] x).
Membership: y ∈ O_f(x) iff y = f^[n] x for some n (definition of range).
Forward invariance f(O_f(x)) ⊆ O_f(x) and O_f(x) = {x} ∪ O_f(f x) from f^[n+1] x = f^[n] (f x) (Function.iterate_succ_apply').
Functoriality: if g ∘ fa = fb ∘ g (Function.Semiconj g fa fb) then g ∘ fa^[n] = fb^[n] ∘ g (Function.Semiconj.iterate_right), so g(O_fa(x)) = O_fb(g x).
acceptance: Under n ↦ n + 1 on ℕ the orbit of 0 is ℕ; under the identity every orbit is a singleton.
Under z ↦ z² − 1 on ℤ the orbit of 1 is {1, 0, −1} (Silverman, AWS notes, Example 2).

sources.excerpt: The orbit of x is the set of points obtained by applying the iterates of ϕ to x. It is denoted Oϕ(x) = {x, ϕ(x), ϕ2(x), ϕ3(x), . . .}.

nodes.statement: For f : α → α, a point x is preperiodic (IsPreperiodicPt f x) if some iterate f^[m] x lies in Mathlib's periodicPts f, i.e. f^[m + n] x = f^[m] x for some m and some n ≥ 1. The preperiodic points form preperiodicPts f ⊇ periodicPts f.
hypotheses: α any type.
Period n ≥ 1 (a periodic point of period 0 is excluded, as in Mathlib's periodicPts).
proofSteps: Define IsPreperiodicPt f x := ∃ m, f^[m] x ∈ Function.periodicPts f and preperiodicPts f := {x | IsPreperiodicPt f x}.
Periodic points are preperiodic (m = 0); x preperiodic iff f x preperiodic (shift m by one, using Function.IsPeriodicPt.apply_iterate).
On a finite type every point is preperiodic, by pigeonhole on the orbit map (Finite.exists_ne_map_eq_of_infinite).
For g ↦ g^d on a group with d ≥ 2: g^{d^{m+n}} = g^{d^m} with n ≥ 1 gives g^{d^m(d^n − 1)} = 1, so g has finite order; conversely if g has order N the powers d^m mod N repeat.
acceptance: 1 is preperiodic but not periodic for z ↦ z² − 1 on ℤ; 2 is wandering (Silverman, AWS notes, Example 2).
For g ↦ g^d (d ≥ 2) on a group the preperiodic points are the torsion elements (AWS notes, Exercise A).

nodes.title: Preperiodic iff the forward orbit is finite
nodes.statement: For f : α → α and x : α: IsPreperiodicPt f x ↔ (forwardOrbit f x).Finite.
hypotheses: α any type.
proofSteps: (⇒) If f^[m + n] x = f^[m] x with n ≥ 1, every f^[k] x with k ≥ m equals f^[m + ((k − m) mod n)] x (Function.IsPeriodicPt.iterate_mod_apply applied at f^[m] x), so O_f(x) ⊆ {f^[k] x : k < m + n}, a finite set (Set.Finite.subset).
(⇐) If O_f(x) is finite the orbit map ℕ → O_f(x) is not injective (Finite.exists_ne_map_eq_of_infinite): f^[i] x = f^[j] x with i < j, so f^[i] x is periodic of period j − i.
acceptance: For z ↦ z² − 1 on ℤ, O(1) = {1, 0, −1} is finite and O(2) is infinite.

sources.excerpt: We recall that a point P is called pre-periodic for φ if its orbit {P, φ(P), φ²(P), φ³(P), . . .} is finite. (Equivalently, P is pre-periodic if some iterate φ^i(P) is periodic.)

nodes.title: Semiconjugacies preserve preperiodic points
nodes.statement: (a) If g : α → β satisfies g ∘ fa = fb ∘ g (Function.Semiconj g fa fb) and x is preperiodic for fa, then g x is preperiodic for fb. (b) If moreover g is bijective, x is preperiodic for fa iff g x is preperiodic for fb.
hypotheses: No hypothesis on α, β; (b) needs g bijective.
proofSteps: (a) From f^[m] x ∈ periodicPts fa and Function.IsPeriodicPt.map (with Function.Semiconj.iterate_right to move g past fa^[m]) get fb^[m] (g x) = g (fa^[m] x) ∈ periodicPts fb.
(b) The inverse of a bijective semiconjugacy semiconjugates fb to fa; apply (a) to it.
acceptance: Conjugation by a Möbius map identifies the preperiodic points of ϕ and ϕ^f (Silverman, AWS notes, Exercise D).

sources.excerpt: Prove that α ∈ P1(C) is periodic for ϕ of period n if and only if f^{−1}(α) is periodic for ϕ^f of period n. In particular, there is a natural identification of Per(ϕ, P1(C)) with Per(ϕ^f, P1(C)). Formulate and prove an analogous statement for preperiodic points.

nodes.title: Iterates of an endomorphism act on points by its powers
nodes.statement: Let C be a category, X, T objects and φ ∈ End X (Mathlib's monoid CategoryTheory.End X). For every T-point P : T ⟶ X and n ∈ ℕ, (Q ↦ Q ≫ φ)^[n] P = P ≫ φ^n. Consequently P is periodic of period n for Q ↦ Q ≫ φ iff P ≫ φ^n = P: the iterates of a morphism of schemes (C = schemes over S, T = Spec K) are the powers φ^n in End X, and equality of iterates is equality of morphisms.
hypotheses: Any category; φ^n is the power in CategoryTheory.End X, whose product is xs * ys = ys ≫ xs (CategoryTheory.End.mul_def).
proofSteps: Induction on n: the case n = 0 is P ≫ 𝟙 = P; for n + 1 use Function.iterate_succ_apply', φ^(n+1) = φ^n * φ = φ ≫ φ^n (pow_succ' and CategoryTheory.End.mul_def) and associativity of composition.
The periodicity statement is the case of Function.IsPeriodicPt unfolded with the first identity.
acceptance: For C = Type and T = a point, the statement is Mathlib's Function.End pow = iterate.
For X = P¹_K the powers of the scheme morphism of a rational map f are the morphisms of f^n (DY.0/rational-map-to-scheme-endomorphism).

nodes.title: The resultant of a pair of binary forms
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring R, binary forms F, G ∈ R[X₀, X₁] and formal degrees m, n ∈ ℕ, Res_{m,n}(F, G) := Polynomial.resultant F(X, 1) G(X, 1) m n, Mathlib's (m + n) × (m + n) Sylvester determinant of the dehomogenisations F(X, 1) = aeval ![X, 1] F. For a homogeneous lift (F₀, F₁) of a degree-d rational map the resultant is Res_d(F₀, F₁) := Res_{d,d}(F₀, F₁); since Res_{d,d}(cF₀, cF₁) = c^{2d} Res_{d,d}(F₀, F₁), the resultant of the map is defined up to (K^×)^{2d}, and its valuation on a normalised lift is well defined. Orientation (pinned): Res_{d,d}(X₀^d, X₁^d) = 1 and Res_{d,d}(X₁^d, X₀^d) = (−1)^d; for m = n = d this is the determinant of Silverman (AWS notes, Example 23), Rumely ((1)) and Milnor (Appendix A).
hypotheses: R commutative; F, G arbitrary (in applications homogeneous of degrees m, n, so that F(X, 1), G(X, 1) have degree ≤ m, n).
Formal degrees are explicit: they matter when a leading coefficient vanishes (a root at ∞).
proofSteps: Define binaryResultant m n F G := Polynomial.resultant (aeval ![X, 1] F) (aeval ![X, 1] G) m n.
Compatibility with Mathlib's homogenisation: aeval ![X, 1] (homogenize f m) = f when deg f ≤ m (Polynomial.aeval_homogenize_X_one), so Res_{m,n}(homogenize f m, homogenize g n) = resultant f g m n.

Scaling: Res_{m,n}(cF, G) = c^n Res and Res_{m,n}(F, cG) = c^m Res (Polynomial.resultant_C_mul_left, Polynomial.resultant_C_mul_right); symmetry (Polynomial.resultant_comm); base change (Polynomial.resultant_map_map); Res_{m,n}(0, G) = 0 for n ≠ 0 (Polynomial.resultant_zero_left).

Res_{d,d}(X₀^d, X₁^d) = resultant (X^d) 1 d d = 1 (Polynomial.resultant_X_pow_left); for a polynomial p of degree n, Res_{n,n} of Mathlib's toTupleMvPolynomial p is lead(p)^n (repeat Polynomial.resultant_succ_left_deg on the constant second form).
acceptance: Res_{1,1}(aX₀ + bX₁, cX₀ + eX₁) = ae − bc (Milnor, Appendix A).
Res_{2,2}(X₀² + 2X₁², X₀X₁) = 2: the displayed resultant of (z² + 2)/z, which vanishes modulo 2 (acceptance example, see DY.0/good-reduction-of-a-rational-map).
For quadratic forms the value is Silverman's polynomial a₂²b₀² − a₂a₁b₁b₀ + a₁²b₂b₀ − 2a₂a₀b₂b₀ + a₂a₀b₁² − a₁a₀b₂b₁ + a₀²b₂² (AWS notes, Example 23).

nodes.title: Bimultiplicativity of the binary resultant
nodes.statement: For binary forms over a commutative ring with F₁, F₂, G homogeneous of degrees m₁, m₂, n: Res_{m₁+m₂,n}(F₁F₂, G) = Res_{m₁,n}(F₁, G) · Res_{m₂,n}(F₂, G); symmetrically Res_{m,n₁+n₂}(F, G₁G₂) = Res_{m,n₁}(F, G₁) · Res_{m,n₂}(F, G₂).
hypotheses: Homogeneity gives deg F_i(X, 1) ≤ m_i and deg G(X, 1) ≤ n (MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous.totalDegree_le).
proofSteps: Dehomogenisation is a ring homomorphism, so (F₁F₂)(X, 1) = F₁(X, 1)F₂(X, 1).

With k_i = m_i − deg F_i(X, 1), Polynomial.resultant_add_left_deg moves the formal degree m_i to the actual degree at the cost of the factor (−1)^{n k_i} g_n^{k_i}, where g_n is the coefficient of X^n in G(X, 1).

At actual degrees Mathlib's Polynomial.resultant_mul_left gives the product formula; the correction factors for F₁F₂ are the products of those for F₁ and F₂ (natDegree of a product ≤ the sum, Polynomial.natDegree_mul_le).
The second formula follows from the first by Polynomial.resultant_comm (or directly from Polynomial.resultant_mul_right and Polynomial.resultant_add_right_deg).
acceptance: X₀X₁ against X₀ + X₁: Res_{2,1}(X₀X₁, X₀ + X₁) = Res_{1,1}(X₀, X₀ + X₁) · Res_{1,1}(X₁, X₀ + X₁) = 1 · (−1) = −1.

sources.excerpt: The resultant result_{m,n}(p, q), can be characterized as the unique function from V_m × V_n to C which is bimultiplicative result_{m1+m2,n}(p1 · p2, q) = result_{m1,n}(p1, q) · result_{m2,n}(p2, q)
sources.match: Exactly the formula, with formal degrees.

nodes.title: Binary forms split into linear forms over an algebraically closed field
nodes.statement: Let K be algebraically closed and G ∈ K[X₀, X₁] nonzero and homogeneous of degree n. Then G = ∏_{i=1}^{n} (a_i X₀ + b_i X₁) with (a_i, b_i) ≠ (0, 0); the points [−b_i : a_i] ∈ ℙ¹(K) are the zeros of G, the point ∞ = [1 : 0] occurring n − deg G(X, 1) times.
hypotheses: K algebraically closed; G ≠ 0 homogeneous of degree n.
proofSteps: g = G(X, 1) is nonzero of degree k ≤ n, and G = homogenize g n (Polynomial.homogenize_eq_of_isHomogeneous).
g splits (IsAlgClosed.splits_domain): g = lead(g) ∏_{r ∈ roots g} (X − r) (Polynomial.C_leadingCoeff_mul_prod_multiset_X_sub_C).

Homogenising the product with the degrees 1 for each factor and n − k for the constant (Polynomial.homogenize_finsetProd, Polynomial.homogenize_C) gives lead(g) X₁^{n−k} ∏ (X₀ − r X₁); absorb lead(g) into one factor.
acceptance: X₀X₁² = X₀ · X₁ · X₁ (zeros [0 : 1] once and ∞ twice).
X₀² + X₁² = (X₀ + iX₁)(X₀ − iX₁) over ℚ̄, with no factorisation over ℚ.

sources.excerpt: More generally, whenever the leading coefficient a0 is non-zero, we can factor p as p(z) = a0 (z −ξ1) · · · (z −ξm)

nodes.title: The resultant vanishes exactly at a common zero
nodes.statement: Let K be a field, d ≥ 1 and F₀, F₁ ∈ K[X₀, X₁] homogeneous of degree d. Then Res_{d,d}(F₀, F₁) = 0 iff F₀ and F₁ have a common zero x ∈ K̄² ∖ {0} (K̄ = AlgebraicClosure K), i.e. a common zero in ℙ¹(K̄).
hypotheses: d ≥ 1 (in degree 0 the resultant is 1 for every pair).
Homogeneity of degree exactly d with formal degrees d, d.
proofSteps: Base change to K̄ does not change whether the resultant vanishes (Polynomial.resultant_map_map, injectivity of K → K̄).
If F₀ = 0 (or F₁ = 0) the resultant is 0 (Polynomial.resultant_zero_left) and the other form has a zero in ℙ¹(K̄) by DY.0/binary-form-factorisation (d ≥ 1).
Otherwise factor F₀ = ∏ ℓ_i and F₁ = ∏ m_j into linear forms (DY.0/binary-form-factorisation) and expand by DY.0/binary-resultant-mul: Res = ∏_{i,j} Res_{1,1}(ℓ_i, m_j).

Res_{1,1}(aX₀ + bX₁, cX₀ + eX₁) = ae − bc (2 × 2 Sylvester determinant, Matrix.det_fin_two) vanishes iff the two linear forms are proportional iff they have the same zero; so Res = 0 iff some ℓ_i and m_j share a zero.
acceptance: (X₀², X₀X₁) share [0 : 1] and Res = 0; (X₀², X₁²) have resultant 1.
(X₀(X₀² + X₁²), X₁(X₀² + X₁²)) over ℚ: no common zero in ℙ¹(ℚ), but the common zeros [±i : 1] over ℚ̄ make Res_{3,3} = 0; the criterion is over K̄, not K.

sources.excerpt: In fact the resultant result_{m,n}(p, q) is zero if and only if either: (1) the two polynomials p and q have a root in common, or (2) both deg(p) < m and deg(q) < n.

nodes.title: The resultant under a linear change of the pair of forms
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring R, a matrix A ∈ M₂(R) and binary forms F₀, F₁ homogeneous of degree d: Res_{d,d}(A₀₀F₀ + A₀₁F₁, A₁₀F₀ + A₁₁F₁) = det(A)^d · Res_{d,d}(F₀, F₁).
hypotheses: R commutative; F_j homogeneous of degree d.
proofSteps: The Sylvester matrix is linear in the coefficient vectors of both polynomials (Polynomial.sylvester): its first d columns carry shifts of the second form, its last d columns shifts of the first.

Hence Syl(A·F) = Syl(F) · M where M is, after reindexing Fin (d + d) ≃ Fin 2 × Fin d, the Kronecker product of the 2 × 2 matrix of A (with rows and columns ordered as in the Sylvester blocks) with the d × d identity.
det M = det(A)^d (Matrix.det_kronecker, Matrix.det_reindex_self), and Matrix.det_mul gives the claim.
acceptance: A = diag(c, c): Res(cF₀, cF₁) = c^{2d} Res (Rumely).
A = [[0, 1], [1, 0]] (det −1): Res(F₁, F₀) = (−1)^d Res(F₀, F₁), in agreement with binaryResultant_comm since (−1)^{d·d} = (−1)^d.

sources.excerpt: This function is (−1)^{mn}-symmetric and bihomogeneous of degree (n, m), that is result_{m,n}(p, q) = (−1)^{mn} result_{n,m}(q, p), result_{m,n}(λp, µq) = λ^n µ^m result_{m,n}(p, q).
sources.match: The diagonal and swap cases; the general linear case is their common extension.

sources.excerpt: For any c ∈ K×, we have Res(cF, cG) = c^{2d} Res(F, G).
sources.match: The scalar case A = cI.

nodes.title: The resultant under a linear substitution of the variables
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring R, A ∈ M₂(R) and binary forms F₀, F₁ homogeneous of degree d, write F∘A for the substitution X_i ↦ Σ_j A_ij X_j (linearSubst A). Then Res_{d,d}(F₀∘A, F₁∘A) = det(A)^{d²} · Res_{d,d}(F₀, F₁).
hypotheses: R commutative; F_j homogeneous of degree d.
proofSteps: Universal identity: both sides are integer polynomials in the entries of A and the coefficients of F; by Polynomial.resultant_map_map it suffices to prove it for the universal forms over ℤ[a, b, A], hence over the algebraic closure of its fraction field (an injective ring map).

Over an algebraically closed field factor F₀ = ∏_i ℓ_i and F₁ = ∏_j m_j into linear forms (DY.0/binary-form-factorisation; if a form is 0 both sides vanish by Polynomial.resultant_zero_left); then F_k∘A factor as ∏ (ℓ_i∘A) and ∏ (m_j∘A).
Expand both sides by DY.0/binary-resultant-mul into d² factors Res_{1,1}(ℓ_i∘A, m_j∘A) and Res_{1,1}(ℓ_i, m_j).
For linear forms, Res_{1,1}(ℓ∘A, m∘A) = det(A) · Res_{1,1}(ℓ, m): the coefficient matrix of (ℓ∘A, m∘A) is that of (ℓ, m) times A (Matrix.det_fin_two, Matrix.det_mul).
acceptance: A = diag(a, 1) on (X₀^d, X₁^d): Res(a^d X₀^d, X₁^d) = (a^d)^d = a^{d²}.
A = [[0, 1], [1, 0]] on (X₀^d, X₁^d) gives Res(X₁^d, X₀^d) = (−1)^{d²} = (−1)^d.

sources.excerpt: Similarly, if b0 ≠ 0 then we can set q(z) = b0 (z − η1) · · · (z − ηn) and write result(p, q) = (−1)^{mn} b0^m ∏_{j=1}^{n} p(ηj) = a0^n b0^m ∏_{i=1}^{m} ∏_{j=1}^{n} (ξi − ηj).
sources.match: The product formula over the roots, which the linear substitution multiplies factorwise by det(A).

sources.excerpt: It is known (see ([25], Exercise 2.7(c), p.76) that Res(F^γ, G^γ) = Res(F, G) · det(γ)^{d²+d}
sources.match: The combined formula, of which this is the d² part.

nodes.title: The resultant of a conjugated lift
nodes.statement: For A ∈ M₂(R) and binary forms F₀, F₁ of degree d, Rumely's homogeneous conjugate F^A := adj(A) ∘ F ∘ A, (F^A)_i = Σ_j adj(A)_ij (F_j∘A), satisfies Res_{d,d}(F^A_0, F^A_1) = det(A)^{d²+d} · Res_{d,d}(F₀, F₁).
hypotheses: R commutative; F_j homogeneous of degree d; A need not be invertible (for invertible A, F^A is a lift of the conjugate A^{-1}∘f∘A).
proofSteps: F_j∘A is homogeneous of degree d (MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous.aeval); apply DY.0/resultant-postcomp-linear with the matrix adj(A), whose determinant is det(A)^{2−1} = det(A) (Matrix.det_adjugate), giving det(A)^d · Res(F∘A).

nodes.title: The resultant as a Nullstellensatz certificate
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring R, d ≥ 1 and binary forms F₀, F₁ homogeneous of degree d, there are binary forms G_{k,j} (k, j ∈ {0, 1}) homogeneous of degree d − 1 with G_{k,0}F₀ + G_{k,1}F₁ = Res_{d,d}(F₀, F₁) · X_k^{2d−1} for k = 0, 1. In particular, over a field, if Res ≠ 0 then F₀(x) = F₁(x) = 0 forces x = 0, and q_{k,j} = G_{k,j}/Res is the certificate consumed by Mathlib's Height.logHeight_eval_ge with M = d − 1, N = d.
hypotheses: d ≥ 1; R commutative (no domain hypothesis).
proofSteps: Apply Polynomial.exists_mul_add_mul_eq_C_resultant to f = F₀(X, 1), g = F₁(X, 1) with formal degrees d, d (natDegree ≤ d by homogeneity): f·p + g·q = C(Res) with deg p, deg q < d.

Homogenise to degree 2d − 1 = d + (d − 1): F₀·homogenize p (d−1) + F₁·homogenize q (d−1) = Res·X₁^{2d−1} (Polynomial.homogenize_mul, Polynomial.homogenize_eq_of_isHomogeneous, Polynomial.homogenize_C); this is the case k = 1.

For k = 0 apply the case k = 1 to F∘σ with σ the swap of variables and substitute σ back; DY.0/resultant-precomp-linear gives Res(F∘σ) = det(σ)^{d²} Res(F) = (−1)^{d} Res(F), absorbed into the G_{0,j}.
If Res ≠ 0 over a field and F₀(x) = F₁(x) = 0 then Res·x_k^{2d−1} = 0 for both k, so x = 0.
acceptance: F = (X₀², X₁²): Res = 1 and the certificate is X₀·X₀² + 0 = X₀³, 0 + X₁·X₁² = X₁³.
F = (X₀² + 2X₁², X₀X₁): Res = 2 and 2X₁³ = X₁·(X₀² + 2X₁²) − X₀·(X₀X₁).

nodes.title: Homogeneous lifts of a degree-d self-map of ℙ¹
nodes.statement: For a field K and d ∈ ℕ, HomogeneousLift K d is the type of pairs F = (F₀, F₁) of binary forms in K[X₀, X₁], homogeneous of degree d, not both zero, with Res_{d,d}(F₀, F₁) ≠ 0. Evaluation F(x) = (F₀(x), F₁(x)) satisfies F(x) ≠ 0 for x ≠ 0 and F(cx) = c^d F(x). Constructors: scaling by c ∈ K^×, the identity (X₀, X₁), polynomial maps (Mathlib's toTupleMvPolynomial), invertible matrices (degree 1) and base change along field homomorphisms.
hypotheses: K a field.
The condition 'not both zero' only matters for d = 0 (for d ≥ 1 it follows from Res ≠ 0).
By DY.0/binary-resultant-eq-zero-iff, for d ≥ 1 the condition Res ≠ 0 says that F₀, F₁ have no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. no common factor.
proofSteps: Define the structure with fields forms, isHomogeneous, forms_ne_zero, binaryResultant_ne_zero.
eval_ne_zero: by DY.0/resultant-certificate, Res·x_k^{2d−1} = Σ_j G_{k,j}(x)F_j(x) = 0 for both k if F(x) = 0, so x = 0 (d ≥ 1); for d = 0, F(x) = (F₀, F₁) ≠ 0.
eval_smul: homogeneity (MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous gives F(cx) = c^d F(x)).

ofPolynomial: Mathlib's toTupleMvPolynomial p is a pair of forms of degree natDegree p with resultant lead(p)^{natDegree p} (binaryResultant_toTupleMvPolynomial), nonzero for p ≠ 0, and equal to 1 for p = 0 (natDegree 0, pair (0, 1)).
ofGL γ = (γ₀₀X₀ + γ₀₁X₁, γ₁₀X₀ + γ₁₁X₁) has resultant det γ ≠ 0 (the linear case of DY.0/resultant-of-a-rational-map).
map σ: MvPolynomial.map σ preserves homogeneity (MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous.map) and Res (Polynomial.resultant_map_map, σ injective).
acceptance: (X₀², X₁²) is a lift of z ↦ z² (resultant 1); (X₀², X₀X₁) is not (common zero [0 : 1]).
(X₀² + 2X₁², X₀X₁) is a lift over ℚ of (z² + 2)/z.

sources.excerpt: Then there are homogeneous polynomials F(X, Y ), G(X, Y ) ∈K[X, Y ] of degree d, having no common factor, such that the map [X : Y ] ↦ [F(X, Y ) : G(X, Y )] gives the action of ϕ on P1.

nodes.title: Composition of homogeneous lifts
nodes.statement: For lifts F of degree d and G of degree e over a field K, F ∘ G := (F₀(G₀, G₁), F₁(G₀, G₁)) (MvPolynomial.aeval G.forms) is a lift of degree d·e, with (F ∘ G)(x) = F(G(x)); composition is associative up to equality of forms, (X₀, X₁) is a two-sided unit, and scaling F scales F ∘ G.
hypotheses: K a field; F, G lifts of degrees d, e (any d, e ∈ ℕ).
proofSteps: Homogeneity: F_i(G₀, G₁) is homogeneous of degree e·d (MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous.aeval); rewrite e·d = d·e.

Nonvanishing: if some x ≠ 0 in K̄² were a common zero of F ∘ G, then y = G(x) ≠ 0 (DY.0/binary-resultant-eq-zero-iff for G over K̄) and F(y) = 0 (the same for F): a contradiction; so Res(F ∘ G) ≠ 0 by DY.0/binary-resultant-eq-zero-iff for d·e ≥ 1 (for d·e = 0 one of the lifts is constant and the composite is a nonzero constant pair).
eval_comp: evaluation of aeval is composition (MvPolynomial.eval of aeval).
Associativity and units: aeval is associative under substitution (MvPolynomial.bind₁ is a monad), aeval ![X₀, X₁] = id.
acceptance: (X₀², X₁²) ∘ (X₀², X₁²) = (X₀⁴, X₁⁴).
(X₀², X₁²) ∘ (X₀ + X₁, X₁) = ((X₀ + X₁)², X₁²) ≠ (X₀² + X₁², X₁²) = (X₀ + X₁, X₁) ∘ (X₀², X₁²).

nodes.title: Rational self-maps of ℙ¹ over a field
nodes.statement: For a field K, RationalMap K is the quotient of Σ_d HomogeneousLift K d by the relation 'same degree and proportional forms'. Its degree is the degree of any lift. Composition of lifts makes RationalMap K a monoid (unit: the class of (X₀, X₁)), with deg(f g) = deg f · deg g, so f^n is the n-th iterate as a map (not merely on points). Polynomial maps p ↦ z ↦ p(z) embed K[X] (under composition) via Mathlib's toTupleMvPolynomial, and f ↦ F₀(X, 1)/F₁(X, 1) ∈ RatFunc K is injective.
hypotheses: K a field.
Maps of degree 0 are the constants, one for each point of ℙ¹(K); Rat_d(K) is {f | deg f = d}.
proofSteps: Define the setoid on Σ_d HomogeneousLift K d and RationalMap K as its quotient; mk F is the class of F and degree is the first component (well defined).

Monoid: mul on representatives is DY.0/homogeneous-lift-comp; well defined because (cF) ∘ G = c(F ∘ G) and F ∘ (cG) = c^d (F ∘ G) (homogeneity); associativity and units from the corresponding lift identities.

ofPolynomial p is mk (HomogeneousLift.ofPolynomial p) (for p = 0 the lift (0, 1) is the constant 0); ofPolynomial (p ∘ q) = ofPolynomial p * ofPolynomial q because the composite of the lifts (homogenize p m, X₁^m) and (homogenize q n, X₁^n) is (homogenize (p ∘ q) (mn), X₁^{mn}) (Polynomial.homogenize_mul).

toRatFunc f := F₀(X, 1)/F₁(X, 1) in RatFunc K (well defined on the class). For deg f ≥ 1, F₁(X, 1) ≠ 0 and Res ≠ 0 makes F₀(X, 1), F₁(X, 1) coprime with max(deg F₀(X, 1), deg F₁(X, 1)) = deg f, so f is recovered from the fraction; the constant map ∞ goes to Mathlib's junk value 0 = (1 : RatFunc K)/0, which is why injectivity is stated on {f | 1 ≤ deg f}.
acceptance: deg(z²) = 2 and (z²)^n = z^{2^n} as rational maps.
Over 𝔽_p, z^p ≠ z as rational maps although they agree on ℙ¹(𝔽_p) (see DY.0/rational-map-action-on-points).

sources.excerpt: A rational map ϕ(z) is a ratio of polynomials ϕ(z) = F(z) G(z) = a0 + a1z + · · · + adzd b0 + b1z + · · · + bdzd having no common factors. The degree of ϕ is deg ϕ = max{deg F, deg G}.
sources.match: The rational function of a map; our degree is the common degree d of the forms, equal to max{deg F, deg G} by the no-common-factor condition.

sources.excerpt: Evidently Rat_d is a Zariski open subset of the complex projective space CP^{2d+1} consisting of ratios (a0 : . . . : ad : b0 : . . . : bd).
sources.match: Rat_d is the set of lifts of degree d up to scaling, i.e. the degree-d part of RationalMap K.

sources.excerpt: A rational map from Pn to itself is determined by an (n + 1)-tuple of polynomials in n + 1 variables, all homogeneous of the same degree d.

nodes.title: The action of a rational map on ℙ¹(K)
nodes.statement: RationalMap.toEnd : RationalMap K →* Function.End (ℙ¹(K)) sends f = mk F to [x] ↦ [F(x)] on Mathlib's ℙ K (Fin 2 → K). It is a monoid homomorphism, so toEnd (f^n) = (toEnd f)^[n]. It is injective when K is infinite and not injective over finite fields.
hypotheses: K a field; ℙ¹(K) = Mathlib's Projectivization ℙ K (Fin 2 → K), with [x : 1] = mk ![x, 1] and ∞ = [1 : 0].
proofSteps: Well defined on points: F(x) ≠ 0 for x ≠ 0 (DY.0/homogeneous-lift, eval_ne_zero) and F(cx) = c^d F(x), so Projectivization.lift applies; scaling F does not change [F(x)] (Projectivization.mk_eq_mk_iff).
Multiplicativity from (F ∘ G)(x) = F(G(x)) (DY.0/homogeneous-lift-comp); powers are iterates since Function.End's power is iteration.

Injectivity for infinite K: if f, g of degrees d, e act identically then F₀G₁ − F₁G₀ vanishes on K², hence is 0 (MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous.funext), so F₀G₁ = F₁G₀; as F₀, F₁ have no common factor (Res ≠ 0) the lifts are proportional and d = e.
Over 𝔽_p, z^p fixes every point of ℙ¹(𝔽_p) (Fermat), so toEnd (z^p) = toEnd 1 while z^p ≠ 1.
acceptance: z² sends [2 : 1] to [4 : 1] and fixes ∞.
Over 𝔽_p, z^p and the identity have the same action but differ as rational maps.

nodes.title: Units of the monoid of rational maps: PGL₂
nodes.statement: The units of RationalMap K are exactly the maps of degree 1, and unitsEquivPGL : (RationalMap K)ˣ ≃* PGL(2, K) (Mathlib's Matrix.ProjGenLinGroup) sends the class of the linear lift of γ ∈ GL₂(K) to the class of γ; the action of a unit on ℙ¹(K) is Mathlib's action of PGL(2, K) on ℙ K (Fin 2 → K).
hypotheses: K a field.
proofSteps: deg is multiplicative with deg 1 = 1, so a unit has degree 1; a degree-1 lift (a X₀ + b X₁, c X₀ + e X₁) has resultant ae − bc ≠ 0 (DY.0/resultant-of-a-rational-map, linear case), i.e. is ofGL of an invertible matrix, with inverse the class of ofGL γ⁻¹.
The map GL₂(K) → (RationalMap K)ˣ, γ ↦ mk (ofGL γ) is a surjective homomorphism with kernel the scalars, which is the kernel of Matrix.ProjGenLinGroup.mk; this gives the MulEquiv.
Compatibility with points: toEnd (mk (ofGL γ)) [x] = [γ x] = Projectivization.PGL.mk_smul_mk.
acceptance: z ↦ 1/z (lift (X₁, X₀)) is a unit of order 2; z ↦ z + 1 is a unit of infinite order over ℚ; z² is not a unit.

sources.excerpt: These are the only automorphisms of P1(C), and two matrices give the same linear fractional transformation if and only if they are scalar multiples of one another, so Aut(P1(C)) = PGL2(C) = GL2(C)/C∗.

nodes.statement: For a field homomorphism σ : K → L, RationalMap.map σ : RationalMap K →* RationalMap L applies σ to the coefficients of a lift, and projMap σ : ℙ¹(K) → ℙ¹(L) applies σ to coordinates; both are injective, deg is preserved, and toEnd (map σ f) (projMap σ P) = projMap σ (toEnd f P). Over a field F algebraic over ℚ every rational map is the base change of a map over a number field L ⊆ F.
hypotheses: σ a ring homomorphism of fields (injective).
proofSteps: map on lifts is HomogeneousLift.map (DY.0/homogeneous-lift); it respects proportionality and composition (MvPolynomial.map commutes with aeval), giving a monoid homomorphism.
projMap σ [x] = [σ x] via Projectivization.lift (σ injective keeps σ x ≠ 0); compatibility with toEnd because MvPolynomial.eval (σ ∘ x) (map σ F) = σ (eval x F).

Field of definition: the finitely many coefficients of a lift generate L = ℚ(coefficients) (IntermediateField.adjoin), finite-dimensional because F is algebraic over ℚ (IntermediateField.finiteDimensional_adjoin); the lift has coefficients in L.

nodes.title: Rational maps as endomorphisms of the scheme ℙ¹_K
nodes.statement: For a field K there is an injective monoid homomorphism RationalMap K → End(ℙ¹_K) into the K-endomorphisms of the projective line ℙ¹_K = Proj K[X₀, X₁], sending mk F to the morphism [F₀ : F₁]; its action on K-points is RationalMap.toEnd and every K-endomorphism of ℙ¹_K is in the image. Hence f^n corresponds to the n-th power of a scheme morphism, and by DY.0/iterate-of-endomorphism-on-points iterate equality is equality of morphisms of schemes.
hypotheses: K a field; ℙ¹_K and the morphism attached to forms without common zero are supplied by SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0 (request).
proofSteps: Take the morphism [F₀ : F₁] of the supplier for each lift; proportional lifts give the same morphism, composites of forms give composites of morphisms, (X₀, X₁) gives the identity.

Injectivity: two morphisms that agree agree on K̄-points, where they are toEnd of the base changes (DY.0/rational-map-base-change), which is injective since K̄ is infinite (DY.0/rational-map-action-on-points).
The K-point compatibility is the supplier's description of [F₀ : F₁] on points; iterate statements follow from DY.0/iterate-of-endomorphism-on-points with T = Spec K.

nodes.title: Conjugation of rational maps by PGL₂
nodes.statement: PGL(2, K) acts on RationalMap K by γ • f = γ ∘ f ∘ γ⁻¹ (the action of the unit group through unitsEquivPGL and Mathlib's ConjAct); two maps are conjugate iff they are IsConj in the monoid RationalMap K. Conjugation preserves degree, intertwines the actions on ℙ¹(K) (toEnd (γ • f) ∘ γ = γ ∘ toEnd f), and on lifts is γ ∘ F ∘ adj(γ), whose resultant is det(γ)^{d²+d} Res(F). Convention: Silverman's and Rumely's f^γ = γ⁻¹ ∘ f ∘ γ is γ⁻¹ • f.
hypotheses: K a field.
proofSteps: Define the action as the pullback along unitsEquivPGL.symm of Mathlib's MulDistribMulAction of ConjAct (RationalMap K)ˣ on the monoid (ConjAct.units_smul_def).
IsConj f g ↔ ∃ γ, γ • f = g by definition of IsConj (a unit c with c * f = g * c).
Degree: deg (γ f γ⁻¹) = 1·d·1; points: toEnd is a monoid homomorphism (DY.0/rational-map-action-on-points) and units act by PGL(2, K) (DY.0/units-of-rational-maps).
Lift formula: γ⁻¹ is the class of adj(γ); the resultant of the lift γ ∘ F ∘ adj(γ) is given by DY.0/resultant-conj (applied to adj γ, whose adjugate is γ).
Preperiodic points correspond under the bijection γ of ℙ¹(K) (DY.0/preperiodic-of-semiconj).
acceptance: Conjugating z² by z ↦ z + 1 gives z² − 2z + 2; by z ↦ 1/z it gives z² again.
z² and z² + 1 are not conjugate over ℚ (three versus one ℚ-rational fixed points).

nodes.title: The moduli space M_d(K) of degree-d maps
nodes.statement: For a field K and d ∈ ℕ, ModuliSpace K d is the set of conjugacy classes (Mathlib's ConjClasses of the monoid RationalMap K) of maps of degree d, i.e. Rat_d(K)/PGL₂(K). For K algebraically closed it is the set of K-points of Silverman's geometric quotient M_d = Rat_d/SL₂ (whose scheme structure is recorded as a gap); for non-closed K it separates twists. Base change K → L induces M_d(K) → M_d(L).
hypotheses: K a field; no algebraic closedness in the definition.
Scheme structure, affineness and dimension 2d − 2 of M_d are not part of this node (gap: geometric invariant theory).
proofSteps: Degree is a conjugacy invariant (DY.0/conjugacy-of-rational-maps), so it descends to ConjClasses (RationalMap K) (conjDegree); ModuliSpace K d is the fibre over d.
mk f = mk g iff IsConj f g (ConjClasses.mk_eq_mk_iff_isConj); every class has a representative.
Base change: IsConj is preserved by the monoid homomorphism map σ (DY.0/rational-map-base-change).
acceptance: M₀(K) is a point.
1/z² and 2/z² are different points of M₂(ℚ) with the same image in M₂(ℚ̄) (a conjugacy γ must preserve the critical points {0, ∞}, forcing γ(z) = cz or c/z with c³ = 2).

sources.excerpt: Two maps in Rat2 are said to be holomorphically conjugate if they belong to the same orbit. Definition: The quotient space of Rat2 under this action will be denoted by M2 , and called the moduli space of holomorphic conjugacy classes

sources.excerpt: For each degree d ≥2, the moduli space Md is the space of conformal conjugacy classes of maps f : P1 →P1 defined over C. It is an affine algebraic variety of dimension 2d−2. Silverman showed that it exists as a geometric quotient over Spec Z

nodes.title: The zeros of a binary form in ℙ¹, with multiplicity
nodes.statement: For a field K, n ∈ ℕ and a binary form G, binaryRoots n G ∈ Multiset ℙ¹(K) consists of [r : 1] for each root r of G(X, 1) (with multiplicity) and ∞ = [1 : 0] with multiplicity n − deg G(X, 1); for G = 0 it is empty. For G ≠ 0 homogeneous of degree n its underlying set is the zero set of G in ℙ¹(K), and it has n elements when K is algebraically closed.
hypotheses: K a field; n is the formal degree (the multiplicity of ∞ depends on it).
proofSteps: Define binaryRoots n G := ((G(X, 1)).roots.map (r ↦ [r : 1])) + (n − deg G(X, 1)) • {∞} (Polynomial.roots), and 0 for G = 0.
Membership: for x = (x₀, x₁) with x₁ ≠ 0, G(x) = x₁^n G(x₀/x₁, 1) (Polynomial.eval_homogenize); at ∞, G(1, 0) is the coefficient of X₀^n, zero iff deg G(X, 1) < n.
Cardinality n over an algebraically closed field: deg G(X, 1) roots (IsAlgClosed.card_roots_eq_natDegree) plus n − deg at ∞.
Multiplicativity under products (roots of a product, Polynomial.roots_mul) and invariance under scaling.
acceptance: X₁^n: n copies of ∞, although its dehomogenisation 1 has no roots.
X₀² + X₁² has no roots in ℙ¹(ℚ).

nodes.title: The fixed points of a rational map, with multiplicity
nodes.statement: For f = mk F of degree d, the fixed-point form is X₁F₀ − X₀F₁ (degree d + 1), and fixedPoints f := binaryRoots (d + 1) (X₁F₀ − X₀F₁). For d ≥ 2 the form is nonzero, P ∈ fixedPoints f iff toEnd f P = P, the multiset has d + 1 elements over an algebraically closed field, and conjugation transports it: fixedPoints (γ • f) = γ · fixedPoints f.
hypotheses: K a field; d ≥ 2 for the nonvanishing of the form (for the identity map the form is 0).
proofSteps: Well defined on the class: scaling F scales the form (DY.0/roots-of-a-binary-form, binaryRoots_smul).
Nonvanishing for d ≥ 2: if X₁F₀ = X₀F₁ then X₀ | F₀ and X₁ | F₁ with F₀ = X₀H, F₁ = X₁H, and H of degree d − 1 ≥ 1 is a common factor, contradicting Res ≠ 0 (DY.0/binary-resultant-eq-zero-iff).
Membership: [x] is fixed iff F(x) is proportional to x iff x₁F₀(x) − x₀F₁(x) = 0 (DY.0/roots-of-a-binary-form, mem_binaryRoots_iff).

Conjugation: the fixed-point form of γ ∘ F ∘ adj(γ) is the fixed-point form of F composed with adj(γ) (the 2 × 2 determinant det[y, γF(adj(γ)y)] with y = γx/det γ), whose roots are γ applied to those of F.
acceptance: z² has fixed points 0, 1, ∞; z + 1 has ∞ twice; over ℚ, z² + 1 has only ∞ (its finite fixed points solve z² − z + 1 = 0).

nodes.title: The multiplier of a rational map at a fixed point
nodes.statement: For f with lift F and a fixed point P: if P = [z : 1] then μ_P(f) = f'(z), the derivative at z of the rational function F₀(X, 1)/F₁(X, 1) (F₁(z, 1) ≠ 0 at a finite fixed point); if P = ∞ then μ_∞(f) = μ_0(ι • f) with ι(z) = 1/z. Coordinate-free (all characteristics): if F(x) = c·x with c ≠ 0 then μ_{[x]}(f) = (∂₀F₀(x) + ∂₁F₁(x))/c − d. The value at a non-fixed point is unspecified (junk).
hypotheses: K a field; P fixed by f for the value to be meaningful.
proofSteps: Finite fixed point: with f(z) = F₀(z,1)/F₁(z,1) and F₁(z, 1) ≠ 0 (since f(z) = z is finite), μ = (F₀'F₁ − F₀F₁')(z)/F₁(z, 1)² (Polynomial.derivative).
At ∞ use the unit ι = [z ↦ 1/z] of DY.0/units-of-rational-maps and the finite formula for ι • f at 0.

Trace formula: Euler's identity x₀∂₀F_i + x₁∂₁F_i = d F_i for forms of degree d (MvPolynomial.pderiv) gives, at a finite fixed point [z : 1] with F(z, 1) = c(z, 1), ∂₀F₀ − z∂₀F₁ = tr DF − dc, and f'(z) = (∂₀F₀ − z∂₀F₁)/c.
Polynomial maps: μ_{[z:1]} = p'(z); μ_∞ = 0 when deg p ≥ 2 (ι • p = 1/p(1/w) = w^n/(...) vanishes to order n at 0).
μ_P = 1 iff P is a multiple root of the fixed-point form: the derivative of F₀(z,1) − zF₁(z,1) at the fixed point is c(μ − 1).
acceptance: z²: μ₀ = 0, μ₁ = 2, μ_∞ = 0; z + 1: μ_∞ = 1 (parabolic); z^p over 𝔽_p: μ₁ = 0.

nodes.title: Milnor's relation σ₃ = σ₁ − 2
nodes.statement: Let K be algebraically closed of characteristic 0 and f a rational map of degree 2 over K. Then σ₃(f) = σ₁(f) − 2, i.e. μ₁μ₂μ₃ − (μ₁ + μ₂ + μ₃) + 2 = 0 for the multipliers at the three fixed points.
hypotheses: K algebraically closed, characteristic 0 (Milnor works over ℂ); deg f = 2.
proofSteps: By conjugation invariance (DY.0/multiplier-symmetric-functions) replace f by a normal form (DY.0/quadratic-fixed-point-normal-form).

Fixed point normal form z(z + b)/(cz + 1), bc ≠ 1: the fixed points are 0, ∞ and (1 − b)/(1 − c) with multipliers b, c and (2 − b − c)/(1 − bc) (DY.0/fixed-point-multiplier, direct computation); then bc(2 − b − c)/(1 − bc) − b − c − (2 − b − c)/(1 − bc) + 2 = 0 is a polynomial identity after clearing 1 − bc.
Normal form z + 1/z: the single fixed point ∞ has multiplicity 3 and multiplier 1 (multiplier_eq_one_iff), so σ₃ = 1 = σ₁ − 2.

sources.excerpt: and are subject only to the restriction that µ1µ2µ3 −(µ1 + µ2 + µ3) + 2 = 0 , (1) or in other words σ3 = σ1 −2 . (1′)
sources.match: Exactly the relation.

sources.excerpt: The third fixed point lies at (1 −µ1)/(1 −µ2) , and has multiplier µ3 = (2 −µ1 −µ2)/(1 −µ1µ2) .
sources.match: The computation used in place of Milnor's index-formula proof (which integrates dz/(z − f(z)) and is not algebraic).

nodes.title: Milnor's normal forms for quadratic maps
nodes.statement: Let K be algebraically closed of characteristic 0 and f of degree 2 over K. Either f has two distinct fixed points and is conjugate to z(z + μ₁)/(μ₂z + 1) with μ₁μ₂ ≠ 1, μ₁ and μ₂ the multipliers at 0 and ∞; or f has a single fixed point and is conjugate to z + 1/z. In the first case the normal form is determined by (μ₁, μ₂).
hypotheses: K algebraically closed of characteristic 0; deg f = 2.
proofSteps: Two distinct fixed points: move them to 0 and ∞ by a unit (DY.0/units-of-rational-maps, 2-transitivity of PGL₂ on ℙ¹, Mathlib's generalLinearGroup_is_two_pretransitive); then f(z) = z(az + b)/(cz + e) with a ≠ 0, e ≠ 0, ae − bc ≠ 0; scale the lift so that e = 1 and conjugate by z ↦ kz to make a = 1.
Read off μ₀ = b and μ_∞ = c from DY.0/fixed-point-multiplier; the condition Res ≠ 0 is 1 − bc ≠ 0.

One fixed point: move it to ∞ and its preimage other than ∞ to 0, so f = p(z)/z with f(z) − z = (p(z) − z²)/z having no finite zero, hence f = z + c/z with c ≠ 0; conjugating by z ↦ √c z (characteristic ≠ 2, K closed) gives z + 1/z.
acceptance: z² (fixed points 0, ∞, 1) is the normal form with μ₁ = μ₂ = 0.
z + 1/z has the triple fixed point ∞.

sources.excerpt: This yields the normal form f(z) = z (z + b)/(cz + 1) with 1 − bc ≠ 0, (3) where b = µ1 and c = µ2 are evidently equal to the multipliers at zero and infinity respectively.
sources.match: The first normal form.

sources.excerpt: If we normalize so that the critical points of f are ±1 , then c = 1 and f(z) = z + z−1 . (4)
sources.match: The second normal form.

nodes.title: Milnor: M₂ is the affine plane
nodes.statement: Let K be algebraically closed of characteristic 0. The map M₂(K) → K², ⟨f⟩ ↦ (σ₁(f), σ₂(f)), is a bijection.
hypotheses: K algebraically closed of characteristic 0 (Milnor: K = ℂ).
This is the statement on K-points; the isomorphism of schemes M₂ ≅ A²_ℤ (Silverman 1998) is part of the geometric-invariant-theory gap.
proofSteps: Well defined by DY.0/multiplier-symmetric-functions.

Injective: equal (σ₁, σ₂) give equal σ₃ (DY.0/quadratic-fixed-point-relation), hence equal multisets of multipliers {μ₁, μ₂, μ₃}. If all three are 1, both maps have a triple fixed point (multiplier_eq_one_iff) and are conjugate to z + 1/z; otherwise choose two fixed points whose multipliers satisfy μᵢμⱼ ≠ 1 (if μ₁μ₂ = 1 then (1) forces μ₁ = μ₂ = 1 and μ₃ ≠ 1), and both maps are conjugate to the same normal form z(z + μᵢ)/(μⱼz + 1) (DY.0/quadratic-fixed-point-normal-form).

Surjective: given (s₁, s₂), let μ₁, μ₂, μ₃ be the roots of t³ − s₁t² + s₂t − (s₁ − 2); if they are not all 1, some pair has μ₁μ₂ ≠ 1 and the normal form z(z + μ₁)/(μ₂z + 1) has third multiplier (2 − μ₁ − μ₂)/(1 − μ₁μ₂) = μ₃ by (1); if all are 1 take z + 1/z.
acceptance: Over ℚ the map is not injective: 1/z² and 2/z² have the same multipliers (twists).

sources.excerpt: Hence the moduli space M2 is canonically isomorphic to C2 , with coordinates σ1 and σ2 .
sources.match: Exactly the theorem over ℂ; the proof transfers to any algebraically closed field of characteristic 0.

sources.excerpt: We note that M2 ≃C2 [Mi1] while Md is singular in all degrees d > 2 [We, MSW].
sources.match: The use of the theorem in the paper routed to this layer.

nodes.title: The critical points of a rational map, with multiplicity
nodes.statement: For f = mk F of degree d, the Jacobian form Jac(F) = ∂₀F₀·∂₁F₁ − ∂₁F₀·∂₀F₁ is a binary form of degree 2d − 2, and criticalPoints f := binaryRoots (2d − 2) (Jac F). At a finite point [z : 1] with F₁(z, 1) ≠ 0 this is the vanishing of f'(z). In characteristic 0 and d ≥ 1 there are 2d − 2 critical points with multiplicity over an algebraically closed field (Riemann–Hurwitz), each of multiplicity at most d − 1; conjugation transports them.
hypotheses: K a field; in characteristic p the Jacobian form may vanish identically (inseparable maps), and the counting statements assume characteristic 0.
proofSteps: Jac(cF) = c² Jac(F), so the roots depend only on f (DY.0/roots-of-a-binary-form, binaryRoots_smul); Jac(F) is homogeneous of degree 2(d − 1) (MvPolynomial.pderiv lowers degree by 1).

Affine characterisation: with f_i = F_i(X, 1), Euler's identity z∂₀F_i + ∂₁F_i = d F_i at (z, 1) gives Jac(F)(z, 1) = d·(f₀'f₁ − f₀f₁')(z); in characteristic 0, for F₁(z, 1) ≠ 0 the point is critical iff the derivative of f₀/f₁ vanishes at z.

Nonvanishing and count in characteristic 0: f₁ ≠ 0 (otherwise F₁ = 0 and Res = 0), and d·f₁²·(f₀/f₁)' ≠ 0 because a map of degree d ≥ 1 is not constant; so Jac(F) ≠ 0 and it has 2d − 2 roots (card_binaryRoots).
Conjugation: Jac(γ ∘ F ∘ adj γ) = det(γ)^2 · (Jac F) ∘ adj(γ) by the chain rule, so criticalPoints (γ • f) = γ · criticalPoints f; chain rule for composites gives the critical points of f ∘ g.
acceptance: z³ over ℚ: 0 and ∞, each twice.
z^p over 𝔽_p: Jac = 0 and the definition returns no critical points.
Milnor's normal form z(z + μ₁)/(μ₂z + 1): Jac = 2(μ₂X₀² + 2X₀X₁ + μ₁X₁²).

sources.excerpt: We say that α is a critical point if ϕ′(α) = 0, in which case ϕ(α) is a critical value.
sources.match: The affine definition, which the Jacobian form extends to ∞.

sources.excerpt: Theorem 5 (Riemann–Hurwitz formula). Let ϕ(z) ∈ C(z) be a rational function of degree d ≥ 1. Then 2d − 2 = Σ_{α∈P1(C)} (eα(ϕ) − 1).
sources.match: The count 2d − 2 with multiplicity e_α − 1.

nodes.title: Critically marked maps and their moduli M_d^cm(K)
nodes.statement: A critically marked map of degree d is (f, c) with deg f = d and c : Fin (2d − 2) → ℙ¹(K) listing criticalPoints f with multiplicity; PGL(2, K) acts on (f, c) by γ • (f, c) = (γ • f, γ ∘ c), and CriticallyMarkedModuliSpace K d is the orbit quotient. The forgetful map to M_d(K) is surjective over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, and its fibres are the orbits of the relabelling action of Sym(2d − 2).
hypotheses: K a field; the finite branched cover M_d^cm → M_d of DeMarco–Mavraki–Ye carrying a universal family is scheme-level and belongs to the geometric-invariant-theory gap.
proofSteps: Define CriticallyMarkedMap K d as the subtype and the action through DY.0/conjugacy-of-rational-maps and DY.0/critical-points-of-a-rational-map (criticalPoints_smul keeps the marking valid).
Quotient by MulAction.orbitRel; forget (f, c) = mk f is well defined.
Surjectivity: over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 the multiset has 2d − 2 elements (card_criticalPoints), so it can be listed.
Fibres: two markings of the same f differ by a permutation; conjugacies of the map act compatibly.
acceptance: d = 1: no critical points and M₁^cm = M₁.
d = 2: z² has one preimage (z ↦ 1/z swaps its critical points 0, ∞ and commutes with z²); a map with trivial automorphism group has two.

sources.excerpt: Recall from §2 that a critically marked quadratic rational map (f , ω1 , ω2) is a map f ∈Rat2 together with an ordered list of its critical points.

nodes.title: Milnor: M₂^cm is the surface A³(A − 1) = BC
nodes.statement: Let K be algebraically closed of characteristic 0. There is a bijection M₂^cm(K) ≅ {(A, B, C) ∈ K³ : A³(A − 1) = BC}, given on the critical point normal form (αz² + β)/(γz² + δ) with αδ − βγ = 1 (critical points marked 0, ∞) by A = αδ, B = α³β, C = γδ³; the relabelling (ω₁, ω₂) ↦ (ω₂, ω₁) corresponds to (A, B, C) ↦ (A, C, B).
hypotheses: K algebraically closed of characteristic 0 (two distinct critical points need characteristic ≠ 2).
proofSteps: A quadratic map has two distinct critical points (card_criticalPoints and count_criticalPoints_le of DY.0/critical-points-of-a-rational-map); conjugate the marked pair to (0, ∞) (DY.0/units-of-rational-maps), giving the normal form f(z) = (αz² + β)/(γz² + δ) with αδ − βγ = 1 after scaling.
The normal form is unique up to z ↦ λ²-rescaling, acting by (α, β, γ, δ) ↦ (αλ, β/λ³, γλ³, δ/λ); A, B, C are invariant and satisfy A³(A − 1) = BC (since A − 1 = βγ).

Conversely (A, B, C) on the surface determines (α, β, γ, δ) up to this action: if B ≠ 0 or A ≠ 0 take α = 1, β = B, δ = A and γ = (A − 1)/B or C/A³; the case C ≠ 0 is symmetric; A = B = C = 0 is 1/z².
The conjugacy z ↦ 1/f(1/z) exchanges the marked critical points and (B, C).
acceptance: The point (0, 0, 0) is the class of z ↦ 1/z² (its two markings are equivalent).
z² (marked (0, ∞)) has A = 1, B = C = 0.

sources.excerpt: Lemma 6.1. The moduli space M^cm_2 for critically marked quadratic rational maps can be identified with the hypersurface W consisting of all triples (A, B, C) ∈ C³ which satisfy the equation A³(A − 1) = BC. (14)
sources.match: Exactly the theorem over ℂ.

sources.excerpt: The deck transformation (f, ω1, ω2) ↔ (f, ω2, ω1) of M^cm_2 over M2, which interchanges the two critical points, corresponds to the map (A, B, C) ↔ (A, C, B).

nodes.title: Good reduction of a rational map
nodes.statement: Let R be a valuation ring with fraction field K and residue field k. A rational map f over K has good reduction (over R) if it has a lift (F₀, F₁) with coefficients in R whose resultant Res_{d,d}(F₀, F₁) is a unit of R. Its reduction f̃ is then the class over k of the reduced lift (F̃₀, F̃₁), a rational map of the same degree d.
hypotheses: R a valuation ring (e.g. ℤ_(p), ℤ_p, the valuation ring of a complete nonarchimedean field), K = Frac R, k = R/𝔪.
proofSteps: Define HasGoodReduction R f := ∃ F integral homogeneous of degree deg f, IsUnit (Res_{d,d}(F₀, F₁)), with map (algebraMap R K) F a lift of f.

reduction: map the integral lift along IsLocalRing.residue; the reduced resultant is the residue of Res (Polynomial.resultant_map_map), nonzero because Res is a unit (IsLocalRing.residue_ne_zero_iff_isUnit), so it is a lift of degree d over k; independence of the chosen lift is DY.0/good-reduction-iff-normalized-resultant-unit (two integral lifts with unit resultant differ by a unit of R).
Polynomial maps: the lift (homogenize p n, X₁^n) has resultant lead(p)^n, a unit iff lead(p) is.
Degree-one maps from GL₂(R): resultant det γ ∈ R^×.
acceptance: (z² + 2)/z over ℚ has resultant 2 on its normalised lift (X₀² + 2X₁², X₀X₁): bad reduction at 2 (the reduction (X₀², X₀X₁) has the common zero [0 : 1] and degree drops), good at every odd p.
z² + c, c ∈ ℤ: good reduction everywhere.
z²/2 is conjugate over ℚ to z² (good reduction) but has bad reduction at 2.

sources.excerpt: We say that ϕ(z) has good reduction at p if deg(ϕ̃) = deg(ϕ), or equivalently, if F̃(z) and G̃(z) have no common factors in Fp[z].
sources.match: The definition for ℤ_(p); the unit-resultant form is DY.0/good-reduction-iff-normalized-resultant-unit.

sources.excerpt: This gives the alternative definition ϕ has good reduction at p ⇐⇒ p ∤Res(F, G).
sources.match: The form adopted as the definition.

sources.excerpt: The reduction ϕ̃ is the map [X̃ : Ỹ] ↦ [F̃(X̃, Ỹ) : G̃(X̃, Ỹ)] on P1(k̃) obtained by reducing F and G (mod M) and eliminating common factors. If ϕ̃ has degree d, then ϕ is said to have good reduction.
sources.match: The definition over a nonarchimedean valuation ring.

nodes.title: Good reduction is read off a normalised lift
nodes.statement: Let R be a valuation ring with fraction field K and f a rational map of degree d over K. For any integral lift F of f that is normalised (some coefficient is a unit of R): f has good reduction iff Res_{d,d}(F₀, F₁) ∈ R^× iff the reduced forms F̃₀, F̃₁ over k have nonzero resultant (the reduction still has degree d).
hypotheses: R a valuation ring, K = Frac R; F integral and normalised.
proofSteps: Normalised lifts exist and are unique up to R^×: scale any lift by the inverse of a coefficient of minimal valuation (valuation ring property); two normalised lifts differ by c ∈ K^× with c and c^{-1} integral.
Any integral lift is c·F with c ∈ R, whose resultant is c^{2d}·Res(F) (DY.0/resultant-of-a-rational-map, binaryResultant_smul_smul): a unit iff c is a unit and Res(F) is a unit.
IsUnit x ↔ residue x ≠ 0 in a local ring (IsLocalRing.residue_ne_zero_iff_isUnit), and the residue of Res(F) is the resultant of the reduced forms (Polynomial.resultant_map_map).
For d ≥ 1, the reduced resultant is nonzero iff the reduced forms have no common zero over k̄ (DY.0/binary-resultant-eq-zero-iff), i.e. no common factor, i.e. the reduced map has degree d.
acceptance: (X₀² + 2X₁², X₀X₁) is normalised with resultant 2: good reduction at p iff p ≠ 2.
The non-normalised lift (2X₀² + 4X₁², 2X₀X₁) has resultant 32 at every p, which is why normalisation is required.

nodes.title: Reduction of points of ℙ¹ modulo the maximal ideal
nodes.statement: For a valuation ring R with fraction field K and residue field k, projReduction R : ℙ¹(K) → ℙ¹(k) sends [x] to [x̃], where x is scaled to have coordinates in R with at least one unit coordinate and x̃ is its coordinatewise residue. It is surjective and sends ∞ to ∞.
hypotheses: R a valuation ring, K = Frac R.
proofSteps: Every x ≠ 0 in K² can be scaled into R² with a unit coordinate (valuation ring: divide by a coordinate of minimal valuation); two such scalings differ by a unit of R, so [x̃] is well defined (Projectivization.lift).
x̃ ≠ 0 because a unit coordinate has nonzero residue (IsLocalRing.residue_ne_zero_iff_isUnit).
Surjectivity: lift a representative with a nonzero coordinate from k to R (IsLocalRing.residue is surjective).

nodes.title: Reduction commutes with composition and iteration
nodes.statement: Let R be a valuation ring with fraction field K. If f and g have good reduction then so does f g, and (f g)~ = f̃ g̃; in particular f^n has good reduction and (f^n)~ = (f̃)^n.
hypotheses: R a valuation ring; f, g with good reduction.
proofSteps: Take integral lifts F, G with unit resultants. F ∘ G has integral coefficients and reduces to F̃ ∘ G̃ (reduction is a ring homomorphism, compatible with MvPolynomial.aeval).

F̃ and G̃ have nonzero resultant over k, so F̃ ∘ G̃ is a lift over k (DY.0/homogeneous-lift-comp), i.e. its resultant — the residue of Res(F ∘ G) — is nonzero; hence Res(F ∘ G) is a unit (IsLocalRing.residue_ne_zero_iff_isUnit) and f g has good reduction with reduction mk(F̃ ∘ G̃) = f̃ g̃.
Powers by induction.

nodes.title: Reduction commutes with evaluation
nodes.statement: Let R be a valuation ring with fraction field K and f a rational map with good reduction. For every P ∈ ℙ¹(K): projReduction (f(P)) = f̃(projReduction P).
hypotheses: R a valuation ring; f with good reduction.
proofSteps: Take an integral lift F with unit resultant and a representative x ∈ R² of P with a unit coordinate.

F(x) ∈ R² reduces to F̃(x̃), which is nonzero because x̃ ≠ 0 and F̃ is a lift over k (DY.0/homogeneous-lift, eval_ne_zero); so F(x) has a unit coordinate and projReduction [F(x)] = [F̃(x̃)] (DY.0/reduction-of-points).

nodes.title: Conjugation by GL₂(R) preserves good reduction
nodes.statement: Let R be a valuation ring with fraction field K and γ ∈ GL₂(R). Then γ • f has good reduction iff f does.
hypotheses: γ with entries in R and det γ ∈ R^×.
proofSteps: If F is an integral lift with unit resultant, γ ∘ F ∘ adj(γ) is integral and is a lift of γ • f (DY.0/conjugacy-of-rational-maps, smul_mk), with resultant det(γ)^{d²+d} Res(F) (DY.0/resultant-conj), a unit.
The converse applies the same to γ⁻¹ ∈ GL₂(R).

nodes.title: Tate's limit of a height along a self-map
nodes.statement: For a set S, a self-map φ : S → S, a function h : S → ℝ and α ∈ ℝ, tateLimit φ h α P := lim_{n→∞} h(φⁿ(P))/αⁿ, defined as Mathlib's limUnder along atTop. When α > 1 and h ∘ φ − αh is bounded the limit exists (DY.1/tate-limit-tendsto); the value then depends on h only up to bounded functions, is linear in h, and is unchanged when (φ, α) is replaced by (φ^k, α^k).
hypotheses: S any type; α real; the junk value of limUnder is never used by the theorems, which all assume α > 1 and the bound |h(φQ) − αh(Q)| ≤ C for all Q ∈ S (Call–Silverman (3)).
proofSteps: Define tateLimit as Filter.limUnder atTop (n ↦ h(φ^[n] P)/α^n).

tateLimit_congr_of_bounded: if h' − h is bounded by B, then h' satisfies the hypothesis with constant C + (α + 1)B and tateLimit φ h' α satisfies (i) and (ii) of DY.1/tate-limit-unique for h, hence equals tateLimit φ h α.

tateLimit_const_mul and tateLimit_iterate: the sequences for c·h and for (φ^k, α^k) are c times, respectively a subsequence of, the sequence for (φ, h, α) (Filter.Tendsto.const_mul, Filter.Tendsto.comp).
tateLimit_nonneg: a limit of nonnegative terms (le_of_tendsto).
acceptance: φ = id, α = 2: the limit is 0 for every h.
φ(x) = 2x, h = id on ℝ, α = 2: the sequence is constant and the limit is x.
α = 1, φ(x) = x + 1, h = id: the sequence x + n diverges, so α > 1 is essential.

nodes.title: Tate's telescoping estimate
nodes.statement: Let α > 1 and C ≥ 0 with |h(φQ) − αh(Q)| ≤ C for all Q ∈ S (Call–Silverman (3)). Then for every P ∈ S and m ≤ n: |h(φⁿP)/αⁿ − h(φᵐP)/αᵐ| ≤ C/((α − 1)αᵐ).

proofSteps: Telescoping: h(φⁿP)/αⁿ − h(φᵐP)/αᵐ = Σ_{i=m+1}^{n} α^{−i}(h(φQ_i) − αh(Q_i)) with Q_i = φ^{i−1}P (Function.iterate_succ_apply').

nodes.title: Uniqueness of Tate's limit
nodes.statement: Let α > 1 and suppose h ∘ φ − αh is bounded. If g : S → ℝ satisfies (i) g − h is bounded and (ii) g ∘ φ = αg, then g = tateLimit φ h α. Hence tateLimit φ h α is the unique function with (i) and (ii).
hypotheses: ∃ C, |h(φQ) − αh(Q)| ≤ C for all Q ∈ S (Call–Silverman (3)).
proofSteps: tateLimit φ h α satisfies (i) (DY.1/tate-limit-error-bound) and (ii) (DY.1/tate-limit-functional-equation).
The difference δ = g − tateLimit φ h α is bounded, say by B, and δ(φP) = αδ(P); so αⁿ|δ(P)| = |δ(φⁿP)| ≤ B for all n, forcing δ(P) = 0 since αⁿ → ∞.

nodes.title: Tate's limit is transported along semiconjugacies
nodes.statement: Let π : S → T with π ∘ φ = ψ ∘ π (Function.Semiconj π φ ψ), α > 1, h : S → ℝ and k : T → ℝ with h ∘ φ − αh and k ∘ ψ − αk bounded, and k ∘ π − h bounded. Then tateLimit ψ k α ∘ π = tateLimit φ h α.
hypotheses: α > 1; the three boundedness hypotheses.
proofSteps: g := tateLimit ψ k α ∘ π satisfies g ∘ φ = (tateLimit ψ k α) ∘ ψ ∘ π = αg (DY.1/tate-limit-functional-equation for ψ, k).
g − h = (tateLimit ψ k α − k) ∘ π + (k ∘ π − h) is bounded (DY.1/tate-limit-error-bound).
Conclude by DY.1/tate-limit-unique.

Iterates: π = id, (φ, α) replaced by (φ^k, α^k) is the API item tateLimit_iterate.

nodes.title: Zero Tate limit and Northcott give preperiodicity
nodes.statement: Let α > 1 with h ∘ φ − αh bounded, and let A ⊆ S be forward invariant (φ(A) ⊆ A) such that {Q ∈ A : h(Q) ≤ B} is finite for every B (Northcott on A). If P ∈ A and tateLimit φ h α P = 0, then P is preperiodic for φ.
hypotheses: α > 1; ∃ C, |h(φQ) − αh(Q)| ≤ C for all Q ∈ S (Call–Silverman (3)).
Northcott for h on the forward-invariant set A.

nodes.title: The absolute logarithmic Weil height on ℙ¹
nodes.statement: For a field F of characteristic 0, projLineAbsLogHeight : ℙ¹(F) → ℝ is h([x₀ : x₁]) = absLogHeight₁(x₀/x₁) if x₁ ≠ 0 and h([1 : 0]) = 0, where absLogHeight₁ is Mathlib's absolute logarithmic Weil height of a field element (junk value 0 at transcendental elements). It is nonnegative, invariant under x ↦ 1/x and under field embeddings, and on a number field K equals Mathlib's relative Projectivization.logHeight divided by [K : ℚ].
hypotheses: F of characteristic 0; the values are meaningful at points with algebraic coordinates (F algebraic over ℚ in every theorem that uses them).
proofSteps: Well defined on ℙ¹: scaling (x₀, x₁) by t ≠ 0 does not change x₀/x₁ or the vanishing of x₁ (Projectivization.lift).
Nonnegativity: absLogHeight₁ = log absMulHeight₁ with absMulHeight₁ ≥ 1 (a power of Mathlib's mulHeight₁ ≥ 1, or the junk 1).

Inversion: absLogHeight₁(1/x) = absLogHeight₁(x) (Height.logHeight₁ of an inverse is unchanged, Mathlib's logHeight₁_inv, transported by DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0/abs-mul-height-eq-rpow).
Embeddings: DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0/abs-mul-height-eq-of-minpoly-eq (conjugate elements have equal absolute height).

nodes.title: Mathlib's height-bound constant under finite extension
nodes.statement: Let K ⊆ L be number fields and p : ι' → MvPolynomial ι K a finite family. Then Height.mulHeightBound (map (algebraMap K L) ∘ p) = Height.mulHeightBound p ^ [L : K]. Consequently the normalised constants log max(mulHeightBound p, 1)/[K : ℚ] do not depend on the number field in which they are computed.
hypotheses: K ⊆ L number fields (an algebra K → L), heights relative to NumberField.instAdmissibleAbsValues.
proofSteps: mulHeightBound is the product over archimedean places (with multiplicity) of max_j Σ_s |coeff_s p_j|_v and over finite places of max_j max(max_s |coeff_s p_j|_v, 1); mapping the coefficients to L does not change the supports (MvPolynomial.support_map_of_injective, MvPolynomial.coeff_map).

Archimedean part: for w | v, w(σc) = v(c) (NumberField.InfinitePlace.comap_apply); regroup by DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.0/infinite-places-over (Σ_{w|v} mult w = mult v·[L:K]); rewrite the multiset products by NumberField.prod_archAbsVal_eq.

Finite part: for P | p, |σc|_P = |c|_p^{e(P|p) f(P|p)} (NumberField.FinitePlace.equivHeightOneSpectrum_symm_apply_algebraMap), maxima commute with the power, and Σ_{P|p} e f = [L : K] (Ideal.sum_ramification_inertia_eq_finrank).

nodes.title: Call–Silverman canonical height of a polarized morphism
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, V/K a smooth projective variety, φ : V → V a morphism and L an ample line bundle on V with φ*L ≅ L^{⊗d} for an integer d ≥ 2, and let h_L : V(K̄) → ℝ be a Weil height for L. Then ĥ_{V,φ,L}(P) = lim d^{−n} h_L(φⁿP) exists for every P ∈ V(K̄), |ĥ_{V,φ,L} − h_L| ≤ c/(d − 1) where c bounds |h_L ∘ φ − d h_L|, ĥ_{V,φ,L} ∘ φ = d·ĥ_{V,φ,L}, ĥ_{V,φ,L} is the unique function with ĥ − h_L bounded and ĥ ∘ φ = dĥ, and it does not depend on the choice of the Weil height h_L.
hypotheses: K a number field; V smooth projective over K; φ a morphism over K; L ample with φ*L ≅ L^{⊗d}, d ≥ 2.
The Weil height machine for line bundles on V (functoriality, additivity, dependence on the isomorphism class) is supplied by HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions:RP.0 (request).

Uniqueness: DY.1/tate-limit-unique.

nodes.statement: Let F be a field with Height.AdmissibleAbsValues, W an elliptic curve over F and h the naive height of the x-coordinate (Tau Ceti's WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.naiveHeight). Then tateLimit (Q ↦ 2•Q) h 4 = 2·canonicalHeight (Tau Ceti's Point.canonicalHeight), and for every integer m ≥ 2, tateLimit (Q ↦ m•Q) h m² = 2·canonicalHeight. Normalisation: Call–Silverman's ĥ_{E,[m],η} for η the class of 2(O), with h_{2(O)} = h, is twice Tau Ceti's canonical height, which is the Néron–Tate height for (O); points of Tate limit 0 are exactly the torsion points under Northcott for the field height.
hypotheses: F with admissible absolute values and decidable equality (Tau Ceti's group law); W elliptic.
proofSteps: (2 • ·)^[n] P = 2^n • P (smul_iterate); Tau Ceti's Point.tendsto_naiveHeight_two_pow_nsmul_div_four_pow says h(2^nP)/(2·4^n) → canonicalHeight P, so h(2^nP)/4^n → 2·canonicalHeight P (Filter.Tendsto.const_mul) and tateLimit returns this limit (Filter.Tendsto.limUnder_eq).

General m: g = 2·canonicalHeight satisfies g(mP) = m²g(P) (Point.canonicalHeight_nsmul) and |g − h| ≤ 2D (Point.abs_canonicalHeight_sub_naiveHeight_le), hence also |h(mP) − m²h(P)| ≤ 2D(1 + m²); DY.1/tate-limit-unique gives g = tateLimit (m • ·) h m².
Zero set: Point.canonicalHeight_eq_zero_iff_isOfFinAddOrder (Northcott transferred from the field height by Tau Ceti's instance).
acceptance: The point at infinity has Tate limit 0; a point of order 3 has Tate limit 0 for every m.

sources.excerpt: Example 1. Let A be an abelian variety, let [n]: A → A be the multiplication-by-n map for some n ≥ 2, and let η ∈ Pic(A) be a symmetric divisor. (That is, [−1]*η = η.) As is well-known, one then has the relation [n]*η = n²η
sources.match: The acceptance example (multiplication on an abelian variety), made concrete for elliptic curves.

nodes.title: Multiplication on an abelian variety: the Néron–Tate height
nodes.statement: Let A be an abelian variety over a number field K and L a symmetric line bundle on A. For every integer m ≥ 2, [m]*L ≅ L^{⊗m²} and the canonical height ĥ_{A,[m],L} of DY.1/canonical-height (or DY.1/canonical-height-for-a-divisorial-eigenclass when L is not ample) is independent of m and equals the Néron–Tate height ĥ_{A,L} of HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions:RP.0.
hypotheses: A an abelian variety over a number field; L symmetric; [m]*L ≅ L^{⊗m²} and the Néron–Tate height with ĥ_{A,L}(mP) = m²ĥ_{A,L}(P) and ĥ_{A,L} − h_L bounded are supplied by RP.0 (request).
proofSteps: ĥ_{A,L} has bounded difference from h_L and satisfies ĥ_{A,L} ∘ [m] = m²ĥ_{A,L} (RP.0); by the uniqueness in DY.1/canonical-height (DY.1/tate-limit-unique) it is ĥ_{A,[m],L} for every m ≥ 2.
acceptance: dim A = 1: DY.1/tate-limit-of-elliptic-doubling with L = O(2(O)).

sources.excerpt: so one obtains a canonical height ĥ_η = ĥ_{A,η,[n]} satisfying ĥ_η(nP) = n²ĥ_η(P). This is the classical canonical height constructed by Néron and Tate.
sources.match: Exactly the comparison.

nodes.title: Upper bound ‖F(x)‖_v ≤ C_v ‖x‖_v^d for a lift
nodes.statement: Let F = (F₀, F₁) be a pair of binary forms of degree d over a field K and v an absolute value on K. Put C_v(F) = max_i Σ_m v(coeff_m F_i) (sum over the monomials of F_i) and, when v is nonarchimedean, C_v(F) = max_{i,m} v(coeff_m F_i). Then ‖F(x)‖_v ≤ C_v(F)·‖x‖_v^d for every x ∈ K². In particular, if v is nonarchimedean and every coefficient of F lies in the valuation ring (v ≤ 1 on the coefficients), then ‖F(x)‖_v ≤ ‖x‖_v^d.
hypotheses: F₀, F₁ homogeneous of the same degree d
v an absolute value on K (archimedean or not)
proofSteps: Apply Mathlib's AbsoluteValue.eval_mvPolynomial_le (archimedean form: v(p(x)) ≤ (Σ_m v(coeff_m p))·(⨆ i, v(x i))^N for p homogeneous of degree N) to F₀ and F₁ and take the maximum.
For v nonarchimedean use IsNonarchimedean.eval_mvPolynomial_le instead, which gives the constant ⨆_m v(coeff_m p).
If all coefficients are v-integral the nonarchimedean constant is ≤ 1.
acceptance: For F = (X₀², X₁²) the bound holds with C_v = 1 and is an equality.
For F = (X₀² − X₁², X₁²) at the archimedean place of ℚ, C_∞ = 2 and x = (1, 1) gives ‖F(x)‖ = 1 ≤ 2.

sources.locator: Lemma 3.1 and its proof, pp. 6–7 (arXiv v2)
sources.excerpt: For each place v of k, there are constants 0 < Cv ≤ Dv such that for all z ∈ C2v, Cv(∥z∥v)d ≤ ∥F(z)∥v ≤ Dv(∥z∥v)d .
sources.match: The right-hand inequality; BR prove it 'trivially by the ultrametric inequality' and by compactness at archimedean places, the node gives the explicit coefficient constant valid over any field.

sources.excerpt: If v is nonarchimedean and F1, F2 have v-integral coeﬃcients, then we may choose g1(x, y), g2(x, y), and h1(x, y), h2(x, y) to have v-integral coeﬃcients as well. In this case we can take Cv = |Res(F)|v and Dv = 1.
sources.match: The integral case Dv = 1.

nodes.title: Lower bound c_v ‖x‖_v^d ≤ ‖F(x)‖_v from the resultant
nodes.statement: Let F = (F₀, F₁) be binary forms of degree d ≥ 1 over K with Res(F) ≠ 0, and v an absolute value on K. There is a constant c_v(F) > 0 with c_v(F)·‖x‖_v^d ≤ ‖F(x)‖_v for all x ∈ K². Explicitly, take the forms G_{kj} of degree d − 1 of DY.0/resultant-certificate, with Σ_j G_{kj}F_j = Res(F)·X_k^{2d−1}; then one may take c_v(F) = v(Res(F)) / (2·C_v(G)) (archimedean v) and c_v(F) = v(Res(F)) / C_v(G) (nonarchimedean v), where C_v(G) is the constant of DY.2/lift-norm-upper-bound for the four forms G_{kj}. If v is nonarchimedean and F has v-integral coefficients, the forms G_{kj} can be taken v-integral and c_v(F) = v(Res(F)): v(Res F)·‖x‖_v^d ≤ ‖F(x)‖_v ≤ ‖x‖_v^d.
hypotheses: F₀, F₁ homogeneous of degree d ≥ 1
Res(F) ≠ 0 (F lifts a rational map of degree d)
proofSteps: Certificate (DY.0/resultant-certificate): there are binary forms G_{kj} of degree d − 1, with coefficients in any commutative ring containing those of F (the valuation ring when F is v-integral), such that Σ_j G_{kj}·F_j = Res(F)·X_k^{2d−1} for k = 0, 1.

Evaluate at x: v(Res F)·v(x_k)^{2d−1} = v(Σ_j G_{kj}(x)F_j(x)) ≤ 2·max_j v(G_{kj}(x))·‖F(x)‖_v (archimedean; no factor 2 in the nonarchimedean case) ≤ 2·C_v(G)·‖x‖_v^{d−1}·‖F(x)‖_v by DY.2/lift-norm-upper-bound.
Take the maximum over k = 0, 1 and divide by ‖x‖_v^{d−1} (x ≠ 0; the case x = 0 is trivial).
acceptance: For F = (X₀² + X₁², 3X₀X₁) over ℚ₃ (Res(F) = 9): 3⁻²·‖x‖₃² ≤ ‖F(x)‖₃ for all x ∈ ℚ₃², and over ℂ₃ the point x = (i, 1) has ‖F(x)‖₃ = 1/3 < 1 = ‖x‖₃², so the lower constant cannot be taken to be 1 although F is 3-integral.
For a lift with good reduction (v-integral coefficients, v(Res F) = 1) the two bounds coincide: ‖F(x)‖_v = ‖x‖_v^d.

sources.excerpt: there exist polynomials g1(x, y), g2(x, y), and h1(x, y), h2(x, y), which are homogeneous of degree d −1 in x and y and whose coeﬃcients lie in k, such that g1(x, y)F1(x, y) + g2(x, y)F2(x, y) = Res(F)x2d−1 ,
sources.match: The resultant certificate and the ultrametric estimate C′_v|x|^{2d−1} ≤ C″_v max(|F1|, |F2|); at archimedean places BR use compactness of the unit sphere of ℂ², the node uses the certificate at every place so that no completeness is needed.

sources.excerpt: In this case we can take Cv = |Res(F)|v and Dv = 1.
sources.match: The v-integral constant c_v = v(Res F).

nodes.title: ‖F(x)‖_v = ‖x‖_v^d for a lift with good reduction
nodes.statement: Let v be a nonarchimedean absolute value on K and F a lift of degree d whose coefficients lie in the valuation ring and with v(Res F) = 1 (a normalised lift of a map with good reduction at v, DY.0/good-reduction-of-a-rational-map). Then ‖F(x)‖_v = ‖x‖_v^d for all x ∈ K²; in particular F maps primitive vectors (‖x‖_v = 1) to primitive vectors, and ‖Fⁿ(x)‖_v = ‖x‖_v^{dⁿ} for all n.
hypotheses: v nonarchimedean
F v-integral with v(Res F) = 1
proofSteps: Upper bound ‖F(x)‖ ≤ ‖x‖^d from DY.2/lift-norm-upper-bound (integral case).
Lower bound v(Res F)·‖x‖^d ≤ ‖F(x)‖ from DY.2/lift-norm-lower-bound (integral case) with v(Res F) = 1.
Iterate by induction on n.
acceptance: For f(z) = z² − z − 1, F = (X₀² − X₀X₁ − X₁², X₁²) has Res(F) = 1 and ‖F(x)‖_p = ‖x‖_p² at every prime p.
Non-example: F = (X₀^p − X₀X₁^{p−1}, pX₁^p) over ℚ_p (Res = p^p) has ‖F(0, 1)‖_p = 1/p < 1.

sources.excerpt: By Remark 3.3, it follows that ∥F(z)∥v = ∥z∥d v, and therefore ∥F (n)(z)∥v = ∥z∥dn v for all n ≥1.
sources.match: Exactly the statement, for F with 𝒪-coefficients and |Res(F)|_v = 1.

nodes.title: The homogeneous escape rate G_{F,v}
nodes.statement: Conventions (pinned for the whole layer): K is a field and v : K → ℝ an absolute value (Mathlib's AbsoluteValue K ℝ); for x = (x₀, x₁) ∈ K², ‖x‖_v = max(v(x₀), v(x₁)) (Mathlib's ⨆ i, v (x i)). A lift of a rational map f of degree d is a pair F = (F₀, F₁) of binary forms of degree d with Res(F) ≠ 0 (DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line, DY.0/resultant-of-a-rational-map); f([x₀ : x₁]) = [F₀(x) : F₁(x)], the affine coordinate is z ↔ [z : 1], ∞ = [1 : 0], and Fⁿ is the n-fold composite, a lift of fⁿ of degree dⁿ. The (homogeneous) escape rate of F at v is G_{F,v}(x) = lim_{n→∞} d^{−n}·log ‖Fⁿ(x)‖_v for x ∈ K² ∖ {0} (d ≥ 2); by DY.2/escape-rate-tendsto the limit exists. It is defined at every absolute value, archimedean or not, without completeness of K; for a place v of a number field K it is taken with the absolute value v itself (Mathlib's InfinitePlace, resp. normalised FinitePlace).
hypotheses: Res(F) ≠ 0
x ≠ 0 (the formula is extended by the junk value of limUnder at x = 0)
proofSteps: Define G_{F,v}(x) as the limit (limUnder along atTop) of the real sequence d^{−n}·log ‖Fⁿ(x)‖_v.
Existence of the limit, the uniform rate and every transformation rule are separate nodes (DY.2/escape-rate-tendsto and following).
acceptance: G_{F,v} = log ‖·‖_v for F = (X₀^d, X₁^d) at every v.
For the (z^p − z)/p lift at p, G(0, 1) = −(log p)/(p − 1).

sources.locator: (2.3), §2.2, p. 7 (arXiv v2; the norm is misprinted, see ArithmeticDynamics/E301)
sources.excerpt: As observed in [BR, Chapter 10], its escape-rate function (2.3) GFt,v(z, w) := lim n→∞ 1/4n log ∥F n t (z, w)∥v,
sources.match: The escape rate of the Lattès lift F_t; the node is the same construction for an arbitrary lift F of degree d.

sources.excerpt: For v ∈ Mk and z = (z0, z1) ∈ C2v\{0}, define the homogeneous local dynamical height ĤF,v : C2v\{0} → R by ĤF,v(z) := lim n→∞ 1/dn log ∥F (n)(z)∥v.
sources.match: Baker–Rumely's homogeneous local dynamical height is G_{F,v} (with their normalised |·|_v; see the API item escapeRate_rpow_abv).
