the Legendre-family symmetries are stated as identities between escape rates of conjugate lifts
explicit formulas for G_{F_t,v}(z, 1) at v ∤ 2 and v | 2
−log ‖s(z)‖_{t,v} = G_{F_t,v}(z, 1) defines the invariant adelic metric on O(1)
the Arakelov–Green function g_{φ,v} is built from Ĥ_{F,v} = G_{F,v}
good reduction is detected by G_{F,v} = log ‖·‖_v

api.name: escapeRate
api.statement: For v an absolute value on K, a lift F of degree d and x ∈ K², escapeRate v F x = lim_{n→∞} d^{−n}·log ‖Fⁿ(x)‖_v (defined through limUnder; DY.2/escape-rate-tendsto shows the limit exists for x ≠ 0 and d ≥ 2).

api.name: escapeRate_tendsto
api.statement: d ≥ 2, Res F ≠ 0, x ≠ 0 ⟹ d^{−n} log ‖Fⁿ(x)‖_v → escapeRate v F x (node DY.2/escape-rate-tendsto).

api.name: escapeRate_apply_lift
api.statement: escapeRate v F (F x) = d · escapeRate v F x (node DY.2/escape-rate-functional-equation).

api.name: escapeRate_smul
api.statement: escapeRate v F (a • x) = escapeRate v F x + log (v a) for a ≠ 0 (node DY.2/escape-rate-homogeneity).

api.name: escapeRate_const_smul_lift
api.statement: escapeRate v (c • F) x = escapeRate v F x + log (v c)/(d − 1) for c ≠ 0 (node DY.2/escape-rate-scale-lift).

api.name: escapeRate_iterate_lift
api.statement: If G is a lift of degree dᵐ (m ≥ 1) with G.eval = (F.eval)^[m], then escapeRate v G x = escapeRate v F x (node DY.2/escape-rate-iterate-lift).

api.name: escapeRate_conj
api.statement: For A ∈ GL₂(K) and a lift G with G.eval y = A⁻¹·F.eval(A·y) (a lift of the conjugate map): escapeRate v G x = escapeRate v F (A·x) (node DY.2/escape-rate-conjugation).

api.name: escapeRate_abs_sub_log_norm_le
api.statement: There is C with |escapeRate v F x − log ‖x‖_v| ≤ C for all x ≠ 0; explicitly log c_v(F)/(d − 1) ≤ escapeRate v F x − log ‖x‖_v ≤ log C_v(F)/(d − 1) (node DY.2/escape-rate-sub-log-norm-bounds).

api.name: escapeRate_algebraMap
api.statement: For a field extension L/K and an absolute value w on L restricting to v, escapeRate w (F.map (algebraMap K L)) (algebraMap x) = escapeRate v F x (node DY.2/escape-rate-base-change).

api.name: escapeRate_comp_ringEquiv
api.statement: For σ : L ≃ₐ[K] L and absolute values w, w′ on L with w′ = w ∘ σ: escapeRate w′ F y = escapeRate w F (σ ∘ y) for F defined over K: the escape rate is Galois-equivariant (used for the Galois-averaged decomposition of DeMarco–Krieger–Ye (2.3)).

api.name: escapeRate_rpow_abv
api.statement: For 0 < s ≤ 1 (so that v^s is again an absolute value), escapeRate (v^s) F x = s · escapeRate v F x; this converts between the normalised absolute values of Mathlib's places and the standard ones |·|_p used by DeMarco–Krieger–Ye.

api.name: continuous_escapeRate
api.statement: For E a normed field and v its norm (NormedField.toAbsoluteValue), escapeRate is continuous on E² ∖ {0} (node DY.2/escape-rate-continuous).

api.name: escapeRate_nonpos_iff
api.statement: escapeRate v F x ≤ 0 ⟺ the orbit (Fⁿ(x))ₙ is bounded (node DY.2/escape-rate-nonpos-iff-bounded-orbit).

api.name: escapeRate_monomial
api.statement: For F = (X₀^d, X₁^d), escapeRate v F x = log ‖x‖_v at every absolute value v.

tests.name: escapeRate_powerMap
tests.statement: For F = (X₀², X₁²) over ℚ and v = |·|_∞: escapeRate v F (3, 1) = log 3 and escapeRate v F (1, 1) = 0.

tests.name: escapeRate_padicCantor_zero
tests.statement: For p prime, F = (X₀^p − X₀X₁^{p−1}, pX₁^p) over ℚ and v = |·|_p: escapeRate v F (0, 1) = −(log p)/(p − 1); the one-step value (1/p)·log ‖F(0, 1)‖_p = −(log p)/p is different, so the limit is not the first term.

tests.name: escapeRate_goodReduction_degenerate
tests.statement: For F = (X₀² − X₀X₁ − X₁², X₁²) and any prime p, escapeRate |·|_p F x = log ‖x‖_p for every x ∈ ℚ² ∖ {0}.

tests.name: escapeRate_monicPolynomial_compat
tests.statement: For a polynomial map f(z) = z² + c over ℂ with lift F = (X₀² + cX₁², X₁²): escapeRate |·| F (z, 1) = lim 2^{−n} log max(|fⁿ(z)|, 1), the Green function of the filled Julia set; for c = 0 this is Real.posLog |z|.

tests.name: escapeRate_depends_on_lift
tests.statement: The escape rate depends on the lift, not only on f: with F = (X₀², X₁²) and 2F, escapeRate |·|_∞ (2F) x = escapeRate |·|_∞ F x + log 2 ≠ escapeRate |·|_∞ F x.

nodes.title: Existence of the escape rate, with a uniform rate
nodes.statement: Let F be a lift of degree d ≥ 2 with Res(F) ≠ 0 and v an absolute value on K, with constants c_v = c_v(F) > 0 and C_v = C_v(F) from DY.2/lift-norm-lower-bound and DY.2/lift-norm-upper-bound, and B_v = max(log C_v, −log c_v). For every x ∈ K² ∖ {0} the limit G_{F,v}(x) = lim d^{−n} log ‖Fⁿ(x)‖_v exists, and |d^{−n} log ‖Fⁿ(x)‖_v − G_{F,v}(x)| ≤ B_v/((d − 1)·dⁿ) for all n ≥ 0; the convergence is uniform on K² ∖ {0}.
hypotheses: Res(F) ≠ 0
x ≠ 0 (so Fⁿ(x) ≠ 0 for all n, by the lower bound)
proofSteps: Put T_j(x) = d^{−(j+1)} log ‖F^{j+1}(x)‖ − d^{−j} log ‖F^j(x)‖ = d^{−(j+1)}(log ‖F(F^j x)‖ − d log ‖F^j x‖).
By the two bounds applied at y = F^j(x) ≠ 0: log c_v ≤ log ‖F(y)‖ − d log ‖y‖ ≤ log C_v, so |T_j(x)| ≤ B_v/d^{j+1}.
The telescoping series Σ_j T_j converges absolutely and uniformly (geometric tail, summable_geometric_of_lt_one), and its tail from n is ≤ B_v/((d − 1)dⁿ).
Hence the partial sums d^{−n} log ‖Fⁿ(x)‖ = log ‖x‖ + Σ_{j<n} T_j(x) converge uniformly; the limit is G_{F,v}(x) (limUnder of a convergent sequence).
acceptance: For F = (X₀², X₁²) all T_j vanish and G = log ‖·‖.
For the ℚ₃ example F = (X₀² + X₁², 3X₀X₁) and x = (i, 1) ∈ ℂ₃², the sequence 2^{−n} log ‖Fⁿ(x)‖₃ equals −(1/2)·log 3 from n = 1 on.

sources.excerpt: The limit limn→∞ 1/dn log ∥F (n)(z)∥v exists for all z ∈ C2v\{0}, and 1/dn log ∥F (n)(z)∥v converges uniformly on C2v\{0} to ĤF,v(z).
sources.match: The theorem, with the telescoping proof; the rate |T_j| ≤ C/d^{j+1} is BR's estimate.

nodes.title: Two-sided bound for G_{F,v} − log ‖·‖_v
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of DY.2/escape-rate-tendsto, for every x ∈ K² ∖ {0}: log c_v(F)/(d − 1) ≤ G_{F,v}(x) − log ‖x‖_v ≤ log C_v(F)/(d − 1). In particular |G_{F,v}(x) − log ‖x‖_v| ≤ B_v/(d − 1). If v is nonarchimedean and F is v-integral: log ‖x‖_v + log v(Res F)/(d − 1) ≤ G_{F,v}(x) ≤ log ‖x‖_v.
hypotheses: Res(F) ≠ 0
proofSteps: G(x) − log ‖x‖ = Σ_{j≥0} T_j(x) with d^{−(j+1)} log c_v ≤ T_j(x) ≤ d^{−(j+1)} log C_v (proof of DY.2/escape-rate-tendsto).
Sum the geometric series Σ_{j≥0} d^{−(j+1)} = 1/(d − 1).
The integral case uses c_v = v(Res F) and C_v ≤ 1 from the integral clauses of the two bound lemmas.
acceptance: For F = (X₀^p − X₀X₁^{p−1}, pX₁^p) over ℚ_p and x = (0, 1): the bounds read −p·log p/(p − 1) ≤ −(log p)/(p − 1) ≤ 0.

sources.excerpt: The proof yields the explicit bound | ĤF,v(z) −log ∥z∥v| ≤ C / (d −1), valid for all z ∈ C2v\{0}.
sources.match: The symmetric form; the node records the sharper one-sided constants that the same telescoping gives.

nodes.title: Functional equation G_{F,v}(F(x)) = d·G_{F,v}(x)
nodes.statement: For a lift F of degree d ≥ 2 with Res(F) ≠ 0 and x ∈ K² ∖ {0}: G_{F,v}(F(x)) = d·G_{F,v}(x). More generally G_{F,v}(Fᵐ(x)) = dᵐ·G_{F,v}(x).
hypotheses: Res(F) ≠ 0
proofSteps: d^{−n} log ‖Fⁿ(F x)‖ = d·d^{−(n+1)} log ‖F^{n+1}(x)‖; pass to the limit with DY.2/escape-rate-tendsto (F(x) ≠ 0 by the lower bound).
Induct on m.
acceptance: For F = (X₀², X₁²): log ‖(a², b²)‖ = 2 log ‖(a, b)‖.

sources.excerpt: (LH2) ĤF,v(F(z)) = d · ĤF,v(z).
sources.match: Exactly the statement.

nodes.title: Logarithmic homogeneity G_{F,v}(αx) = G_{F,v}(x) + log v(α)
nodes.statement: For α ∈ K^× and x ∈ K² ∖ {0}: G_{F,v}(αx) = G_{F,v}(x) + log v(α). Consequently x ↦ G_{F,v}(x) − log ‖x‖_v is constant on the lines through 0 and descends to ℙ¹(K).
hypotheses: Res(F) ≠ 0
proofSteps: Fⁿ is homogeneous of degree dⁿ, so Fⁿ(αx) = α^{dⁿ}Fⁿ(x) and d^{−n} log ‖Fⁿ(αx)‖ = log v(α) + d^{−n} log ‖Fⁿ(x)‖.
Pass to the limit (DY.2/escape-rate-tendsto); ‖αx‖ = v(α)‖x‖ gives the descent.
acceptance: G_{F,v}(2·x) = G_{F,v}(x) + log 2 at the archimedean place of ℚ.

sources.excerpt: (LH3) ĤF,v scales logarithmically, i.e., for all c ∈ C∗v, ĤF,v(cz) = ĤF,v(z) + log |c|v .
sources.match: Exactly the statement.

sources.excerpt: The final equality follows from the logarithmic homogeneity of G.
sources.match: Used in the Legendre symmetries.

nodes.title: Changing the lift: G_{cF,v} = G_{F,v} + log v(c)/(d − 1)
nodes.statement: For c ∈ K^×: G_{cF,v}(x) = G_{F,v}(x) + log v(c)/(d − 1) for all x ≠ 0. In particular the escape rate of a rational map is determined up to an additive constant, and for v-integral lifts normalised by max v(coeff) = 1 the constant is determined up to log v(unit) = 0.
hypotheses: Res(F) ≠ 0
proofSteps: By induction (cF)ⁿ = c^{(dⁿ − 1)/(d − 1)}·Fⁿ: (cF)^{n+1}(x) = c·F((cF)ⁿ(x)) = c·c^{d(dⁿ − 1)/(d − 1)}F^{n+1}(x) by homogeneity.

nodes.title: Transformation of the escape rate under conjugation
nodes.statement: Let A ∈ GL₂(K) and F^A = A⁻¹ ∘ F ∘ A (a lift of the conjugate φ⁻¹ ∘ f ∘ φ, φ the Möbius map of A; DY.0/conjugacy-of-rational-maps). Then G_{F^A,v}(x) = G_{F,v}(A x) for all x ≠ 0. More generally, for A, B ∈ GL₂(K) with B ∘ F = F′ ∘ B (F′ another lift of degree d), G_{F′,v}(Bx) = G_{F,v}(x). In DY.0's convention γ • f = γ ∘ f ∘ γ⁻¹ (DY.0/conjugacy-of-rational-maps), with γ the class of A, γ • f has the lift A ∘ F ∘ A⁻¹ and G_{A∘F∘A⁻¹, v}(x) = G_{F,v}(A⁻¹x).

A ∈ GL₂(K)

So |d^{−n} log ‖(F^A)ⁿ(x)‖ − d^{−n} log ‖Fⁿ(Ax)‖| ≤ d^{−n}·const → 0; conclude with DY.2/escape-rate-tendsto.

nodes.title: Continuity of the escape rate
nodes.statement: Let K be a normed field (archimedean or nonarchimedean, e.g. ℂ or ℂ_p) and v = ‖·‖. For a lift F of degree d ≥ 2 with Res(F) ≠ 0, x ↦ G_{F,v}(x) is continuous on K² ∖ {0}, and so is x ↦ G_{F,v}(x) − log ‖x‖_v, which descends to a continuous bounded function on ℙ¹(K).
hypotheses: K a normed field, v its norm
Res(F) ≠ 0
proofSteps: Each x ↦ d^{−n} log ‖Fⁿ(x)‖ is continuous on K² ∖ {0}: Fⁿ is polynomial, Fⁿ(x) ≠ 0 there (DY.2/lift-norm-lower-bound), and log and max are continuous on (0, ∞).
The convergence is uniform (DY.2/escape-rate-tendsto); a uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous (TendstoUniformly.continuous).
The difference with log ‖x‖ is bounded (DY.2/escape-rate-sub-log-norm-bounds) and homogeneous of degree 0 (DY.2/escape-rate-homogeneity), hence descends to ℙ¹(K) with the quotient topology.
acceptance: For f(z) = z² over ℂ the descended function is 0; for the (z^p − z)/p lift over ℂ_p the descended function equals −(log p)/(p − 1) on ℤ_p and 0 on {|z|_p > 1}, and is continuous in between.

nodes.title: G_{F,v}(x) ≤ 0 exactly on the filled Julia set of F
nodes.statement: For a lift F of degree d ≥ 2 with Res(F) ≠ 0, v an absolute value and x ∈ K²: the orbit (Fⁿ(x))ₙ is bounded for ‖·‖_v if and only if x = 0 or G_{F,v}(x) ≤ 0. If G_{F,v}(x) > 0 then ‖Fⁿ(x)‖_v → ∞.
hypotheses: Res(F) ≠ 0
proofSteps: If ‖Fⁿ x‖ ≤ M for all n then d^{−n} log ‖Fⁿ x‖ ≤ d^{−n} log M → 0.
Conversely put R = c_v^{−1/(d−1)} (so c_v = R^{−(d−1)}), giving ‖F(z)‖ ≥ R·(‖z‖/R)^d for all z (DY.2/lift-norm-lower-bound).
If ‖y‖ > R, put α = ‖y‖/R > 1; by induction ‖Fⁿ(y)‖ ≥ R·α^{dⁿ}, hence G(y) ≥ lim d^{−n}(log R + dⁿ log α) = log α > 0 and ‖Fⁿ(y)‖ → ∞.
An unbounded orbit reaches some y = F^{n₀}(x) with ‖y‖ > R, and G(x) = d^{−n₀}·G(y) > 0 by DY.2/escape-rate-functional-equation.
acceptance: For the (z^p − z)/p lift over ℚ_p, G(x, 1) ≤ 0 exactly for x ∈ ℤ_p (the orbit of x ∈ ℤ_p stays in ℤ_p).

nodes.title: Good reduction implies G_{F,v} = log ‖·‖_v
nodes.statement: Let v be a nonarchimedean absolute value on K and f a rational map of degree d ≥ 2 with good reduction at v (DY.0/good-reduction-of-a-rational-map), and let F be a normalised lift (v-integral coefficients, v(Res F) = 1). Then G_{F,v}(x) = log ‖x‖_v for every x ∈ K² ∖ {0}, over K and over every extension of v (in particular over ℂ_v). No algebraic closedness of K is needed.
hypotheses: v nonarchimedean
F v-integral with v(Res F) = 1
proofSteps: ‖Fⁿ(x)‖ = ‖x‖^{dⁿ} (DY.2/lift-norm-of-good-reduction), so every term of the defining sequence equals log ‖x‖.
The extension statement follows from DY.2/escape-rate-base-change, since the normalisation of F is preserved by extension of v.

nodes.title: G_{F,v} = log ‖·‖_v on an algebraically closed field implies good reduction
nodes.statement: Let K be a field with a nonarchimedean absolute value v whose residue field is algebraically closed (for instance K algebraically closed, e.g. ℂ_v), and let F be a lift of degree d ≥ 2 with v-integral coefficients, some coefficient of absolute value 1. If G_{F,v}(x) = log ‖x‖_v for all x ∈ K² ∖ {0}, then v(Res F) = 1, i.e. f has good reduction at v. The hypothesis on the residue field cannot be dropped: see DY.2/example-bad-reduction-nonclosed-field.
hypotheses: v nonarchimedean
residue field k of v algebraically closed
F v-integral and normalised (max v(coeff) = 1)
proofSteps: Suppose v(Res F) < 1. By DY.0/good-reduction-iff-normalized-resultant-unit the resultant of the reduced forms F̃₀, F̃₁ vanishes in k (the resultant commutes with reduction, an API item of DY.0/resultant-of-a-rational-map), and F̃ ≠ (0, 0) since F is normalised.
By DY.0/binary-resultant-eq-zero-iff the forms F̃₀, F̃₁ have a common nontrivial zero over an algebraic closure of k, hence over k itself since k is algebraically closed; call it ỹ ≠ 0 in k².
Lift ỹ to y in the valuation ring with ‖y‖ = 1; then ‖F(y)‖ < 1.
By the integral upper bound ‖F(z)‖ ≤ ‖z‖^d, ‖Fⁿ(y)‖ ≤ ‖F(y)‖^{d^{n−1}}, so G(y) ≤ (1/d)·log ‖F(y)‖ < 0 = log ‖y‖, a contradiction.
acceptance: For F = (X₀² + X₁², 3X₀X₁) over ℂ₃: G(i, 1) = −(1/2)·log 3 < 0 = log ‖(i, 1)‖, consistent with v(Res F) = 1/9.

nodes.title: G_{F,v} = log ‖·‖_v at all but finitely many places
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, F a lift over K of degree d ≥ 2 with Res(F) ≠ 0 and x ∈ K² ∖ {0}. There is a finite set S of finite places of K such that for every finite place v ∉ S: F is v-integral with v(Res F) = 1, ‖x‖_v = 1, and G_{F,v}(x) = log ‖x‖_v = 0.

Res(F) ≠ 0

Outside the union S of these finite sets, F has good reduction at v and ‖x‖_v = 1; conclude with DY.2/escape-rate-of-good-reduction.

nodes.title: The local canonical height λ̂_{F,v}
nodes.statement: Conventions (pinned for the whole layer): K is a field and v : K → ℝ an absolute value (Mathlib's AbsoluteValue K ℝ); for x = (x₀, x₁) ∈ K², ‖x‖_v = max(v(x₀), v(x₁)) (Mathlib's ⨆ i, v (x i)). A lift of a rational map f of degree d is a pair F = (F₀, F₁) of binary forms of degree d with Res(F) ≠ 0 (DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line, DY.0/resultant-of-a-rational-map); f([x₀ : x₁]) = [F₀(x) : F₁(x)], the affine coordinate is z ↔ [z : 1], ∞ = [1 : 0], and Fⁿ is the n-fold composite, a lift of fⁿ of degree dⁿ. The local canonical height of F at v (relative to the divisor (∞), in the affine coordinate) is λ̂_{F,v}(z) = G_{F,v}(z, 1) for z ∈ K; homogeneously, λ̂_{F,v}([x₀ : x₁]) = G_{F,v}(x₀, x₁) − log v(x₁) for x₁ ≠ 0, which is independent of the representative by DY.2/escape-rate-homogeneity. It is the DeMarco–Krieger–Ye local height λ_{t,v} (for F = F_t) and the Baker–Rumely height ĥ_{F,v,(∞)} (in their chart), and depends on the lift F only through the additive constant log v(c)/(d − 1).
hypotheses: Res(F) ≠ 0
proofSteps: Define λ̂_{F,v}(z) := G_{F,v}(z, 1).
The homogeneous formula: G_{F,v}(x₀, x₁) = G_{F,v}(x₀/x₁, 1) + log v(x₁) by DY.2/escape-rate-homogeneity.
acceptance: For F = (X₀², X₁²): λ̂ = log⁺ v.
For good reduction at v: λ̂ = log⁺ v.

nodes.title: The normalised dynamical Green function g_{F,v} on ℙ¹(K)
nodes.statement: For a lift F of degree d ≥ 2 with Res(F) ≠ 0 and an absolute value v on K, the dynamical Green function is g_{F,v} : ℙ¹(K) → ℝ, g_{F,v}([x]) = G_{F,v}(x) − log ‖x‖_v. It is bounded, and λ̂_{F,v}(z) = g_{F,v}([z : 1]) + log⁺ v(z). It is the function that extends to the Berkovich line (DY.2/berkovich-escape-potential) and whose Laplacian gives the canonical measure.

Boundedness is DY.2/escape-rate-sub-log-norm-bounds; the relation with λ̂ uses ‖(z, 1)‖_v = max(v(z), 1) and log max(v(z), 1) = log⁺ v(z).

nodes.title: The global height limit is the sum of the escape rates
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field with Mathlib's places: InfinitePlace K (with multiplicity mult(v)) and FinitePlace K (normalised absolute values), so that Height.logHeight x = Σ_{v | ∞} mult(v)·log ‖x‖_v + Σ_{v ∤ ∞} log ‖x‖_v for x ∈ K² ∖ {0}. For a lift F over K of degree d ≥ 2 with Res(F) ≠ 0 and x ∈ K² ∖ {0}, the limit lim_{n→∞} d^{−n}·Height.logHeight(Fⁿ(x)) exists and equals Σ_{v | ∞} mult(v)·G_{F,v}(x) + Σ_{v ∤ ∞} G_{F,v}(x), a sum with only finitely many nonzero terms. The right-hand side does not change when x is replaced by αx (α ∈ K^×) or F by cF (c ∈ K^×).
hypotheses: K a number field
Res(F) ≠ 0
proofSteps: Let S be the finite set of DY.2/escape-rate-trivial-at-almost-all-places for F and x. For v ∉ S finite, ‖Fⁿ(x)‖_v = 1 for all n (DY.2/lift-norm-of-good-reduction), so those places contribute 0 to every term.

Hence d^{−n}·logHeight(Fⁿ x) = Σ_{v | ∞} mult(v)·d^{−n} log ‖Fⁿ x‖_v + Σ_{v ∈ S} d^{−n} log ‖Fⁿ x‖_v (NumberField.mulHeight_eq, sum over a finite set), a finite sum of convergent sequences (DY.2/escape-rate-tendsto).

Independence of x ↦ αx: the sum changes by Σ_v n_v log v(α) = 0 (product formula NumberField.prod_abs_eq_one) using DY.2/escape-rate-homogeneity; independence of F ↦ cF: it changes by (1/(d − 1))·Σ_v n_v log v(c) = 0 using DY.2/escape-rate-scale-lift.

F a lift over K of f, d ≥ 2

nodes.title: Periodic points reduce to periodic points with dividing period
nodes.statement: Setting: v is a nonarchimedean absolute value on K with valuation ring 𝒪 = {a : v(a) ≤ 1}, maximal ideal 𝔪 = {a : v(a) < 1} and residue field k = 𝒪/𝔪 (Mathlib's ValuationSubring and IsLocalRing.ResidueField), a ↦ ã the residue map; p = char k ≥ 0 is the residue characteristic. A lift F is normalised if its coefficients lie in 𝒪 and one of them is a unit; f has good reduction at v when v(Res F) = 1 for a normalised lift (DY.0/good-reduction-of-a-rational-map), and then f̃ = [F̃₀ : F̃₁] is a rational map over k of the same degree d. If f has good reduction at v and P ∈ ℙ¹(K) is periodic for f of exact period n, then red(P) is periodic for f̃ of exact period m dividing n. Preperiodic points reduce to preperiodic points.
hypotheses: v nonarchimedean
f has good reduction at v
P periodic of exact period n
proofSteps: By DY.0/reduction-commutes-with-evaluation, red semiconjugates f to f̃, so IsPeriodicPt f n P implies IsPeriodicPt f̃ n (red P) (Mathlib's Function.IsPeriodicPt.map).
Hence minimalPeriod f̃ (red P) divides n (Function.IsPeriodicPt.minimalPeriod_dvd).
For preperiodic P, fᵃ(P) = fᵇ(P) gives f̃ᵃ(red P) = f̃ᵇ(red P).
acceptance: f(z) = z² − z − 1: the 2-cycle {1, −1} reduces mod 3 to the 2-cycle {1, 2} of z² + 2z + 2 (m = n = 2) and mod 2 to the fixed point 1 of z² + z + 1 (m = 1 divides n = 2).

nodes.title: The multiplier of a periodic cycle
nodes.statement: Let f be a rational map of degree d ≥ 1 over a field K (any characteristic; DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line) and P ∈ ℙ¹(K) periodic of exact period n ≥ 1. The multiplier of the cycle of P is λ(P) = λ_{fⁿ}(P), the fixed-point multiplier of fⁿ at P (DY.0/fixed-point-multiplier). With a lift F, Φ = Fⁿ and Φ(x) = μ·x for a representative x of P, DY.0's trace formula gives λ(P) = tr(DΦ(x))/μ − dⁿ with dⁿ read in K: no division by the degree occurs, so the residue characteristic is kept (in characteristic p | d the value is still defined). In an affine chart containing the orbit, λ(P) = ∏_{i<n} f′(fⁱ(z)) (DY.2/multiplier-chain-rule); it is the same for all points of the cycle (DY.2/multiplier-constant-on-cycle), and for P fixed by fᵐ (n | m) the multiplier of P for fᵐ is λ(P)^{m/n}.
hypotheses: P periodic of exact period n ≥ 1 for f
proofSteps: Define λ(P) := λ_{fⁿ}(P) with n = minimalPeriod (toEnd f) P (Mathlib's Function.minimalPeriod; toEnd is DY.0/rational-map-action-on-points), using DY.0/fixed-point-multiplier for fⁿ, the n-th power in DY.0's monoid of rational maps.
The trace formula is DY.0's characterisation of the fixed-point multiplier, applied to the lift Fⁿ of fⁿ.
acceptance: The tests; DY.2/multiplier-chain-rule identifies the value with the product of derivatives along the cycle.

sources.excerpt: Given a periodic point x ∈P1(L) of minimal period n ≥1, we define the multiplier of x to be λ := (φn)′(x), at least in the case that x̸ = ∞.
sources.match: The multiplier of a periodic point as the multiplier of the fixed point x of φⁿ.

sources.excerpt: Let α be a periodic point of ϕ of exact period n. The multiplier of ϕ at α is the quantity λα(ϕ) = (ϕn)′(α).

nodes.title: Chain rule: the multiplier of a cycle is a product of derivatives
nodes.statement: Write λₙ(P) = λ_{fⁿ}(P) for the multiplier of P as a fixed point of fⁿ (DY.0/fixed-point-multiplier). If P = [z : 1] has fⁿ(P) = P and the orbit z, f(z), …, f^{n−1}(z) avoids ∞ and the poles of f, then λₙ(P) = ∏_{i=0}^{n−1} f′(fⁱ(z)).

orbit in the affine chart where f is regular
proofSteps: By DY.0/fixed-point-multiplier, λ_{fⁿ}(P) is the derivative at z of the rational function of fⁿ, and (fⁿ)′(z) = ∏ f′(fⁱ(z)) by the chain rule for rational functions (Polynomial.derivative_comp on numerators and denominators).

nodes.title: All points of a cycle have the same multiplier
nodes.statement: Write λₙ(P) = λ_{fⁿ}(P) for the multiplier of P as a fixed point of fⁿ (DY.0/fixed-point-multiplier). If fⁿ(P) = P then λₙ(f(P)) = λₙ(P); hence λₙ is constant on the cycle of P, and for P of exact period n the multiplier of the cycle is well defined. Also λ_{kn}(P) = λₙ(P)^k.

proofSteps: Choose A ∈ GL₂(K̄) moving the finite cycle of P off ∞ and off the poles of f (a Möbius map avoiding finitely many points exists over the infinite field K̄); by DY.0/fixed-point-multiplier-conj the multipliers are unchanged.
In the chart, DY.2/multiplier-chain-rule gives λₙ(fʲ(z)) = ∏_{i} f′(f^{i+j}(z)), the same cyclic product for every j.
λ_{kn}(z) = ∏_{i<kn} f′(fⁱ(z)) = (∏_{i<n} f′(fⁱ(z)))^k by periodicity of the orbit.
The identity holds over K because DY.0's multiplier is compatible with base change to K̄ (DY.0/rational-map-base-change).

nodes.title: Multipliers of cycles reduce to multipliers
nodes.statement: Setting: v is a nonarchimedean absolute value on K with valuation ring 𝒪 = {a : v(a) ≤ 1}, maximal ideal 𝔪 = {a : v(a) < 1} and residue field k = 𝒪/𝔪 (Mathlib's ValuationSubring and IsLocalRing.ResidueField), a ↦ ã the residue map; p = char k ≥ 0 is the residue characteristic. A lift F is normalised if its coefficients lie in 𝒪 and one of them is a unit; f has good reduction at v when v(Res F) = 1 for a normalised lift (DY.0/good-reduction-of-a-rational-map), and then f̃ = [F̃₀ : F̃₁] is a rational map over k of the same degree d. Let f have good reduction at v and P ∈ ℙ¹(K) with fⁿ(P) = P. Then the multiplier λₙ(f, P) := λ_{fⁿ}(P) (DY.0/fixed-point-multiplier) lies in 𝒪 and its residue is the multiplier of the reduced point: (λₙ(f, P))~ = λₙ(f̃, red P) ∈ k, computed in characteristic p = char k by the same formula. In particular |λₙ(f, P)|_v ≤ 1, and λₙ(f, P) ∈ 𝔪 whenever f̃ⁿ is inseparable (in characteristic p, f̃ⁿ ∈ k(z^p) has derivative 0, so all its multipliers vanish).
hypotheses: v nonarchimedean
f has good reduction at v
fⁿ(P) = P

nodes.title: Expansion of a map of good reduction on a fixed residue disc
nodes.statement: Setting: v is a nonarchimedean absolute value on K with valuation ring 𝒪 = {a : v(a) ≤ 1}, maximal ideal 𝔪 = {a : v(a) < 1} and residue field k = 𝒪/𝔪 (Mathlib's ValuationSubring and IsLocalRing.ResidueField), a ↦ ã the residue map; p = char k ≥ 0 is the residue characteristic. A lift F is normalised if its coefficients lie in 𝒪 and one of them is a unit; f has good reduction at v when v(Res F) = 1 for a normalised lift (DY.0/good-reduction-of-a-rational-map), and then f̃ = [F̃₀ : F̃₁] is a rational map over k of the same degree d. Let g have good reduction and suppose red(0) = [0 : 1] is fixed by g̃ (v(g(0)) < 1). Then for z ∈ 𝔪: g(z) = µ + λz + z²·A(z)/(1 + z·B(z)) with µ = g(0) ∈ 𝔪, λ = g′(0) ∈ 𝒪, A, B ∈ 𝒪[z]; g maps 𝔪 into 𝔪, λ̃ is the multiplier of the fixed point 0̃ of g̃, and for every ν ∈ K with µ ∈ ν𝒪: g(z) ≡ µ + λz mod ν²𝒪 for all z ∈ ν𝒪.

g has good reduction

nodes.title: Periods of points under good reduction (Morton–Silverman)
nodes.statement: Setting: v is a nonarchimedean absolute value on K with valuation ring 𝒪 = {a : v(a) ≤ 1}, maximal ideal 𝔪 = {a : v(a) < 1} and residue field k = 𝒪/𝔪 (Mathlib's ValuationSubring and IsLocalRing.ResidueField), a ↦ ã the residue map; p = char k ≥ 0 is the residue characteristic. A lift F is normalised if its coefficients lie in 𝒪 and one of them is a unit; f has good reduction at v when v(Res F) = 1 for a normalised lift (DY.0/good-reduction-of-a-rational-map), and then f̃ = [F̃₀ : F̃₁] is a rational map over k of the same degree d. Let f have degree d ≥ 2 and good reduction at v, and let P ∈ ℙ¹(K) be periodic of exact period n. Let m be the exact period of red(P) under f̃, λ̃ = λ_m(f̃, red P) ∈ k the multiplier of the reduced cycle, and r the multiplicative order of λ̃ in k^× (r = ∞ when λ̃ = 0 or λ̃ is not a root of unity). Then either n = m, or n = m·r·p^e for some e ≥ 0, where p = char k; if char k = 0 then e = 0. (Over ℚ_p the exponent satisfies e ≤ 1 for p odd and e ≤ 3 for p = 2 by DY.2/period-exponent-bound.)

f of degree ≥ 2 with good reduction at v
P ∈ ℙ¹(K) periodic of exact period n
proofSteps: m | n by DY.2/reduction-of-periodic-points. Replace f by g = f^m (good reduction and g̃ = f̃^m by DY.0/reduction-commutes-with-composition); P has exact period N = n/m under g (Function.minimalPeriod_iterate_eq_div_gcd) and red P is fixed by g̃ with multiplier λ̃.

If N = 1 then n = m. Otherwise choose A ∈ GL₂(𝒪) whose second column is a primitive representative of P (so A·[0 : 1] = P and det A is a unit) and conjugate: the conjugate has good reduction (DY.0/good-reduction-conj-integral), P moves to 0, and periods and multipliers are unchanged (DY.0/fixed-point-multiplier-conj).
If λ̃ ≠ 1: by DY.2/orbit-congruence-geometric-sum λ̃ ≠ 0 and λ̃^N = 1, so r is finite and r | N. Replace g by g^r and N by N/r; the new multiplier λ̃^r = 1. If N/r = 1 then n = m·r.

If λ̃ = 1 and N ≥ 2: DY.2/orbit-congruence-geometric-sum gives N = 0 in k, so p = char k > 0 and p | N; replace g by g^p (multiplier still ≡ 1) and N by N/p, and repeat. The process stops since N decreases; it ends with N = 1, giving n = m·r·p^e (r = 1 when the reduced multiplier was already 1).
In characteristic 0 the second case would give N = 0 in k with N ≥ 2, impossible; so e = 0.

If char k = 0 (e.g. K = ℂ((t)) with the t-adic absolute value) no p-power case occurs.

nodes.title: Valuation recursion along p-power iterates (Hutz)
nodes.statement: Setting: v is a nonarchimedean absolute value on K with valuation ring 𝒪 = {a : v(a) ≤ 1}, maximal ideal 𝔪 = {a : v(a) < 1} and residue field k = 𝒪/𝔪 (Mathlib's ValuationSubring and IsLocalRing.ResidueField), a ↦ ã the residue map; p = char k ≥ 0 is the residue characteristic. A lift F is normalised if its coefficients lie in 𝒪 and one of them is a unit; f has good reduction at v when v(Res F) = 1 for a normalised lift (DY.0/good-reduction-of-a-rational-map), and then f̃ = [F̃₀ : F̃₁] is a rational map over k of the same degree d. Assume moreover that v is discrete, normalised by v(π) = 1 for a uniformiser π, write ord for the valuation (so ord(p) is the absolute ramification index when char K = 0), and p = char k > 0. Let g have good reduction, with 0 a periodic point of exact period p^e (e ≥ 1), g̃(0̃) = 0̃ and g′(0) ≡ 1 mod 𝔪. For 0 ≤ k ≤ e − 1 put x_k = g^{p^k}(0), b_k = ord(x_k) and c_k = ord((g^{p^k})′(0) − 1) (∞ if the difference is 0). Then b₀, c₀ ≥ 1, and for 0 ≤ k ≤ e − 2: b_{k+1} ≥ min(2b_k, b_k + (p − 1)c_k, b_k + ord(p)) and c_{k+1} ≥ min(b_k, c_k + ord(p), p·c_k). Moreover min(b_{e−1}, c_{e−1}) ≤ ord(p), and if b_{e−1} > ord(p) then (p − 1)·c_{e−1} ≤ ord(p).
hypotheses: v discrete, normalised
residue characteristic p > 0
0 of exact period p^e, e ≥ 1, fixed mod 𝔪 with multiplier ≡ 1
proofSteps: Apply DY.2/residue-disc-expansion to h_k = g^{p^k}: h_k(z) = x_k + λ_k z + O(z²) on 𝔪, with λ_k = 1 + (unit)·π^{c_k}.

x_{k+1} = h_k^p(0) ≡ (1 + λ_k + ⋯ + λ_k^{p−1})·x_k mod x_k²; expand λ_k^i = Σ_j C(i, j)(λ_k − 1)^j and use the hockey-stick identity Σ_{i=1}^{p−1} C(i, j) = C(p, j + 1) (Mathlib's Nat.sum_Icc_choose), divisible by p for 1 ≤ j ≤ p − 2 (Nat.Prime.dvd_choose_self), with the last coefficient 1: this gives the bound for b_{k+1}.
(h_k^p)′(0) ≡ (h_k′(0))^p mod π^{b_k} (chain rule along the orbit, which stays within π^{b_k}𝒪 of 0), and (1 + u)^p − 1 has valuation ≥ min(c_k + ord(p), p·c_k): this gives the bound for c_{k+1}.
At k = e − 1, x_e = g^{p^e}(0) = 0 ≠ x_{e−1}, so 1 + λ + ⋯ + λ^{p−1} ≡ 0 mod π^{b_{e−1}}; its valuation is min(ord(p), (p − 1)c_{e−1}) when these differ, giving the final assertions.

nodes.title: Bound on the p-power in the period (Hutz)
nodes.statement: Setting: v is a nonarchimedean absolute value on K with valuation ring 𝒪 = {a : v(a) ≤ 1}, maximal ideal 𝔪 = {a : v(a) < 1} and residue field k = 𝒪/𝔪 (Mathlib's ValuationSubring and IsLocalRing.ResidueField), a ↦ ã the residue map; p = char k ≥ 0 is the residue characteristic. A lift F is normalised if its coefficients lie in 𝒪 and one of them is a unit; f has good reduction at v when v(Res F) = 1 for a normalised lift (DY.0/good-reduction-of-a-rational-map), and then f̃ = [F̃₀ : F̃₁] is a rational map over k of the same degree d. Let v be discrete and normalised, p = char k > 0, and let f have good reduction. In DY.2/periods-under-good-reduction the exponent satisfies 2^{e−1} ≤ ord(p) if p is odd, and F_{e−1} ≤ ord(2) if p = 2, where F_j is the j-th Fibonacci number (Mathlib's Nat.fib). In particular over ℚ_p (ord(p) = 1): e ≤ 1 for p odd and e ≤ 3 for p = 2.
hypotheses: v discrete normalised
p = char k > 0
f good reduction
proofSteps: Reduce as in DY.2/periods-under-good-reduction to g = f^{m r} with 0 of exact period p^e, fixed mod 𝔪 with multiplier ≡ 1.

Let k₀ ≤ e − 1 be the first index with b_{k₀} > ord(p) (k₀ = e if none). For k < k₀, DY.2/p-power-iterate-valuation-recursion gives inductively b_k ≥ 2^k and c_k ≥ 2^{k−1} (p odd), respectively b_k ≥ F_{k+1} and c_k ≥ F_k (p = 2), starting from b₀, c₀ ≥ 1 and b₁ ≥ 2.
If b_{e−1} ≤ ord(p) then 2^{e−1} ≤ b_{e−1} ≤ ord(p) (resp. F_e ≤ ord(2)).

If b_{e−1} > ord(p) then (p − 1)·c_{e−1} ≤ ord(p) by DY.2/p-power-iterate-valuation-recursion. The b_k increase strictly (each term of the b-recursion exceeds b_k), so b_k ≥ ord(p) + 1 for all k ≥ k₀, and the c-recursion gives c_{k+1} ≥ min(ord(p) + 1, p·c_k) for k₀ ≤ k ≤ e − 2.

If for some such k the minimum were ord(p) + 1, then (inductively) c_{e−1} ≥ ord(p) + 1 > ord(p)/(p − 1), a contradiction; so c_{k+1} ≥ p·c_k along the chain and c_{e−1} ≥ p^{e−1−k₀}·c_{k₀} ≥ 2^{e−2} for p odd (using c_{k₀} ≥ 2^{k₀−1}, or c₀ ≥ 1 if k₀ = 0), respectively ≥ F_{e−1} for p = 2 (F_{i+1} ≤ 2F_i).
Hence 2^{e−1} ≤ (p − 1)·2^{e−2} ≤ ord(p) for p odd, and F_{e−1} ≤ c_{e−1} ≤ ord(2) for p = 2 (Mathlib's Nat.fib); in the first case likewise F_{e−1} ≤ F_e ≤ ord(2).

nodes.title: The lift bounds at points of the Berkovich affine line
nodes.statement: Setting: K is a complete nonarchimedean field (algebraically closed where stated, e.g. ℂ_v) with absolute value |·|; P^{1,an}_K = A^{1,an}_K ∪ {∞} is the Berkovich projective line of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0, whose points x ∈ A^{1,an}_K are multiplicative seminorms g ↦ [g]_x on K[T] extending |·|, with the weakest topology making every x ↦ [g]_x continuous; ℙ¹(K) ⊂ P^{1,an}_K is dense, ζ_{a,r} is the sup-norm of the closed disc D(a, r) and ζ_{0,1} is the Gauss point; a rational map f acts by its analytification f^{an} ([g]_{f^{an}(x)} = [g ∘ f]_x). The Laplacian Δ on P^{1,an}_K is the one of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.1, normalised as in DeMarco–Krieger–Ye: Δ log max([T], 1) = δ_{ζ_{0,1}} − δ_∞ (the negative of Baker–Rumely's). For a lift F of degree d with Res(F) ≠ 0 over K and every x ∈ A^{1,an}_K: c(F)·max([T]_x, 1)^d ≤ max([F₀(T, 1)]_x, [F₁(T, 1)]_x) ≤ C(F)·max([T]_x, 1)^d, with the nonarchimedean constants of DY.2/lift-norm-lower-bound and DY.2/lift-norm-upper-bound. Hence the functions x ↦ d^{−n}·log max([Fⁿ₀(T, 1)]_x, [Fⁿ₁(T, 1)]_x) − log max([T]_x, 1) converge uniformly on A^{1,an}_K.
hypotheses: K complete nonarchimedean
Res(F) ≠ 0
proofSteps: A multiplicative seminorm on K[T] extending a nonarchimedean absolute value is nonarchimedean ([n]_x = |n| ≤ 1 for n ∈ ℕ), so the ultrametric estimates of DY.2/lift-norm-upper-bound hold for [·]_x.
Evaluate the certificate identities H₀F₀ + H₁F₁ = Res(F)·X₁^{2d−1}, G₀F₀ + G₁F₁ = Res(F)·X₀^{2d−1} at (T, 1) and apply [·]_x (multiplicative) as in DY.2/lift-norm-lower-bound.

nodes.title: The escape potential on the Berkovich line
nodes.statement: Setting: K is a complete nonarchimedean field (algebraically closed where stated, e.g. ℂ_v) with absolute value |·|; P^{1,an}_K = A^{1,an}_K ∪ {∞} is the Berkovich projective line of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0, whose points x ∈ A^{1,an}_K are multiplicative seminorms g ↦ [g]_x on K[T] extending |·|, with the weakest topology making every x ↦ [g]_x continuous; ℙ¹(K) ⊂ P^{1,an}_K is dense, ζ_{a,r} is the sup-norm of the closed disc D(a, r) and ζ_{0,1} is the Gauss point; a rational map f acts by its analytification f^{an} ([g]_{f^{an}(x)} = [g ∘ f]_x). The Laplacian Δ on P^{1,an}_K is the one of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.1, normalised as in DeMarco–Krieger–Ye: Δ log max([T], 1) = δ_{ζ_{0,1}} − δ_∞ (the negative of Baker–Rumely's). For a lift F of degree d ≥ 2 with Res(F) ≠ 0, the Berkovich escape potential ĝ_F : P^{1,an}_K → ℝ is ĝ_F(x) = lim_n (d^{−n} log max([Fⁿ₀(T, 1)]_x, [Fⁿ₁(T, 1)]_x) − log max([T]_x, 1)) for x ∈ A^{1,an}_K and ĝ_F(∞) = g_{F,v}([1 : 0]). It is continuous and bounded, and it is the unique continuous extension of the Green function g_{F,v} of DY.2/dynamical-green-function. The extended local canonical height is λ̂^{an}_F = ĝ_F + log max([T], 1) on A^{1,an}_K.
hypotheses: K complete nonarchimedean
Res(F) ≠ 0
proofSteps: On A^{1,an}_K the defining sequence converges uniformly (DY.2/berkovich-lift-bounds), and each term is continuous in the Gelfand topology (TB.0), so ĝ_F is continuous on A^{1,an}_K.

Near ∞ use the chart u = 1/T: in the coordinates (X₁, X₀) the same construction applies to the swapped lift, and the two formulas agree on A^{1,an}_K ∖ {0} (homogeneity, DY.2/escape-rate-homogeneity, applied seminorm-wise); this gives continuity at ∞.
On type I points the limit is g_{F,v} (the evaluation seminorm at a is g ↦ |g(a)|); uniqueness of the extension follows from density of ℙ¹(K) in P^{1,an}_K (TB.0).
acceptance: Test berkovichEscapePotential_gauss_padicCantor.

nodes.title: The canonical measure µ_{f,v} on the Berkovich line
nodes.statement: Setting: K is a complete nonarchimedean field (algebraically closed where stated, e.g. ℂ_v) with absolute value |·|; P^{1,an}_K = A^{1,an}_K ∪ {∞} is the Berkovich projective line of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0, whose points x ∈ A^{1,an}_K are multiplicative seminorms g ↦ [g]_x on K[T] extending |·|, with the weakest topology making every x ↦ [g]_x continuous; ℙ¹(K) ⊂ P^{1,an}_K is dense, ζ_{a,r} is the sup-norm of the closed disc D(a, r) and ζ_{0,1} is the Gauss point; a rational map f acts by its analytification f^{an} ([g]_{f^{an}(x)} = [g ∘ f]_x). The Laplacian Δ on P^{1,an}_K is the one of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.1, normalised as in DeMarco–Krieger–Ye: Δ log max([T], 1) = δ_{ζ_{0,1}} − δ_∞ (the negative of Baker–Rumely's). For a rational map f of degree d ≥ 2 over K with lift F, the canonical measure is µ_{f,v} = Δĝ_F + δ_{ζ_{0,1}}, a Borel measure on P^{1,an}_K; equivalently Δλ̂^{an}_F = µ_{f,v} − δ_∞ (DeMarco–Krieger–Ye's normalisation). It does not depend on the lift (ĝ_{cF} − ĝ_F is constant, and Δ kills constants). For K not algebraically closed one works over the completion of an algebraic closure (ℂ_v); the measure is invariant under the continuous automorphisms of that field over K.
hypotheses: K complete nonarchimedean
proofSteps: ĝ_F is continuous (DY.2/berkovich-escape-potential) and of bounded differential variation (it is a uniform limit of differences of functions log max([P], [Q]) with P, Q ∈ K[T]); its Laplacian Δĝ_F is a signed Borel measure of total mass 0 (TB.1).
Define µ_{f,v} = Δĝ_F + δ_{ζ_{0,1}}; independence of the lift follows from berkovichEscapePotential_const_smul_lift.
acceptance: The tests; positivity and total mass 1 are DY.2/canonical-measure-is-probability.

nodes.title: Δλ̂_{f,v} = µ_{f,v} − δ_∞
nodes.statement: Setting: K is a complete nonarchimedean field (algebraically closed where stated, e.g. ℂ_v) with absolute value |·|; P^{1,an}_K = A^{1,an}_K ∪ {∞} is the Berkovich projective line of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0, whose points x ∈ A^{1,an}_K are multiplicative seminorms g ↦ [g]_x on K[T] extending |·|, with the weakest topology making every x ↦ [g]_x continuous; ℙ¹(K) ⊂ P^{1,an}_K is dense, ζ_{a,r} is the sup-norm of the closed disc D(a, r) and ζ_{0,1} is the Gauss point; a rational map f acts by its analytification f^{an} ([g]_{f^{an}(x)} = [g ∘ f]_x). The Laplacian Δ on P^{1,an}_K is the one of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.1, normalised as in DeMarco–Krieger–Ye: Δ log max([T], 1) = δ_{ζ_{0,1}} − δ_∞ (the negative of Baker–Rumely's). The extended local canonical height λ̂^{an}_F = ĝ_F + log max([T], 1) satisfies Δλ̂^{an}_F = µ_{f,v} − δ_∞ on P^{1,an}_K.
hypotheses: K complete nonarchimedean
proofSteps: Linearity of Δ and the normalisation Δ log max([T], 1) = δ_{ζ_{0,1}} − δ_∞ (TB.1).
Substitute the definition µ_{f,v} = Δĝ_F + δ_{ζ_{0,1}} (DY.2/canonical-measure).

nodes.title: µ_{f,v} is a probability measure
nodes.statement: Setting: K is a complete nonarchimedean field (algebraically closed where stated, e.g. ℂ_v) with absolute value |·|; P^{1,an}_K = A^{1,an}_K ∪ {∞} is the Berkovich projective line of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0, whose points x ∈ A^{1,an}_K are multiplicative seminorms g ↦ [g]_x on K[T] extending |·|, with the weakest topology making every x ↦ [g]_x continuous; ℙ¹(K) ⊂ P^{1,an}_K is dense, ζ_{a,r} is the sup-norm of the closed disc D(a, r) and ζ_{0,1} is the Gauss point; a rational map f acts by its analytification f^{an} ([g]_{f^{an}(x)} = [g ∘ f]_x). The Laplacian Δ on P^{1,an}_K is the one of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.1, normalised as in DeMarco–Krieger–Ye: Δ log max([T], 1) = δ_{ζ_{0,1}} − δ_∞ (the negative of Baker–Rumely's). µ_{f,v} is a positive Borel measure of total mass 1 on P^{1,an}_K, and it gives no mass to type I points.
hypotheses: K complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean
proofSteps: Total mass: Δĝ_F has total mass 0 because ĝ_F is continuous on the compact space P^{1,an}_K (TB.1); so µ(P^{1,an}_K) = 1.

Positivity on A^{1,an}_K: λ̂^{an}_F is the uniform limit (DY.2/berkovich-lift-bounds) of u_n = d^{−n} log max([Fⁿ₀(T, 1)], [Fⁿ₁(T, 1)]), and each u_n is subharmonic on A^{1,an}_K (log [P] is subharmonic for P ∈ K[T] and a maximum of subharmonic functions is subharmonic, TB.1); uniform limits of subharmonic functions are subharmonic (TB.1), so µ|_{A^{1,an}} = Δλ̂^{an}_F|_{A^{1,an}} ≥ 0 (DY.2/laplacian-of-local-canonical-height).
Positivity at ∞: apply the previous step to the conjugate of f by z ↦ 1/z, whose canonical measure is the pull-back of µ_{f,v} (DY.2/canonical-measure-conjugation).
No mass on type I points: ĝ_F is a continuous potential (TB.1).
acceptance: For (z^p − z)/p the total mass of Haar measure on ℤ_p is 1.

nodes.title: Invariance f^*µ = d·µ and f_*µ = µ
nodes.statement: Setting: K is a complete nonarchimedean field (algebraically closed where stated, e.g. ℂ_v) with absolute value |·|; P^{1,an}_K = A^{1,an}_K ∪ {∞} is the Berkovich projective line of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0, whose points x ∈ A^{1,an}_K are multiplicative seminorms g ↦ [g]_x on K[T] extending |·|, with the weakest topology making every x ↦ [g]_x continuous; ℙ¹(K) ⊂ P^{1,an}_K is dense, ζ_{a,r} is the sup-norm of the closed disc D(a, r) and ζ_{0,1} is the Gauss point; a rational map f acts by its analytification f^{an} ([g]_{f^{an}(x)} = [g ∘ f]_x). The Laplacian Δ on P^{1,an}_K is the one of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.1, normalised as in DeMarco–Krieger–Ye: Δ log max([T], 1) = δ_{ζ_{0,1}} − δ_∞ (the negative of Baker–Rumely's). With f^* and f_* the pull-back and push-forward of Borel measures along f^{an} (with local degrees, TB.1): f^*µ_{f,v} = d·µ_{f,v} and f_*µ_{f,v} = µ_{f,v}.
hypotheses: K complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean
proofSteps: On A^{1,an}_K ∖ (f^{an})^{−1}(∞): λ̂^{an}_F ∘ f^{an} = d·λ̂^{an}_F − log [F₁(T, 1)] (DY.2/local-canonical-height-functional-equation, extended by continuity and density of type I points).
Apply Δ: Δ(h ∘ f^{an}) = f^*(Δh) (TB.1) and Poincaré–Lelong Δ log[F₁(T, 1)] = Σ_{F₁(a, 1) = 0} δ_a − (deg F₁(T, 1))·δ_∞ (TB.1).

f^*δ_∞ is the divisor of poles of f, Σ_{F₁(a,1)=0} δ_a + (d − deg F₁(T, 1))·δ_∞; combining, f^*µ − f^*δ_∞ = d·µ − d·δ_∞ − Σ δ_a + deg F₁(T,1)·δ_∞, i.e. f^*µ = d·µ (DY.2/laplacian-of-local-canonical-height).
f_* f^* = d·id on measures (TB.1) gives f_*µ = µ.
acceptance: For good reduction: f^*δ_{ζ_{0,1}} = d·δ_{ζ_{0,1}} (the Gauss point is totally invariant with local degree d).

nodes.title: µ_{f,v} = δ_{ζ_{0,1}} implies good reduction
nodes.statement: Setting: K is a complete nonarchimedean field (algebraically closed where stated, e.g. ℂ_v) with absolute value |·|; P^{1,an}_K = A^{1,an}_K ∪ {∞} is the Berkovich projective line of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0, whose points x ∈ A^{1,an}_K are multiplicative seminorms g ↦ [g]_x on K[T] extending |·|, with the weakest topology making every x ↦ [g]_x continuous; ℙ¹(K) ⊂ P^{1,an}_K is dense, ζ_{a,r} is the sup-norm of the closed disc D(a, r) and ζ_{0,1} is the Gauss point; a rational map f acts by its analytification f^{an} ([g]_{f^{an}(x)} = [g ∘ f]_x). The Laplacian Δ on P^{1,an}_K is the one of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.1, normalised as in DeMarco–Krieger–Ye: Δ log max([T], 1) = δ_{ζ_{0,1}} − δ_∞ (the negative of Baker–Rumely's). Let K be algebraically closed. If µ_{f,v} = δ_{ζ_{0,1}} then f has good reduction at v.
hypotheses: K complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean
proofSteps: Δĝ_F = µ − δ_{ζ_{0,1}} = 0, so ĝ_F is constant, = c (a continuous function with zero Laplacian on P^{1,an}_K is constant, TB.1). Hence G_{F,v} = log ‖·‖_v + c on K² ∖ {0}.

Normalise F (coefficients in 𝒪, one a unit). The residue field k is algebraically closed, hence infinite, and F̃ ≠ 0, so some ỹ ∈ k² has F̃(ỹ) ≠ 0 (Mathlib's MvPolynomial.funext); lift it to a primitive y with ‖F(y)‖ = 1.
DY.2/escape-rate-functional-equation at y: log ‖F(y)‖ + c = d·(log ‖y‖ + c), i.e. c = d·c, so c = 0 (d ≥ 2). Thus G_{F,v} = log ‖·‖_v and f has good reduction by DY.2/good-reduction-of-escape-rate.
acceptance: Contrapositive: (z² + 1)/(3z) over ℂ₃ has bad reduction, so µ ≠ δ_{ζ_{0,1}}.

nodes.title: Canonical measures of conjugate maps
nodes.statement: Setting: K is a complete nonarchimedean field (algebraically closed where stated, e.g. ℂ_v) with absolute value |·|; P^{1,an}_K = A^{1,an}_K ∪ {∞} is the Berkovich projective line of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0, whose points x ∈ A^{1,an}_K are multiplicative seminorms g ↦ [g]_x on K[T] extending |·|, with the weakest topology making every x ↦ [g]_x continuous; ℙ¹(K) ⊂ P^{1,an}_K is dense, ζ_{a,r} is the sup-norm of the closed disc D(a, r) and ζ_{0,1} is the Gauss point; a rational map f acts by its analytification f^{an} ([g]_{f^{an}(x)} = [g ∘ f]_x). The Laplacian Δ on P^{1,an}_K is the one of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.1, normalised as in DeMarco–Krieger–Ye: Δ log max([T], 1) = δ_{ζ_{0,1}} − δ_∞ (the negative of Baker–Rumely's). For φ ∈ PGL₂(K) (given by A ∈ GL₂(K)): µ_{φ⁻¹∘f∘φ, v} = (φ^{an})^*µ_{f,v} (the pull-back along the homeomorphism φ^{an}, i.e. the push-forward along (φ^{an})⁻¹).
hypotheses: K complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean
A ∈ GL₂(K)
proofSteps: G_{F^A,v}(x) = G_{F,v}(Ax) (DY.2/escape-rate-conjugation), so g_{F^A}([x]) = g_F([Ax]) + log(‖Ax‖/‖x‖) on ℙ¹(K), and by continuity ĝ_{F^A} = ĝ_F ∘ φ^{an} + ℓ_A, where ℓ_A is the continuous extension of [x] ↦ log(‖Ax‖/‖x‖).

nodes.title: Potential good reduction ⟺ µ_{f,v} is a point mass at a type II point
nodes.statement: Setting: K is a complete nonarchimedean field (algebraically closed where stated, e.g. ℂ_v) with absolute value |·|; P^{1,an}_K = A^{1,an}_K ∪ {∞} is the Berkovich projective line of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.0, whose points x ∈ A^{1,an}_K are multiplicative seminorms g ↦ [g]_x on K[T] extending |·|, with the weakest topology making every x ↦ [g]_x continuous; ℙ¹(K) ⊂ P^{1,an}_K is dense, ζ_{a,r} is the sup-norm of the closed disc D(a, r) and ζ_{0,1} is the Gauss point; a rational map f acts by its analytification f^{an} ([g]_{f^{an}(x)} = [g ∘ f]_x). The Laplacian Δ on P^{1,an}_K is the one of TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic:TB.1, normalised as in DeMarco–Krieger–Ye: Δ log max([T], 1) = δ_{ζ_{0,1}} − δ_∞ (the negative of Baker–Rumely's). Let K be algebraically closed. f has potentially good reduction at v (some φ⁻¹ ∘ f ∘ φ, φ ∈ PGL₂(K), has good reduction) if and only if µ_{f,v} = δ_ξ for a type II point ξ ∈ P^{1,an}_K; in that case φ can be any Möbius map with φ^{an}(ζ_{0,1}) = ξ.
hypotheses: K complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean
proofSteps: (⟹) If f^φ = φ⁻¹∘f∘φ has good reduction, µ_{f^φ} = δ_{ζ_{0,1}} (DY.2/canonical-measure-of-good-reduction), so by DY.2/canonical-measure-conjugation µ_f = δ_{φ^{an}(ζ_{0,1})}, and φ^{an} maps type II points to type II points (TB.1).

(⟸) PGL₂(K) acts transitively on type II points (TB.1); choose φ with φ^{an}(ζ_{0,1}) = ξ. Then µ_{f^φ} = (φ^{an})^*δ_ξ = δ_{ζ_{0,1}}, and f^φ has good reduction by DY.2/good-reduction-of-canonical-measure.

nodes.title: The canonical measure at an archimedean place
nodes.statement: Let f be a rational map of degree d ≥ 2 over ℂ with lift F, and g_F = dynamical-green-function at the usual absolute value, a continuous function on the Riemann sphere ℙ¹(ℂ) = OnePoint ℂ (= P^{1,an}_ℂ). With Δ the measure-valued Laplacian on ℙ¹(ℂ) normalised as dd^c (Δ log|z| = δ₀ on ℂ, so Δ log⁺|z| = ω − δ_∞ with ω the normalised arc length on the unit circle), the archimedean canonical measure is µ_{f,∞} = Δg_F + ω. Equivalently Δλ̂_{F,∞} = µ_{f,∞} − δ_∞, and on ℂ µ_{f,∞} = (1/2π)·Δ_eucl(G_F(z, 1)) in the sense of distributions. For v an archimedean place of a number field K one uses the embedding K → ℂ of v.
proofSteps: g_F is continuous on ℙ¹(ℂ) (DY.2/escape-rate-continuous), and on ℂ the function G_F(z, 1) is the uniform limit of the subharmonic functions d^{−n} log max(|Fⁿ₀(z, 1)|, |Fⁿ₁(z, 1)|) (DY.2/escape-rate-tendsto); its distributional Laplacian is therefore a measure. The measure-valued Laplacian of continuous functions on the Riemann sphere is not in the libraries and is recorded as a gap of this layer.
Define µ_{f,∞} = Δg_F + ω; it does not depend on the lift, since g_{cF} − g_F is constant.

nodes.title: The archimedean canonical measure: mass, invariance, no atoms
nodes.statement: For f of degree d ≥ 2 over ℂ: µ_{f,∞} is a Borel probability measure on ℙ¹(ℂ) without atoms, Δλ̂_{F,∞} = µ_{f,∞} − δ_∞, and f^*µ_{f,∞} = d·µ_{f,∞}, f_*µ_{f,∞} = µ_{f,∞}.
proofSteps: Total mass 1: the Laplacian of a continuous function on the compact Riemann sphere has total mass 0.
Positivity: on ℂ, λ̂_{F,∞} = G_F(·, 1) is a uniform limit of subharmonic functions, hence subharmonic; near ∞ use the chart 1/z (DY.2/escape-rate-conjugation).
No atoms: a measure with a continuous potential has no atoms (Riesz decomposition).

Invariance: apply Δ to the functional equation of DY.2/local-canonical-height-functional-equation, with Δ(h ∘ f) = f^*Δh and Δ log|F₁(z, 1)| = Σ δ_{zeros} − deg·δ_∞, exactly as in DY.2/canonical-measure-invariance; then f_* f^* = d.

nodes.title: µ_{f,∞} is Lyubich's measure of maximal entropy
nodes.statement: For f of degree d ≥ 2 over ℂ, µ_{f,∞} equals the Lyubich / Freire–Lopes–Mañé measure: it is the unique Borel probability measure on ℙ¹(ℂ) without atoms with f^*µ = d·µ; for every non-exceptional a ∈ ℙ¹(ℂ), d^{−n}·Σ_{fⁿ(z) = a} δ_z → µ_{f,∞} weakly (with multiplicity); and µ_{f,∞} is the unique f-invariant measure of maximal entropy log d (Lyubich; Mañé). For the Lattès maps of DY.6 it is the push-forward of Haar measure of the elliptic curve.
proofSteps: By DY.2/archimedean-canonical-measure-properties µ_{f,∞} has no atoms and f^*µ = d·µ.

The uniqueness of such a measure, the equidistribution of preimages and the entropy characterisation are the theorems of Lyubich (1983), Freire–Lopes–Mañé (1983) and Mañé (1983) (Baker–Rumely Theorem 2.1); they belong to the complex dynamics of rational maps, which no roadmap of the atlas plans, and are recorded as a gap of this layer. Given them, µ_{f,∞} is Lyubich's measure (Baker–Rumely Proposition 3.36(B)).

nodes.title: Worked example: z² − z − 1, a polynomial with good reduction everywhere
nodes.statement: Let f(z) = z² − z − 1 over ℚ with lift F = (X₀² − X₀X₁ − X₁², X₁²). Then: (a) Res(F) = 1, so f has good reduction at every prime p; G_{F,p} = log ‖·‖_p, λ̂_{F,p} = log⁺|·|_p and µ_{f,p} = δ_{ζ_{0,1}} for every p. (b) The points ±1 form a 2-cycle with multiplier λ₂ = f′(1)f′(−1) = −3, and G_{F,∞}(±1, 1) = 0, so every local canonical height of ±1 vanishes and ĥ_f(±1) = 0. (c) Modulo 2 the cycle reduces to the fixed point 1 of f̃ = z² + z + 1 over 𝔽₂, with reduced multiplier 1 = (−3)~: m = 1, r = 1 and n = 2 = m·r·p, the p-power case of DY.2/periods-under-good-reduction (e = 1, within Hutz's bound e ≤ 3 and Zieve's e ≤ 1 over ℚ₂). (d) Modulo 3 the cycle reduces to the 2-cycle {1, 2} of z² + 2z + 2 over 𝔽₃ (m = n = 2), and its multiplier reduces to (−3)~ = 0: the reduced cycle is superattracting although the cycle upstairs is repelling at ∞. (e) The fixed points 1 ± √2 have multipliers 1 ± 2√2; in ℚ₇ (√2 ≡ 3 mod 7) they reduce to the fixed points 4, 5 of f̃ over 𝔽₇, whose multipliers 0, 2 are the residues of 1 ± 2√2. (f) Holomorphic fixed-point formula: 1/(1 − 0) + 1/(1 − (1 + 2√2)) + 1/(1 − (1 − 2√2)) = 1 (∞ has multiplier 0).
hypotheses: f(z) = z² − z − 1 over ℚ
proofSteps: Res(F) = F₀(1, 0)² = 1 because F₁ = X₁² has the double root [1 : 0] (DY.0/resultant-of-a-rational-map); apply DY.2/escape-rate-of-good-reduction, DY.2/local-canonical-height-weil-bound and DY.2/canonical-measure-of-good-reduction.

f(1) = −1, f(−1) = 1; multipliers by DY.2/multiplier-chain-rule. At ∞: ‖Fⁿ(z, 1)‖_∞ ≥ |Fⁿ₁(z, 1)| = 1 gives G_{F,∞}(z, 1) ≥ 0, and the bounded orbit gives G_{F,∞}(±1, 1) ≤ 0 (DY.2/escape-rate-nonpos-iff-bounded-orbit); sum with DY.2/local-decomposition-of-canonical-height.
Reduction mod 2: f̃ = z² + z + 1, f̃(1) = 1, f̃′(1) = 2·1 + 1 = 1 in 𝔽₂ (DY.2/multiplier-reduction; λ̃₂ = f̃′(1)² = 1 ≡ −3).
Mod 7: 3² ≡ 2, fixed points 1 + 3 = 4 and 1 − 3 ≡ 5, f̃′ = 2z − 1 gives 7 ≡ 0 and 9 ≡ 2.
Formula (f): direct computation with the multipliers of (a)–(e) (Benedetto's Theorem 1.6).
acceptance: Every clause (a)–(f) is a finite computation.

nodes.title: Worked example: (z^p − z)/p, bad reduction with Haar canonical measure
nodes.statement: Let p be prime and f(z) = (z^p − z)/p over ℚ_p, with normalised lift F = (X₀^p − X₀X₁^{p−1}, pX₁^p). Then: (a) Res(F) = p^p (e.g. 4 for p = 2, 27 for p = 3), so f has bad reduction at p; the fixed point 0 has multiplier −1/p and the fixed points with z^{p−1} = 1 + p have multiplier p + 1 − 1/p, all of absolute value p > 1, so f has no potentially good reduction at p. (b) G_{F,p}(z, 1) = λ̂_{F,p}(z) = −(log p)/(p − 1) for z ∈ ℤ_p and = log|z|_p for |z|_p > 1; the filled Julia set of f in ℂ_p is ℤ_p. (c) λ̂_{F,p}(z) = ∫_{ℤ_p} log|z − y|_p dH(y) for all z ∈ ℂ_p, with H the Haar probability measure of ℤ_p, and λ̂^{an}_F(ζ_{0,1}) = 0. (d) µ_{f,p} = H, viewed on ℤ_p ⊂ ℙ¹(ℂ_p) ⊂ P^{1,an}_{ℂ_p}; in particular µ_{f,p} is not a point mass (DY.2/potential-good-reduction-iff-point-mass).
hypotheses: p prime
K = ℚ_p, computations over ℂ_p
proofSteps: (a) Res(F) by the Sylvester determinant (DY.0/resultant-of-a-rational-map); the multipliers by DY.0/fixed-point-multiplier (f′(z) = (p z^{p−1} − 1)/p); DY.2/good-reduction-multipliers-integral excludes potential good reduction.

(b) For z ∈ ℤ_p, z^p ≡ z mod p, so f(ℤ_p) ⊆ ℤ_p; Fⁿ₁(z, 1) = p^{(pⁿ−1)/(p−1)} and Fⁿ₀(z, 1) = fⁿ(z)·Fⁿ₁(z, 1), so ‖Fⁿ(z, 1)‖_p = p^{−(pⁿ−1)/(p−1)} and G = −(log p)/(p − 1). For |x₀| > |x₁| one has ‖F(x)‖ = ‖x‖^p and again |F₀(x)| > |F₁(x)|, so G(z, 1) = log|z|_p. Points of ℂ_p ∖ ℤ_p have unbounded orbits (Benedetto, Example 4.40), so G > 0 there (DY.2/escape-rate-nonpos-iff-bounded-orbit).

(c) Put u(z) = ∫ log|z − y| dH(y). Then u = −(log p)/(p − 1) on ℤ_p (the H-measure of {|y − z| = p^{−k}} is p^{−k}(1 − 1/p)) and u = log|z| for |z| > 1, so u − log⁺|·| is bounded. For w ∈ ℤ_p, f(z) − w = (1/p)·∏_{f(y) = w}(z − y) with the p preimages in ℤ_p (Hensel), and f^*H = p·H (f maps each disc y + p^kℤ_p, k ≥ 1, bijectively onto f(y) + p^{k−1}ℤ_p); hence u(f(z)) = p·u(z) + log p = p·u(z) − log|F₁(z, 1)|_p, the functional equation of λ̂ (DY.2/local-canonical-height-functional-equation). Since f is a polynomial every orbit in ℂ_p avoids ∞, and DY.2/green-function-uniqueness gives u = λ̂. At the Gauss point every Fⁿ₀(T, 1) has Gauss norm 1, so λ̂^{an}(ζ_{0,1}) = 0 = ∫ log max(1, |y|) dH(y).
(d) By continuity (DY.2/berkovich-escape-potential, TB.1) λ̂^{an}_F(x) = ∫ log[T − y]_x dH(y) on A^{1,an}, whose Laplacian is H − δ_∞ (TB.1); by DY.2/laplacian-of-local-canonical-height µ_{f,p} = H.
acceptance: For p = 2: f(z) = (z² − z)/2, Res(F) = 4, G_{F,2}(0, 1) = −log 2 and µ = Haar on ℤ₂.

nodes.title: Worked example: (z² + 1)/(3z), the algebraic-closure hypothesis is needed
nodes.statement: Let f(z) = (z² + 1)/(3z) over ℚ with lift F = (X₀² + X₁², 3X₀X₁). Then: (a) Res(F) = 9, so f has good reduction at every p ≠ 3 and bad reduction at 3. (b) Over ℚ₃: ‖F(x)‖₃ = ‖x‖₃² for all x ∈ ℚ₃², so G_{F,3} = log ‖·‖₃ on ℚ₃² and g_{F,3} = 0 on ℙ¹(ℚ₃) although f has bad reduction; over ℂ₃, G_{F,3}(i, 1) = −(1/2)·log 3 < 0 = log ‖(i, 1)‖₃. So DY.2/good-reduction-of-escape-rate fails without an algebraically closed residue field. (c) The fixed points are ∞ (multiplier 3) and ±1/√2 (multiplier −1/3); |−1/3|₃ = 3 > 1, so f has no potentially good reduction at 3 and µ_{f,3} is not a point mass. (d) Reduction does not commute with f at 3: i and i + 3 have the same reduction in ℙ¹(𝔽̄₃) but f(i) = 0 and f(i + 3) = (2i + 3)/(i + 3) reduce to 0 and 2. (e) At p = 2 (good reduction, f̃(z) = z + 1/z over 𝔽₂): the three fixed points ∞, ±1/√2 all reduce to ∞ (|±1/√2|₂ = √2 > 1), the triple fixed point of f̃, and their multipliers 3, −1/3, −1/3 all reduce to 1, the multiplier of ∞ for f̃. (f) Holomorphic fixed-point formula: 1/(1 − 3) + 2/(1 + 1/3) = 1.
hypotheses: f(z) = (z² + 1)/(3z) over ℚ
proofSteps: (a) Res(F) = F₁(i, 1)·F₁(−i, 1) = (3i)(−3i) = 9 (Sylvester determinant, DY.0/resultant-of-a-rational-map).

(b) For x ∈ ℚ₃² primitive, x₀² + x₁² ≢ 0 mod 3 because −1 is not a square mod 3, so ‖F(x)‖₃ = 1 = ‖x‖₃²; iterate (F(x) is again primitive) to get G = log ‖·‖ (DY.2/escape-rate). Over ℂ₃: F(i, 1) = (0, 3i), F(0, 3i) = (−9, 0), and (1, 0) is fixed up to squaring of the scalar, so ‖Fⁿ(i, 1)‖₃ = 3^{−2^{n−1}} for n ≥ 1 and G(i, 1) = −(1/2)·log 3.

(c) Multipliers by DY.2/multiplier-of-a-periodic-cycle (at ∞: tr DF(1, 0) − 2 = 5 − 2 = 3) and DY.0/fixed-point-multiplier (f′ = (z² − 1)/(3z²) = −1/3 at z² = 1/2); conclude with DY.2/good-reduction-multipliers-integral and DY.2/potential-good-reduction-iff-point-mass.

nodes.title: The order of a binary form at a point of ℙ¹
nodes.statement: Let K be a field, F ∈ K[X, Y] a binary form and P = [a : b] ∈ ℙ¹(K), given by a nonzero vector (a, b). The order of F at P is ord_P F := the largest k ≥ 0 with (bX − aY)^k ∣ F in K[X, Y], i.e. Mathlib's multiplicity of the linear form ℓ_P = bX − aY in F (with Mathlib's junk value when F = 0). It depends only on the point: replacing (a, b) by (ca, cb), c ≠ 0, multiplies ℓ_P by the unit c. For F ≠ 0 homogeneous of degree D, ord_[a:1] F is the root multiplicity of a in the dehomogenisation F(X, 1), and ord_[1:0] F = D − deg F(X, 1). Points over an extension L of K are treated by mapping F to L[X, Y].
hypotheses: K is any field; F ∈ K[X, Y] = MvPolynomial (Fin 2) K with X = X 0, Y = X 1.
The order is used only for F ≠ 0 and P ≠ 0; no algebraic closedness is assumed in the definition.
proofSteps: Define ord_P F := multiplicity(ℓ_P, F) with ℓ_P = P₁·X − P₀·Y (mathlib:multiplicity).

ℓ_P has degree one, hence is irreducible and prime in the unique factorisation domain K[X, Y] (instance inference: MvPolynomial over a field is a unique factorisation monoid), so ord_P(F·G) = ord_P F + ord_P G for F, G ≠ 0.
Scaling P by c ≠ 0 scales ℓ_P by c, which does not change the multiplicity.

Dehomogenisation: for P = [a : 1] and F homogeneous of degree D, F = (X − aY)^k·H with H(a, 1) ≠ 0 if and only if F(X, 1) = (X − a)^k·H(X, 1) with H(a, 1) ≠ 0; hence ord_[a:1] F = rootMultiplicity a (F(X, 1)) (mathlib:MvPolynomial.aeval, mathlib:Polynomial.rootMultiplicity). At ∞ the power of Y dividing F is D − deg F(X, 1) (mathlib:MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous).

nodes.title: Divisibility of binary forms is decided by their orders on ℙ¹
nodes.statement: (a) Let K be algebraically closed and F, G ∈ K[X, Y] nonzero binary forms. Then F ∣ G in K[X, Y] if and only if ord_P F ≤ ord_P G for every P ∈ ℙ¹(K); in particular F = c·∏_P ℓ_P^{ord_P F} with c ∈ K^× and Σ_P ord_P F = deg F. (b) For any field extension L/K and F, G ∈ K[X, Y], if F ∣ G in L[X, Y] then F ∣ G in K[X, Y].
hypotheses: (a) needs K algebraically closed; (b) holds for every field extension.
F, G are homogeneous and nonzero in (a).
proofSteps: Write f = F(X, 1), g = G(X, 1). For F homogeneous of degree a, F = Y^{a − deg f}·Y^{deg f} f(X/Y), so F ∣ G iff a − deg f ≤ b − deg g and f ∣ g in K[X].

By mathlib:IsAlgClosed.dvd_iff_roots_le_roots, f ∣ g iff roots f ≤ roots g, i.e. rootMultiplicity x f ≤ rootMultiplicity x g for all x (mathlib:Polynomial.count_roots); by the affine API of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/binary-form-order-at-a-point these are ord_[x:1] F ≤ ord_[x:1] G, and a − deg f = ord_∞ F.
The factorisation and Σ_P ord_P F = deg F follow from the splitting of f (mathlib:IsAlgClosed.card_roots_eq_natDegree) together with the power of Y.

(b): K[X, Y] → L[X, Y] (mathlib:MvPolynomial.map) is injective and L[X, Y] = L ⊗_K K[X, Y] is free over K[X, Y] on a K-basis of L containing 1. If G = F·H with H ∈ L[X, Y], expanding H in that basis and comparing the coefficient of 1 gives G = F·H₁ with H₁ ∈ K[X, Y].
acceptance: Over ℚ̄: X² + XY + Y²/4 ∣ X³ + (3/2)X²Y + (3/4)XY² + Y³/8 since both are powers of X + Y/2; X ∤ Y.

nodes.title: The n-th period polynomial Φₙ(φ) = Y·Fₙ − X·Gₙ
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and φ = (F, G) a pair of forms in R[X, Y] (a lift of a self-map of ℙ¹). The composite lift of φⁿ is (F₀, G₀) = (X, Y) and (F_{n+1}, G_{n+1}) = (F(Fₙ, Gₙ), G(Fₙ, Gₙ)). The n-th period form is Φₙ(φ) := Y·Fₙ(X, Y) − X·Gₙ(X, Y) ∈ R[X, Y]. If F, G are homogeneous of degree d then Φₙ is homogeneous of degree dⁿ + 1; Φ₀ = 0; replacing the lift by (uF, uG), u ∈ R^×, multiplies Φₙ by u^{1 + d + ⋯ + d^{n−1}}. For a polynomial map f of degree d with lift (Y^d f(X/Y), Y^d), Φₙ(X, 1) = fⁿ(X) − X.
hypotheses: R is any commutative ring; convention X = X 0, Y = X 1, and the sign Y·Fₙ − X·Gₙ of Morton–Silverman (21).
The lift, not only the rational map, is part of the data: the forms of φⁿ are the composite ones.
proofSteps: The composite lift is DY.0's iterate of the rational map (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); define Φₙ := Y·Fₙ − X·Gₙ.

Homogeneity: Fₙ, Gₙ are homogeneous of degree dⁿ by induction, since substituting forms of degree dⁿ into forms of degree d gives forms of degree d^{n+1} (mathlib:MvPolynomial.IsHomogeneous); hence Φₙ is homogeneous of degree dⁿ + 1.
Φ₀ = Y·X − X·Y = 0. Scaling: (uF, uG) has composite lift u^{1+d+⋯+d^{n−1}}(Fₙ, Gₙ) by induction.
For a polynomial map: Fₙ = Y^{dⁿ} fⁿ(X/Y) and Gₙ = Y^{dⁿ} by induction, so Φₙ(X, 1) = fⁿ(X) − X (mathlib:Polynomial.iterate_comp_eval).
acceptance: For z ↦ z² with lift (X², Y²): Φ₁ = X²Y − XY² = XY(X − Y), whose zeros are 0, 1 and ∞, the three fixed points.

nodes.title: The zeros of Φₙ are the points of period n
nodes.statement: Let φ be a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d ≥ 1 over a field K, inducing f : ℙ¹(K) → ℙ¹(K). For n ≥ 0 and P = [v] ∈ ℙ¹(K): Φₙ(φ)(v) = 0 if and only if fⁿ(P) = P.
hypotheses: K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio.
proofSteps: The composite lift of a morphism has no common zero: (Fₙ(v), Gₙ(v)) ≠ 0 for v ≠ 0 (induction, DY.0's iterate of a morphism), and fⁿ([v]) = [Fₙ(v) : Gₙ(v)].
Φₙ(v) = v₁Fₙ(v) − v₀Gₙ(v) is minus the determinant of the vectors v and (Fₙ(v), Gₙ(v)); it vanishes iff they are proportional, i.e. iff [Fₙ(v) : Gₙ(v)] = [v₀ : v₁] (mathlib:Projectivization.mk).

nodes.title: The period form under conjugation by GL₂
nodes.statement: Let φ be a lift over a field K and A ∈ GL₂(K). Let lin = A·(X, Y)ᵀ and let ψ = A⁻¹ ∘ φ ∘ A be the conjugate lift, ψᵢ = Σⱼ (A⁻¹)ᵢⱼ φⱼ(lin). Then for every n, Φₙ(ψ) = det(A)⁻¹·Φₙ(φ)(lin); consequently ord_P Φₙ(ψ) = ord_{AP} Φₙ(φ), i.e. a_P(ψ, n) = a_{AP}(φ, n) and a*_P(ψ, n) = a*_{AP}(φ, n).
hypotheses: A is invertible; ψ is the lift of the conjugate map α⁻¹ ∘ f ∘ α of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/conjugacy-of-rational-maps.
proofSteps: The composite lift of ψ is A⁻¹ ∘ (lift of φⁿ) ∘ A: the inner A⁻¹ and A cancel between consecutive factors.
For a vector v: Φ(ψ)(v) = −det(v, A⁻¹w) with w = φⁿ(Av), and det(v, A⁻¹w) = det(A)⁻¹det(Av, w), so Φₙ(ψ)(v) = det(A)⁻¹Φₙ(φ)(Av).

The substitution v ↦ Av is a graded automorphism of K[X, Y] with ℓ_{AP}(Av) = det(A)·ℓ_P(v), so multiplicities of ℓ_{AP} in Φₙ(φ) and of ℓ_P in Φₙ(φ)(lin) agree (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/binary-form-order-at-a-point).
The statement for a* follows by summing with Möbius weights.
acceptance: Conjugating z² by z ↦ z + 1 moves the fixed point 0 to −1 and a_{−1}(ψ, 1) = a_0(z², 1) = 1.

nodes.title: The multiplicity a_P(n) of a point of period n
nodes.statement: For a lift φ of a morphism of ℙ¹ over a field K, n ≥ 1 and P ∈ ℙ¹(K), the multiplicity of P as a point of period n is a_P(n) = a_P(φ, n) := ord_P Φₙ(φ). It is positive exactly when φⁿ(P) = P; Σ_{P ∈ ℙ¹(K̄)} a_P(n) = dⁿ + 1 for d ≥ 2; a_P(φ, mk) = a_P(φᵐ, k); it is invariant under conjugation (a_P(ψ, n) = a_{AP}(φ, n)). On ℙ¹ it equals Morton–Silverman's intersection multiplicity (Δ·Γ(φⁿ))_{(P,P)}, whose cycle they identify with the root cycle of (21).
hypotheses: K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio.
Points over an extension L are handled by base change of φ to L (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form-base-change).
proofSteps: Define a_P(n) := ord_P Φₙ(φ) (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/binary-form-order-at-a-point).
Positivity: ord_P Φₙ > 0 iff Φₙ(P) = 0 iff φⁿ(P) = P (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form-zero-locus).
Total count over K̄: Φₙ is a nonzero form of degree dⁿ + 1 (API of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form), so Σ_P ord_P Φₙ = dⁿ + 1 (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/binary-form-divisibility-criterion).
Iterates and conjugation: ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form-of-an-iterate and ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form-conjugation.

nodes.title: The essential (dynatomic) multiplicity a*_P(n)
nodes.statement: For a lift φ over a field K, n ≥ 1 and P ∈ ℙ¹(K), a*_P(n) := Σ_{d ∣ n} μ(n/d)·a_P(d) ∈ ℤ, the coefficient of P in the n-th dynatomic cycle Z*ₙ(φ) = Σ_{d∣n} μ(n/d) Z_d(φ). By Möbius inversion a_P(n) = Σ_{d∣n} a*_P(d); a*_P(1) = a_P(1); if P has exact period n then a*_P(n) = a_P(n).
hypotheses: K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio.
μ is Mathlib's ArithmeticFunction.moebius; the sum runs over Nat.divisorsAntidiagonal n.
proofSteps: Define a*_P(n) := Σ_{(i, j) ∈ divisorsAntidiagonal n} μ(i)·a_P(j) (mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.moebius, mathlib:Nat.divisorsAntidiagonal).
Möbius inversion a_P(n) = Σ_{d∣n} a*_P(d): mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.sum_eq_iff_sum_mul_moebius_eq.
If P has exact period n, then a_P(d) = 0 for d ∣ n, d < n (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/multiplicity-of-a-periodic-point), so a*_P(n) = a_P(n).

nodes.title: The formal germ of a map at a fixed point
nodes.statement: For a lift φ = (F, G) over a field K with F(0, 1) = 0 ≠ G(0, 1) (the point 0 = [0 : 1] is fixed), the germ of φ at 0 is g_φ := F(z, 1)·G(z, 1)⁻¹ ∈ K[[z]], a power series with constant coefficient 0 (G(z, 1) is a unit of K[[z]]). Its linear coefficient is the multiplier λ = φ′(0) of the fixed point (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.2/multiplier-of-a-periodic-cycle). For a germ g with constant coefficient 0, gⁿ denotes the n-fold substitution iterate (g⁰ = z, g^{n+1} = g ∘ gⁿ, Mathlib's PowerSeries.subst). A general fixed point P ∈ ℙ¹(K) is moved to 0 by a conjugation (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form-conjugation), which leaves the multiplier unchanged.
hypotheses: K is a field; F(0, 1) = 0 and G(0, 1) ≠ 0 (for a morphism lift, F(0,1) = 0 already forces G(0,1) ≠ 0).
The junk value of Mathlib's power-series inverse is irrelevant because G(0, 1) ≠ 0.
proofSteps: Dehomogenise: F(z, 1), G(z, 1) ∈ K[z] (mathlib:MvPolynomial.aeval), viewed in K[[z]] (mathlib:Polynomial.coeToPowerSeries.ringHom); G(z, 1) has nonzero constant term so is invertible.
g_φ := F(z, 1)·G(z, 1)⁻¹; its constant coefficient is F(0,1)/G(0,1) = 0.
Iteration uses mathlib:PowerSeries.subst, legitimate since the substituted series has constant coefficient 0 (mathlib:PowerSeries.HasSubst.of_constantCoeff_zero').
The coefficient of z in gⁿ is λⁿ (chain rule for substitution: the linear coefficient of g ∘ h is the product of those of g and h, mathlib:PowerSeries.coeff).
Conjugating by z ↦ uz (u ≠ 0) replaces g(z) by u⁻¹g(uz), leaving the linear coefficient unchanged; this is the compatibility with DY.2's conjugation-invariant multiplier.
acceptance: For z² − z: g = −z + z², multiplier −1.

sources.excerpt: (7) z∘φ = z + z^e g for some g ∈ O_P with g(P) ≠ 0.

nodes.title: The germ of φⁿ is the n-th iterate of the germ
nodes.statement: Let φ = (F, G) be a lift over a field K with F(0, 1) = 0 ≠ G(0, 1). Then for every n the composite lift of φⁿ fixes [0 : 1] with Gₙ(0, 1) ≠ 0, and its germ is the n-fold substitution iterate of the germ of φ: g_{φⁿ} = (g_φ)ⁿ.
hypotheses: K a field; F(0, 1) = 0 and G(0, 1) ≠ 0.
proofSteps: Induction on n. By homogeneity Fₙ₊₁(z, 1) = F(Fₙ(z, 1), Gₙ(z, 1)) = Gₙ(z, 1)^d·F(gₙ, 1) where gₙ = Fₙ(z, 1)/Gₙ(z, 1), and likewise for G; hence Gₙ₊₁(0, 1) = Gₙ(0,1)^d G(0, 1) ≠ 0 and g_{φⁿ⁺¹} = F(gₙ, 1)/G(gₙ, 1).

Substitution of gₙ (constant coefficient 0, mathlib:PowerSeries.HasSubst.of_constantCoeff_zero') is a K-algebra homomorphism K[[z]] → K[[z]] (mathlib:PowerSeries.substAlgHom), so it commutes with polynomial evaluation and with inverses of units: F(gₙ, 1)/G(gₙ, 1) = (F(z,1)/G(z,1)) ∘ gₙ = g_φ ∘ gₙ = g_φ^{n+1}.
The dehomogenised forms and germs are those of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/fixed-point-germ and the lift iterates those of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form.
acceptance: For z² − z: the germ of the second iterate is (−z + z²) ∘ (−z + z²) = z − 2z³ + z⁴.

nodes.title: At a fixed point a_P(n) is the order of gⁿ(z) − z
nodes.statement: Let φ be a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d ≥ 2 over a field K fixing 0 = [0 : 1], with germ g. Then for every n ≥ 1, a_{[0:1]}(φ, n) = ord_z(gⁿ(z) − z) (Mathlib's PowerSeries.order, finite since φⁿ ≠ id).
hypotheses: K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio.
F(0, 1) = 0 (the point [0 : 1] is fixed).
proofSteps: By ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/germ-of-an-iterate, Fₙ(z, 1) = Gₙ(z, 1)·gⁿ(z) in K[[z]], so Φₙ(z, 1) = Fₙ(z, 1) − z·Gₙ(z, 1) = Gₙ(z, 1)·(gⁿ(z) − z).
Gₙ(z, 1) is a unit of K[[z]] (Gₙ(0, 1) ≠ 0), so ord_z Φₙ(z, 1) = ord_z(gⁿ − z) (mathlib:PowerSeries.order_mul).

For a polynomial, the power-series order at 0 is the root multiplicity at 0 (mathlib:Polynomial.rootMultiplicity), and ord_[0:1] Φₙ = rootMultiplicity 0 (Φₙ(z, 1)) by the affine API of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/binary-form-order-at-a-point.
The order is finite because Φₙ ≠ 0 (API periodForm_ne_zero of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form).

nodes.title: Simple fixed points of iterates: ord(gⁿ − z) = 1 iff λⁿ ≠ 1
nodes.statement: Let g ∈ K[[z]] have constant coefficient 0 and linear coefficient λ. For every n ≥ 1, ord(gⁿ(z) − z) = 1 if and only if λⁿ ≠ 1; otherwise ord(gⁿ − z) ≥ 2. In particular a_P(φ, m) ≥ 2 iff the multiplier (φᵐ)′(P) = 1.
hypotheses: K is a field and g ∈ K[[z]] has constant coefficient 0; gⁿ is the n-fold substitution iterate (germIterate).
proofSteps: gⁿ has constant coefficient 0 and linear coefficient λⁿ (API coeff_one_germIterate of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/fixed-point-germ), so gⁿ − z has constant coefficient 0 and linear coefficient λⁿ − 1.
Hence ord(gⁿ − z) ≥ 1, with equality iff λⁿ − 1 ≠ 0 (mathlib:PowerSeries.order, mathlib:PowerSeries.coeff).

nodes.title: ord(gⁿ − z) ≥ ord(g − z)
nodes.statement: Let g ∈ K[[z]] have constant coefficient 0. For every n ≥ 1, ord(gⁿ − z) ≥ ord(g − z). Consequently a_P(φ, kn) ≥ a_P(φ, k) for all k, n ≥ 1 at a point P of period k.
hypotheses: K is a field and g ∈ K[[z]] has constant coefficient 0; gⁿ is the n-fold substitution iterate (germIterate).
proofSteps: Let e = ord(g − z), so g = z + O(z^e). If h = z + O(z^e) then g ∘ h = h + (g − z) ∘ h = h + O(h^e) = z + O(z^e), since h has order ≥ 1 (mathlib:PowerSeries.subst).
By induction gⁿ = z + O(z^e), i.e. ord(gⁿ − z) ≥ e.
For the corollary apply this to the germ of φᵏ at P (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/multiplicity-equals-germ-order, ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/germ-of-an-iterate).

nodes.title: Iterates of a germ tangent to the identity
nodes.statement: Let g ∈ K[[z]] with g = z + z^e·u, e ≥ 2, u(0) ≠ 0 (so ord(g − z) = e). Then gⁿ = z + n·z^e·u + O(z^{2e−1}); hence ord(gⁿ − z) = e when n ≠ 0 in K, and ord(gⁿ − z) ≥ 2e − 1 when n = 0 in K (n ≥ 1).
hypotheses: K is a field and g ∈ K[[z]] has constant coefficient 0; gⁿ is the n-fold substitution iterate (germIterate).
e ≥ 2 (g is tangent to the identity); n ≥ 1.
proofSteps: For every power series h with constant coefficient 0 and any i, h ∘ gⁱ = h + O(z^e) (from ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/germ-order-monotone): this is Morton–Silverman's (8).
Induction: z∘g^{n} = z + z^e Σ_{i<n} u∘gⁱ + O(z^{2e−1}) (their (9)): g^{n+1} = g ∘ gⁿ = gⁿ + (gⁿ)^e·u(gⁿ) and (gⁿ)^e = z^e(1 + O(z^{e−1}))^e = z^e + O(z^{2e−1}).
Substituting (8) into (9): gⁿ = z + n z^e u + O(z^{2e−1}) (their (10)). Since u(0) ≠ 0 and 2e − 1 > e, ord(gⁿ − z) = e if n·u(0) ≠ 0, i.e. n ≠ 0 in K, and ≥ 2e − 1 if n = 0 in K.

nodes.title: Rotation germs: r ∣ ord(gʳ − z) − 1
nodes.statement: Let g ∈ K[[z]] have constant coefficient 0 and linear coefficient λ a primitive r-th root of unity with r ≥ 2, and suppose gʳ ≠ z. Then s := ord(gʳ − z) satisfies r ∣ s − 1; in particular s ≥ r + 1 ≥ 3.
hypotheses: K is a field and g ∈ K[[z]] has constant coefficient 0; gⁿ is the n-fold substitution iterate (germIterate).
λ is a primitive r-th root of unity, r ≥ 2 (so the characteristic of K does not divide r); gʳ ≠ z.
proofSteps: h := gʳ has linear coefficient λʳ = 1 (API coeff_one_germIterate), so h = z + c·z^s + O(z^{s+1}) with c ≠ 0 and s ≥ 2 (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/germ-order-multiplier-criterion).
h ∘ g = g ∘ h since both are g^{r+1} (mathlib:PowerSeries.subst is associative on series with zero constant term).
g ∘ h = g(z + c z^s + O(z^{s+1})) = g(z) + g′(z)·c z^s + O(z^{2s}) = g(z) + λ c z^s + O(z^{s+1}) (Taylor expansion of the substitution; s ≥ 2).
h ∘ g = g + c·g^s + O(g^{s+1}) = g(z) + c λ^s z^s + O(z^{s+1}).
Comparing the coefficient of z^s: λc = λ^s c, so λ^{s−1} = 1 and r ∣ s − 1 (mathlib:IsPrimitiveRoot.pow_eq_one_iff_dvd); s ≥ 2 gives s ≥ r + 1.
acceptance: For z² − 3/4 at −1/2 (λ = −1, r = 2): conjugating to 0 gives g = −z + z², g² = z − 2z³ + z⁴, s = 3 and 2 ∣ 2.

nodes.title: Reduction of a*_P to a fixed point
nodes.statement: Let φ be a lift of a morphism of degree d ≥ 2 and P a point of exact period m ≥ 1. Then for every n ≥ 1, a*_P(φ, n) = a*_P(φᵐ, n/m) if m ∣ n, and a*_P(φ, n) = 0 if m ∤ n. If P is not periodic, a*_P(φ, n) = 0 for all n.
hypotheses: K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio.
proofSteps: a_P(φ, k) > 0 iff φᵏ(P) = P iff m ∣ k (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/multiplicity-of-a-periodic-point; mathlib:Function.IsPeriodicPt.minimalPeriod_dvd).
So a*_P(φ, n) = Σ_{d ∣ n, m ∣ d} μ(n/d) a_P(φ, d); if m ∤ n the sum is empty.
If m ∣ n write N = n/m and d = mk: a_P(φ, mk) = a_P(φᵐ, k) (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form-of-an-iterate), so the sum is Σ_{k ∣ N} μ(N/k) a_P(φᵐ, k) = a*_P(φᵐ, N).
acceptance: For z² − 3/4 and P = −1/2 (m = 1): a*_P(φ, 2) = a*_P(φ, 2) trivially; for a 2-cycle point Q, a*_Q(φ, 4) = a*_Q(φ², 2).

nodes.title: The Möbius transform of a multiplicity profile
nodes.statement: Let r ≥ 1, let p be a prime or 0, let B : ℕ → ℤ, and put A(k) = B(v_p(k/r)) if r ∣ k and A(k) = 1 otherwise (v₀ ≡ 0). Then for every N ≥ 1: Σ_{k ∣ N} μ(N/k)·A(k) = [N = 1] + [N = r]·(B(0) − 1) + Σ_{a ≥ 1} [N = r·pᵃ]·(B(a) − B(a − 1)).
hypotheses: r ≥ 1; p = 0 or p prime; v_p = Mathlib's padicValNat, which is identically 0 on positive integers when p = 0.
proofSteps: Write A(k) = 1 + [r ∣ k]·β(v_p(k/r)) with β = B − 1.
Σ_{k∣N} μ(N/k) = [N = 1] (mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.coe_moebius_mul_coe_zeta).

The second part vanishes unless r ∣ N; then with M = N/r it is Σ_{j ∣ M} μ(M/j) β(v_p(j)). Write M = pᵃM′ with p ∤ M′ (for p = 0: a = 0, M′ = M); since μ is multiplicative (mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.isMultiplicative_moebius) the sum factors as (Σ_{i ≤ a} μ(p^{a−i}) β(i))·(Σ_{j′ ∣ M′} μ(M′/j′)) = (β(a) − β(a − 1))·[M′ = 1], with β(−1) := 0.
Collecting terms gives the formula; for p = 0 only N = r survives, with value B(0) − 1.
acceptance: r = 2, p = 0, B ≡ 2: the transform is [N = 1] + [N = 2], the multiplicity pattern of z² − 3/4 at −1/2.

nodes.title: The multiplicity profile k ↦ a_P(k) at a fixed point
nodes.statement: Let φ be a lift of a morphism of degree d ≥ 2 over a field K of characteristic p ≥ 0 with a fixed point P, multiplier λ, and r the multiplicative order of λ (r = 0 if λ is 0 or not a root of unity). Then for k ≥ 1: a_P(k) = 1 if r = 0 or r ∤ k, and a_P(k) = B(v_p(k/r)) if r ≥ 1 and r ∣ k, where B(a) := a_P(r·pᵃ). Moreover B(0) ≥ 2, B is nondecreasing, and if p > 0 then B(a + 1) ≥ 2B(a) − 1.
hypotheses: K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio.
P is fixed by φ; after a conjugation (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form-conjugation) P = [0 : 1] with germ g.
proofSteps: By ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/multiplicity-equals-germ-order, a_P(k) = ord(gᵏ − z).
If r = 0 or r ∤ k then λᵏ ≠ 1, so a_P(k) = 1 (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/germ-order-multiplier-criterion).
If r ∣ k, write k = r·j and h = gʳ; h has linear coefficient 1, so e₀ = ord(h − z) = B(0) ≥ 2 (same lemma).

Write j = pᵃj′ with p ∤ j′ (a = 0 if p = 0). h^{pᵃ} is tangent to the identity with order B(a) ≥ e₀ ≥ 2 (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/germ-order-monotone), and since j′ ≠ 0 in K, ord((h^{pᵃ})^{j′} − z) = B(a) (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/germ-order-parabolic-iterate).
Monotonicity from ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/germ-order-monotone; for p > 0, B(a + 1) = ord((h^{pᵃ})ᵖ − z) ≥ 2B(a) − 1 since p = 0 in K (germ-order-parabolic-iterate).
acceptance: z² − 3/4 at −1/2 over ℚ: λ = −1, r = 2, B ≡ 3, so a(k) = 1 for odd k and 3 for even k.

nodes.title: Effectivity of the dynatomic cycle
nodes.statement: Let φ be a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d ≥ 2 over a field K (any characteristic). Then a*_P(n) ≥ 0 for every n ≥ 1 and every P ∈ ℙ¹(K̄); that is, the n-th dynatomic cycle Z*ₙ(φ) = Σ_{d∣n} μ(n/d) Z_d(φ) is effective.
hypotheses: K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio.
The statement for points over K̄ is the statement over K̄ for the base-changed lift (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form-base-change).
proofSteps: If P is not periodic, a*_P(n) = 0; otherwise let m be its exact period; a*_P(φ, n) = 0 if m ∤ n and = a*_P(φᵐ, n/m) otherwise (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/essential-multiplicity-of-an-iterate).
Replace φ by ψ = φᵐ, so P is fixed, and move P to [0 : 1] by a conjugation over K̄ (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/conjugacy-of-rational-maps, ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form-conjugation).
If r = 0 then a_P(ψ, k) = 1 for all k and a*_P(ψ, N) = [N = 1] ≥ 0 (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/multiplicity-profile-at-a-fixed-point).

If r ≥ 1, the profile of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/multiplicity-profile-at-a-fixed-point and ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/moebius-transform-of-a-multiplicity-profile give a*_P(ψ, N) = [N = 1] + [N = r](B(0) − 1) + Σ_{a≥1}[N = r pᵃ](B(a) − B(a − 1)), a sum of nonnegative terms since B(0) ≥ 2 and B is nondecreasing.
acceptance: For z² + c: Z*ₙ has degree ν₂(n) + [n = 1] with ν₂(1..5) = 2, 2, 6, 12, 30 and no negative coefficients.
