nodes.title: Which formal periods occur: n ∈ {m, m·r, m·r·pᵉ}
nodes.statement: Let φ be a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d ≥ 2 over a field K of characteristic p ≥ 0, P ∈ ℙ¹(K̄) periodic of exact period m, and r the multiplicative order in K̄^× of the multiplier (φᵐ)′(P) (r = ∞ if it is 0 or not a root of unity). For n ≥ 1, a*_P(n) ≥ 1 if and only if (i) n = m; or (ii) n = m·r (if r = 1 then a*_P(m) ≥ 2); or (iii) p > 0 and n = m·r·pᵉ for some e ≥ 1, in which case a*_P(n) ≥ 2^{e−1}(a_P(m·r) − 1). If P is not periodic, a*_P(n) = 0.
hypotheses: K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio.
r = ∞ excludes (ii) and (iii); p = 0 excludes (iii).
proofSteps: Reduce to a fixed point of ψ = φᵐ at [0 : 1] as in ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-cycle-effective (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/essential-multiplicity-of-an-iterate, ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form-conjugation).

With N = n/m: a*_P(ψ, N) = [N = 1] + [N = r](B(0) − 1) + Σ_{a≥1}[N = r pᵃ](B(a) − B(a − 1)) (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/moebius-transform-of-a-multiplicity-profile, ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/multiplicity-profile-at-a-fixed-point); for r = ∞ it is [N = 1].

Each displayed term is ≥ 1 exactly on its support: B(0) − 1 ≥ 1, and for p > 0, B(a) − B(a − 1) ≥ B(a − 1) − 1 ≥ 2^{a−1}(B(0) − 1) ≥ 1 by the growth B(a + 1) ≥ 2B(a) − 1 (same profile lemma), with B(0) = a_P(mr).
For r = 1 the terms at N = 1 add: a*_P(m) = 1 + (B(0) − 1) = a_P(m) ≥ 2.
acceptance: z² − 3/4 over ℚ, P = −1/2: m = 1, r = 2 (multiplier −1), p = 0; the formal periods of P are exactly 1 and 2.
Hutz's Example 3.2 shows in dimension 2 that (iii) genuinely occurs in characteristic 3.

nodes.title: Formal period versus exact period
nodes.statement: Let φ be a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ over a field K. A point P ∈ ℙ¹(K) has formal period n (n ≥ 1) if a*_P(n) > 0, i.e. P occurs in the n-th dynatomic cycle (Morton–Silverman's essential period, Hutz's formal period). Its exact period is Mathlib's Function.minimalPeriod of the induced map f at P. Every point of exact period n has formal period n; a point of formal period n satisfies fⁿ(P) = P and its exact period m divides n, with n ∈ {m, m·r, m·r·pᵉ} (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/formal-period-classification). Formal period 1 is the same as being fixed.
hypotheses: K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio.
f : ℙ¹(K) → ℙ¹(K) is the map induced by φ (DY.0).
proofSteps: Define IsOfFormalPeriod φ n P :⟺ 0 < a*_P(n) (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/essential-multiplicity).
fⁿ(P) = P: a*_P(n) > 0 forces a_P(d) > 0 for some d ∣ n, hence f^d(P) = P and fⁿ(P) = P (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form-zero-locus).
Exact period divides n: mathlib:Function.IsPeriodicPt.minimalPeriod_dvd.
Formal period 1 ⟺ a_P(1) > 0 ⟺ fixed.
acceptance: z² − 3/4, P = −1/2: formal periods {1, 2}, exact period 1.

sources.excerpt: If a*_P(n) > 0, then we call P a formal periodic point of formal period n.
sources.match: The definition.

sources.excerpt: All periodic points of primitive period n are points of formal period n (Proposition 4.1(2)), but there may be periodic points with formal period n and primitive period strictly less than n

nodes.title: Exact period n implies formal period n
nodes.statement: Let φ be a lift of a morphism of degree d ≥ 2 and P a point of exact period n ≥ 1. Then a*_P(n) = a_P(n) ≥ 1; in particular P has formal period n.
hypotheses: K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio.
proofSteps: For d ∣ n with d < n, f^d(P) ≠ P, so a_P(d) = 0 (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/multiplicity-of-a-periodic-point).
Hence a*_P(n) = μ(1)a_P(n) = a_P(n) ≥ 1 (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/essential-multiplicity; fⁿ(P) = P).
acceptance: The 2-cycle {1/2, −3/2} of z² − 7/4 consists of points of formal period 2 (Hutz 2015, Example 1).

sources.excerpt: (2) If P is a periodic point of primitive period n for φ, then a*_P(n) ≠ 0. In particular, points of primitive period n are points of formal period n.

nodes.title: Characteristic zero: formal period n and exact period m < n force n = m·r
nodes.statement: Let K have characteristic 0, φ a lift of a morphism of degree d ≥ 2 over K and P of exact period m. If P has formal period n > m, then n = m·r and the multiplier (φᵐ)′(P) is a primitive (n/m)-th root of unity; in particular P has at most two formal periods, m and m·r.
hypotheses: K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio.
char K = 0.
proofSteps: Apply ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/formal-period-classification with p = 0: case (iii) is excluded, and n ≠ m leaves n = m·r with r finite.
r is the order of the multiplier, so the multiplier is a primitive r-th root of unity (mathlib:orderOf, mathlib:IsPrimitiveRoot) with r = n/m.

nodes.title: A formal periodic point of multiplicity one has exact period n
nodes.statement: Let φ be a lift of a morphism of degree d ≥ 2 over K and n ≥ 1 with n ≠ 0 in K. If a*_P(n) = 1 then P has exact period n. Equivalently, if P has exact period m < n and a*_P(n) ≠ 0 then a*_P(n) ≥ 2.
hypotheses: K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio.
n ≠ 0 in K (Hutz's Example 3.2 shows this is necessary in dimension 2).
proofSteps: By ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/formal-period-classification, n ∈ {m, mr, mrpᵉ}; since p ∤ n (n ≠ 0 in K), n ∈ {m, mr}.

Suppose n = mr with r ≥ 2. The Möbius formula gives a*_P(n) = B(0) − 1 with B(0) = ord((g_{φᵐ})ʳ − z) (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/moebius-transform-of-a-multiplicity-profile, ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/multiplicity-profile-at-a-fixed-point).
ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/germ-order-rotation-congruence gives r ∣ B(0) − 1 with B(0) − 1 ≥ r ≥ 2, contradicting a*_P(n) = 1. So n = m (r = 1 also gives n = m).
acceptance: z² − 3/4, P = −1/2: a*_P(2) = 2 ≠ 1, consistent with P not having exact period 2.

nodes.title: Dynatomic cycles with non-divisible indices are disjoint
nodes.statement: Let φ be a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d ≥ 2 over a field K, and n₁, n₂ ≥ 1 with n₁ ∤ n₂ and n₂ ∤ n₁. Then Z*_{n₁}(φ) and Z*_{n₂}(φ) have disjoint supports: no point has both formal periods.
hypotheses: K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio.
proofSteps: If P lies in both supports, each of n₁, n₂ is m, mr or mrpᵉ (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/formal-period-classification).
These numbers form a chain under divisibility, so the smaller of n₁, n₂ divides the larger, a contradiction.
acceptance: For z² − 3/4: −1/2 lies in Z*₁ and Z*₂, and 1 ∣ 2, consistent with the corollary.

sources.excerpt: Let n₁, n₂ be integers such that n₁ ∤ n₂ and n₂ ∤ n₁. Then Z*_{n₁}(φ) and Z*_{n₂}(φ) have disjoint support.

nodes.title: The dynatomic polynomial Φ*ₙ(φ)
nodes.statement: Let φ be a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d ≥ 2 over a field K and n ≥ 1. The n-th dynatomic polynomial Φ*ₙ(φ) ∈ K[X, Y] is the unique binary form whose image in the fraction field of K[X, Y] is ∏_{m ∣ n} Φₘ(φ)^{μ(n/m)}. It exists by ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-is-polynomial and is unique because K[X, Y] → Frac K[X, Y] is injective; equivalently it is determined recursively by ∏_{m ∣ n} Φ*ₘ(φ) = Φₙ(φ). It is homogeneous of degree Σ_{m∣n} μ(n/m)(dᵐ + 1), its order at every point P is a*_P(n), and its zeros are the points of formal period n. (The Lean prototype is total, with junk value 0 when the Möbius product is not a polynomial.)
hypotheses: K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio.
The definition depends on the chosen lift through the Φₘ; scaling the lift by u ∈ K^× scales Φ*ₙ by a power of u.
proofSteps: Form the element ∏_{(i, j) ∈ divisorsAntidiagonal n} ι(Φⱼ(φ))^{μ(i)} of FractionRing K[X, Y] (mathlib:FractionRing, mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.moebius; ι = algebraMap, zpow in the fraction field).
If it is ι(Q) for some Q, set Φ*ₙ := Q; Q is unique by mathlib:IsFractionRing.injective. Otherwise the junk value 0 (never used for morphisms of degree ≥ 2).
Existence and all listed properties are proved in ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-is-polynomial and ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-degree.
acceptance: For z² + c with lift (X² + cY², Y²): Φ*₁ = Y(X² − XY + cY²), Φ*₂ = X² + XY + (c + 1)Y², and the dehomogenised Φ*₃ is z⁶ + z⁵ + (3c + 1)z⁴ + (2c + 1)z³ + (3c² + 3c + 1)z² + (c + 1)²z + c³ + 2c² + c + 1.

nodes.title: The Möbius product ∏ Φₘ^{μ(n/m)} is a polynomial
nodes.statement: Let φ be a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d ≥ 2 over a field K and n ≥ 1. Then ∏_{m ∣ n} Φₘ(φ)^{μ(n/m)} ∈ Frac K[X, Y] lies in K[X, Y]; i.e. ι(Φ*ₙ(φ)) = ∏_{m∣n} ι(Φₘ(φ))^{μ(n/m)}, ∏_{m∣n} Φ*ₘ(φ) = Φₙ(φ), and ord_P Φ*ₙ(φ) = a*_P(n) for all P.
hypotheses: K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio.
proofSteps: Strong induction on n: suppose forms Q_m with ord_P Q_m = a*_P(m) (all P over K̄) are built for the proper divisors m of n with ∏_{k∣m} Q_k = Φ_m.

The product D = ∏_{m ∣ n, m < n} Q_m has ord_P D = Σ_{m∣n, m<n} a*_P(m) = a_P(n) − a*_P(n) ≤ a_P(n) (Möbius inversion, mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.sum_eq_iff_sum_mul_moebius_eq; effectivity ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-cycle-effective).

Hence D ∣ Φₙ over K̄ (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/binary-form-divisibility-criterion (a); Φₙ ≠ 0 by the API of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form) and so over K (part (b)); put Qₙ := Φₙ/D, with ord_P Qₙ = a*_P(n).

Möbius inversion in the multiplicative group of Frac K[X, Y] (mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.prod_eq_iff_prod_pow_moebius_eq_of_nonzero; all Φₘ ≠ 0) turns ∏_{k∣m} Q_k = Φ_m into Qₙ = ∏_{m∣n} Φₘ^{μ(n/m)}; so Qₙ = Φ*ₙ(φ) (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial).
acceptance: For z² + c: (Φ₂/Φ₁)(X, 1) = (z⁴ + 2cz² − z + c² + c)/(z² − z + c) = z² + z + c + 1, a polynomial (checked by exact division).
Morton's Φ₄(x, c) = (f⁴(x) − x)/(f²(x) − x) is the degree-12 polynomial displayed in Morton 1998, §2 (verified by computer algebra).

sources.excerpt: Then the cycle Z*ₙ(φ) of essential n-periodic points for φ is an effective zero cycle.
sources.match: Effectivity of the cycle is equivalent to the polynomiality of the Möbius product of the forms; proved on curves as Theorem 3.1.

nodes.title: The degree of Φ*ₙ
nodes.statement: For a lift of a morphism of degree d ≥ 2 and n ≥ 1, Φ*ₙ(φ) is homogeneous of degree Σ_{m∣n} μ(n/m)(dᵐ + 1) = νd(n) + [n = 1], where νd(n) = Σ_{m∣n} μ(n/m) dᵐ; for a polynomial map the affine Φ*ₙ(f) has degree νd(n). For d = 2: ν₂(n) = 2, 2, 6, 12, 30, 54, 126 for n = 1, …, 7.
hypotheses: K is a field; φ = (F, G) is a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over K with no common zero in ℙ¹(K̄), i.e. a lift of a morphism of ℙ¹ of degree d (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line); (Fₙ, Gₙ) is the composite lift of φⁿ, so the forms of every iterate are fixed, not only their ratio.
proofSteps: Φₘ is homogeneous of degree dᵐ + 1 (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form), degrees add in products of homogeneous forms, and ∏_{m∣n} Φ*ₘ = Φₙ (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-is-polynomial).
Möbius inversion of n ↦ dⁿ + 1 (mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.sum_eq_iff_sum_mul_moebius_eq) and Σ_{m∣n} μ(n/m) = [n = 1].
acceptance: ν₂(4) = 16 − 4 = 12 = deg Φ₄(x, c) in x (Morton 1998, §2).

nodes.title: Reduction of the dynatomic polynomial at a prime of good reduction
nodes.statement: Let R be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field K and residue field k, and φ a lift with coefficients in R such that both φ_K and its reduction φ̃ are lifts of morphisms of degree d ≥ 2 (good reduction). Then for n ≥ 1 there is a form Q ∈ R[X, Y] with Q = u·Φ*ₙ(φ_K) for some u ∈ K^× and Q̃ = Φ*ₙ(φ̃). In the language of cycles: the reduction of Z*ₙ(φ) is Z*ₙ(φ̃) (and likewise for Zₙ).
hypotheses: R is a discrete valuation ring; φ has good reduction (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/good-reduction-of-a-rational-map): after scaling the lift so that its coefficients lie in R with one of them a unit, φ̃ has no common zero over k̄ (equivalently the resultant is a unit).
proofSteps: Composite lifts and period forms commute with reduction (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form-base-change), and Φₙ(φ̃) ≠ 0 since φ̃ is a morphism of degree ≥ 2 (API of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form); so Φₙ(φ) ∈ R[X, Y] has unit content.

Choose primitive models Qₘ ∈ R[X, Y] of the forms Φ*ₘ(φ_K), m ∣ n (clear denominators and divide by the content; R is a principal ideal domain). By Gauss's lemma (content is multiplicative for polynomials over the unique factorisation domain R, applied to dehomogenisations) ∏_{m∣n} Qₘ = v·Φₙ(φ) with v ∈ R^×.

Reducing, ∏_{m∣n} Q̃ₘ = ṽ·Φₙ(φ̃) for all n with Q̃ₘ ≠ 0; Möbius inversion over k (as in ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-is-polynomial, applied to φ̃, and mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.prod_eq_iff_prod_pow_moebius_eq_of_nonzero) gives Q̃ₙ = w·Φ*ₙ(φ̃) with w ∈ k^×; lift w to R^× and rescale Qₙ (mathlib:IsLocalRing.residue).
acceptance: z² + c with c ∈ ℤ has good reduction at every prime; Φ*₂ = X² + XY + (c + 1)Y² reduces modulo p to Φ*₂ of z² + c̄.

sources.excerpt: Let n ≥ 1 be an integer, let Zₙ(φ) and Z*ₙ(φ) be the cycles of periodic and essential periodic points for φ as defined in Section 1, and similarly let Zₙ(φ̃) and Z*ₙ(φ̃) be the corresponding cycles for φ̃.

sources.excerpt: The rational map φ: ℙ¹_K → ℙ¹_K has good reduction at p if there is a morphism of schemes ℙ¹_{R_p} → ℙ¹_{R_p} over Spec(R_p) whose restriction to the generic fiber is φ.

nodes.title: Periods of rational periodic points at a prime of good reduction
nodes.statement: Let K be the fraction field of a discrete valuation ring R with residue field k of characteristic p ≥ 0, and φ a lift of a morphism of degree d ≥ 2 with good reduction. Let P ∈ ℙ¹(K) have exact period n, let m be the exact period of its reduction P̃ under φ̃, and r the multiplicative order in k̄^× of the multiplier (φ̃ᵐ)′(P̃) (r = ∞ if it is 0). Then n = m, or n = m·r, or n = m·r·pᵉ for some e ≥ 1.
hypotheses: R a discrete valuation ring; good reduction as in ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-reduction; P is K-rational (or, after a finite extension of K and a prime above p, rational over that extension).
proofSteps: P has formal period n (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/exact-period-is-formal-period), so a*_P(φ, n) ≥ 1.

Let Q be the integral model of Φ*ₙ(φ) from ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-reduction. Over a finite extension where Φ*ₙ splits, Q = c·∏ ℓ_{P′}^{a*_{P′}(n)} with integrally normalised linear forms (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/binary-form-divisibility-criterion); all exponents are ≥ 0 (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-cycle-effective).
Reducing, the multiplicity of P̃ in Q̃ = Φ*ₙ(φ̃) is Σ_{P′ ↦ P̃} a*_{P′}(n) ≥ a*_P(n) ≥ 1, so P̃ has formal period n for φ̃.
Apply ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/formal-period-classification to φ̃ over k: n ∈ {m, m·r, m·r·pᵉ}.
acceptance: Hutz 2015, Example 1: z² − 7/4 has possible periods {1, 2} mod 3, {1, 2, 8} mod 5 and {1, 2, 3, 6} mod 7, so every rational periodic point has period 1 or 2.

sources.excerpt: This theorem says that if φ has good reduction over R, then the reduction of the cycle Z*ₙ(φ) modulo p is equal to the cycle Z*ₙ(φ̃) corresponding to the reduced map φ̃ = φ (mod p).
sources.match: Reduction combined with Proposition 3.2 over k gives the constraint.

sources.excerpt: Equivalently, one can take a finite extension L of K so that all of the points in the support of Zₙ(φ) are in ℙ¹(L), choose a prime 𝔓 of L lying over p, and reduce everything modulo 𝔓.
sources.match: The reduction of cycles used in the proof.

nodes.title: A root of Φ*₂ of exact period one: z² − 3/4 at −1/2
nodes.statement: For f(z) = z² − 3/4 over ℚ, Φ*₂(f)(z) = z² + z + 1/4 = (z + 1/2)², so −1/2 is a root of Φ*₂ of multiplicity a*_{−1/2}(2) = 2, yet f(−1/2) = −1/2 has exact period 1; its multiplier f′(−1/2) = −1 is a primitive square root of unity, as ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/formal-period-classification-char-zero requires, and −1/2 has no formal period other than 1 and 2. Likewise, for z² − z, Z*₂ = 2(0) although 0 is fixed (multiplier −1). Correspondingly (−1/2, −3/4) is a rational point of the dynatomic curve Y₁(2) that does not come from a 2-cycle.
hypotheses: Characteristic 0 (over ℚ).
proofSteps: Compute Φ*₂(z² + c) = z² + z + c + 1 (API of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-of-a-polynomial-map, test dynatomicPolynomial_test_quadratic) and substitute c = −3/4.
a*_{−1/2}(2) = a(2) − a(1) = 3 − 1 = 2 (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/multiplicity-profile-at-a-fixed-point with r = 2, B ≡ 3).
The formal periods of −1/2 are {1, 2} by ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/formal-period-classification-char-zero.
The point (x, c) = (−1/2, −3/4) satisfies Φ*₂(x, c) = 0, i.e. lies on Y₁(2) (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-curve).
acceptance: The unit tests IsOfFormalPeriod_test_acceptance, essentialMultiplicity_test_acceptance, dynatomicForm_test_square and DynatomicCurveRing_test_acceptance check this example.

sources.excerpt: For example, (z, c) = (−1/2, −3/4) is a point on C1(2), but −1/2 is actually a fixed point of g(z) = z2−3/4 instead of a point of exact period 2.
sources.match: The example verbatim.

nodes.title: The dynatomic polynomial of a monic polynomial map
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and f ∈ R[z] monic of degree d ≥ 2. Define Φ*₀(f) = 1 and, for n ≥ 1, Φ*ₙ(f) := (fⁿ(z) − z) /ₘ ∏_{m ∣ n, m < n} Φ*ₘ(f) (Mathlib's division by a monic polynomial). Then Φ*ₙ(f) is monic of degree νd(n) = Σ_{m∣n} μ(n/m)dᵐ, ∏_{m∣n} Φ*ₘ(f) = fⁿ(z) − z exactly, the construction commutes with every ring homomorphism, and over a field it is the dehomogenisation of Φ*ₙ of the lift (Y^d f(X/Y), Y^d). For the family z² + c this is Φₙ(z, c) ∈ ℤ[z, c] of Flynn–Poonen–Schaefer and Morton.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring and f ∈ R[z] is monic of degree d ≥ 2 (for z^d + c: R = ℤ[c] or any ring containing c).
For n ≥ 1 the divisor ∏_{m∣n, m<n} Φ*ₘ(f) is monic, so /ₘ is exact division; the recursion is well founded because proper divisors are smaller.
proofSteps: Define by strong recursion on n using mathlib:Polynomial.divByMonic over the proper divisors of n.
fⁿ(z) − z is monic of degree dⁿ for n ≥ 1 (mathlib:Polynomial.Monic.comp, mathlib:Polynomial.natDegree_iterate_comp; subtracting z does not change the leading term since dⁿ ≥ 2).

Monicity, the product formula and the degree formula are ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-of-a-polynomial-map-product and its corollaries; commuting with ring homomorphisms follows from mathlib:Polynomial.map_divByMonic and the fact that map commutes with comp.
acceptance: Φ*₁(z² + c) = z² − z + c, Φ*₂(z² + c) = z² + z + c + 1 (degree 2 = ν₂(2)), Φ*₄(z² + c) is Morton's degree-12 polynomial.

nodes.title: ∏_{m∣n} Φ*ₘ(f) = fⁿ(z) − z for monic f over any ring
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and f ∈ R[z] monic of degree d ≥ 2. For every n ≥ 1, ∏_{m ∣ n} Φ*ₘ(f) = fⁿ(z) − z; each Φ*ₘ(f) is monic of degree νd(m).
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring and f ∈ R[z] is monic of degree d ≥ 2 (for z^d + c: R = ℤ[c] or any ring containing c).
proofSteps: Field case: by ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-dehomogenisation, Φ*ₘ(f) is the dehomogenisation of Φ*ₘ of the lift, and dehomogenising ∏_{m∣n} Φ*ₘ = Φₙ (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-is-polynomial) gives fⁿ(z) − z (API aeval_periodForm_polynomialLift of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form).
Domain case: map to the fraction field, which is injective, and use mathlib:Polynomial.map_divByMonic.

General case: let A = ℤ[a₀, …, a_{d−1}] and F = z^d + Σ aᵢzⁱ ∈ A[z], a monic polynomial over a domain; the ring homomorphism A → R with aᵢ ↦ coeff i f maps F to f, and both sides of the identity commute with this map (mathlib:Polynomial.map_divByMonic; map commutes with comp), so the identity for F implies it for f.
Monicity and degrees: a product of monic polynomials equals the monic fⁿ − z of degree dⁿ; Möbius inversion of the degrees (mathlib:ArithmeticFunction.sum_eq_iff_sum_mul_moebius_eq).
acceptance: f = z² + c over ℤ[c], n = 4: Φ*₁Φ*₂Φ*₄ = f⁴(z) − z with degrees 2 + 2 + 12 = 16.

nodes.title: The affine and homogeneous dynatomic polynomials agree
nodes.statement: Let K be a field and f ∈ K[z] monic of degree d ≥ 2, with lift φ_f = (Y^d f(X/Y), Y^d). For n ≥ 1, Φ*ₙ(φ_f)(X, 1) = Φ*ₙ(f)(X). In particular ∞ has essential multiplicity [n = 1] (it is a superattracting fixed point).
hypotheses: K a field; f monic of degree d ≥ 2.
proofSteps: Strong induction on n. Put Dₘ := Φ*ₘ(φ_f)(X, 1). Dehomogenising ∏_{m∣n} Φ*ₘ(φ_f) = Φₙ(φ_f) (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-is-polynomial) gives ∏_{m∣n} Dₘ = fⁿ(X) − X (API aeval_periodForm_polynomialLift of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/period-form).
Each Dₘ is monic: Dₘ = ∏_{k∣m}(f^k − X)^{μ(m/k)} in K(X) and each f^k − X is monic, so the leading coefficients multiply to 1.

By induction Dₘ = Φ*ₘ(f) for the proper divisors; the product D of these is monic, so Dₙ = (fⁿ − X) /ₘ D = Φ*ₙ(f) (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-of-a-polynomial-map, mathlib:Polynomial.divByMonic).
At ∞: the germ of φ_f at ∞ has multiplier 0, so a_∞(n) = 1 for all n (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/multiplicity-profile-at-a-fixed-point, case r = 0) and a*_∞(n) = [n = 1].
acceptance: For z² + c, n = 1: Φ*₁(φ) = Y(X² − XY + cY²) dehomogenises to z² − z + c = Φ*₁(f), the factor Y accounting for ∞.

nodes.title: The dynatomic polynomial Φ*ₙ(x, c) of the family x^d + c
nodes.statement: For d ≥ 2 and n ≥ 0, Φ*ₙ(x, c) := Φ*ₙ(x^d + c) ∈ ℤ[c][x], the dynatomic polynomial of the monic polynomial x^d + c over ℤ[c] (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-of-a-polynomial-map). It is monic in x of degree νd(n), and for every ring L and c₀ ∈ L its specialisation at c = c₀ is Φ*ₙ(x^d + c₀).

Specialisation: map along the evaluation ℤ[c] → L, c ↦ c₀ (mathlib:Polynomial.eval₂RingHom) and use the API map_dynatomicPolynomial.

nodes.title: The dynatomic curve Y₁(n) of the family x^d + c
nodes.statement: For d ≥ 2 and n ≥ 1, the dynatomic curve Y₁(n) is the affine plane curve over ℤ defined by Φ*ₙ(x, c) = 0, i.e. Spec of the coordinate ring ℤ[c][x]/(Φ*ₙ(x, c)). Its points in a ring L are the pairs (x, c) ∈ L² with Φ*ₙ(x, c) = 0; over a field these are the pairs with x of formal period n for x^d + c (exact period n apart from the points described by ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/formal-period-classification, e.g. (−1/2, −3/4) on Y₁(2)). The substitution σ : x ↦ x^d + c induces an automorphism of Y₁(n) whose n-th power is the identity. The normalisation X₁(n) of its projective closure and the quotient X₀(n) = X₁(n)/⟨σ⟩ are the curves of Flynn–Poonen–Schaefer, Poonen and Stoll; their construction as smooth projective curves belongs to curve theory and is only named here.
hypotheses: d ≥ 2, n ≥ 1; the coordinate ring is Mathlib's AdjoinRoot of Φ*ₙ(x, c) over ℤ[c].
proofSteps: Define the coordinate ring as AdjoinRoot (Φ*ₙ(x, c)) (mathlib:AdjoinRoot) over ℤ[c] (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/unicritical-dynatomic-polynomial).

Points: ring homomorphisms ℤ[c][x]/(Φ*ₙ) → L correspond to pairs (x₀, c₀) with Φ*ₙ(x₀, c₀) = 0 (mathlib:AdjoinRoot.lift); over a field, Φ*ₙ(x₀, c₀) = 0 iff x₀ has formal period n for x^d + c₀ (API eval_dynatomicForm_eq_zero_iff with ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-dehomogenisation).

σ: Φ*ₙ(x, c) divides Φ*ₙ(x^d + c, c) in ℤ[c][x]. Over an algebraic closure of ℚ(c) the roots of Φ*ₙ are permuted by f = x^d + c with multiplicities preserved, because f is a local isomorphism at each root (the critical point 0 is not periodic for transcendental c) and conjugating germs preserves a*; since Φ*ₙ is monic, divisibility over ℚ(c) descends to ℤ[c] (Gauss's lemma). σⁿ = id modulo Φ*ₙ because Φ*ₙ ∣ fⁿ(x) − x (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-of-a-polynomial-map-product).

nodes.title: Y₁(n) over ℂ is smooth and irreducible
nodes.statement: For d ≥ 2 and n ≥ 1, the polynomial Φ*ₙ(x, c) is irreducible in ℂ[x, c] and the affine curve Φ*ₙ(x, c) = 0 in ℂ² is nonsingular: there is no (x, c) with Φ*ₙ = ∂Φ*ₙ/∂x = ∂Φ*ₙ/∂c = 0 (Bousch for d = 2; Buff–Tan; Gao–Ou for all d).
hypotheses: d ≥ 2, n ≥ 1, over ℂ. Gao–Ou prove smoothness and irreducibility of the closure of Xₙ = {(c, z) : z of exact period n, multiplier ≠ 1}; that closure is the zero set of Φ*ₙ by ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/formal-period-classification-char-zero, and Φ*ₙ is squarefree because for generic c its roots are simple.
proofSteps: Identify closure(Xₙ) with V(Φ*ₙ): points of formal period n in characteristic 0 have exact period n, or exact period m ∣ n with multiplier a primitive (n/m)-th root of unity (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/formal-period-classification-char-zero), which is Gao–Ou's description of the boundary ∂Xₙ.

Smoothness (Gao–Ou, Theorem 1.1 / 2.1): a partial derivative of a defining function is the coefficient of a quadratic differential (f_c)_*Q − Q, nonzero by Thurston's contraction principle. This input is recorded as a gap (no roadmap of the atlas plans holomorphic dynamics).
Irreducibility (Gao–Ou, Theorem 1.2; Bousch): a kneading-sequence argument (Lau–Schleicher) shows all components meet; recorded in the same gap.
From the smooth irreducible reduced zero set and squarefreeness of Φ*ₙ, the polynomial is irreducible and its gradient never vanishes on the curve.
acceptance: n = 1, d = 2: Φ*₁ = x² − x + c, ∂/∂c = 1 ≠ 0 everywhere; irreducible (degree one in c).

nodes.title: An explicit height bound for preperiodic points
nodes.statement: Let L be a number field and φ = (F₀, F₁) a pair of binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over L with a Nullstellensatz certificate: forms q(k, j) homogeneous of degree M with Σⱼ q(k, j)·Fⱼ = X_k^{M+d} for k = 0, 1. Let f be the induced map of ℙ¹(L). Then every preperiodic point P = [v] satisfies h(v) ≤ C/(d − 1), where h is Mathlib's logarithmic height Height.logHeight (relative to L) and C = log(2^{[L:ℚ]}·max(H(q), 1)) is the explicit constant of Height.logHeight_eval_ge (H(q) = Height.mulHeightBound q). For a morphism the certificate exists with M = d − 1 by dividing a resultant identity A·F₀ + B·F₁ = Res(F₀, F₁)·X_k^{2d−1} by the resultant.
hypotheses: L a number field with Mathlib's admissible absolute values; φ homogeneous of degree d ≥ 2; the certificate identities hold in L[X, Y].
x is preperiodic for f when some iterate fᵐ(x) is periodic (Mathlib: ∃ m, f^[m] x ∈ Function.periodicPts f); equivalently its forward orbit is finite.
proofSteps: For every v ≠ 0: h(F(v)) ≥ d·h(v) − C (mathlib:Height.logHeight_eval_ge with ι' = Fin 2, N = d; the certificate evaluated at v gives its hypothesis).
h is invariant under scaling (mathlib:Height.logHeight_smul_eq_logHeight), so it is a function on ℙ¹(L), and h(f(P)) = h(F(v)).
If P is preperiodic its forward orbit is finite; let Q be a point of the orbit of maximal height. Then f(Q) is in the orbit, so h(Q) ≥ h(f(Q)) ≥ d·h(Q) − C, whence h(Q) ≤ C/(d − 1), and h(P) ≤ h(Q).
Existence of the certificate for a morphism: the resultant of F₀, F₁ is nonzero and Res·X_k^{2d−1} ∈ (F₀, F₁) with cofactors of degree d − 1 (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/resultant-of-a-rational-map).
acceptance: For z² over ℚ take M = 2 and q(0, 0) = X², q(1, 1) = Y², q(0, 1) = q(1, 0) = 0; then H(q) = 1 and C = log 2, so every preperiodic point has h ≤ log 2; indeed the preperiodic points 0, ±1, ∞ have height 0.

nodes.title: Denominators of preperiodic points of z^d + c
nodes.statement: Let K be a field with a nonarchimedean valuation v (for instance a number field and a finite place), d ≥ 2, c ∈ K and α ∈ K preperiodic for f(z) = z^d + c. If v(c) < 0 then v(c) = d·v(α); if v(c) ≥ 0 then v(α) ≥ 0. Over ℚ: the denominator of every rational preperiodic point α satisfies den(α)^d = den(c); if den(c) is not a d-th power there is no finite rational preperiodic point.
hypotheses: d ≥ 2; v a nonarchimedean valuation (over ℚ: the p-adic valuations padicValRat); stated for preperiodic points, which is what the proof gives and what the search in Hutz 2015 uses (ArithmeticDynamics/E408).
x is preperiodic for f when some iterate fᵐ(x) is periodic (Mathlib: ∃ m, f^[m] x ∈ Function.periodicPts f); equivalently its forward orbit is finite.
proofSteps: Case v(c) < 0 and d·v(α) < v(c): v(f(α)) = d·v(α) by the ultrametric inequality, and inductively v(fⁿ(α)) = dⁿ·v(α) → −∞, so the orbit is infinite.
Case v(c) < 0 and d·v(α) > v(c): v(f(α)) = v(c), so d·v(f(α)) = d·v(c) < v(c) and f(α) falls in the previous case; α is not preperiodic.
Case v(c) ≥ 0 and v(α) < 0: v(f(α)) = d·v(α) < v(α) < 0 and inductively v(fⁿ(α)) → −∞.
Hence for preperiodic α: v(c) < 0 forces d·v(α) = v(c), and v(c) ≥ 0 forces v(α) ≥ 0 (mathlib:padicValRat for K = ℚ).
acceptance: c = −29/16: den c = 16 = 4², and the preperiodic points ±1/4, ±3/4, ±5/4, ±7/4 all have denominator 4.
c = 1/2: den c = 2 is not a square, so z² + 1/2 has no finite rational preperiodic point.

nodes.title: Odd-degree z^d + c over ℚ: only fixed points
nodes.statement: For odd d ≥ 3 and c ∈ ℚ, every rational preperiodic point of f(z) = z^d + c is fixed; there are at most three of them, so #PrePer(f, ℙ¹(ℚ)) ≤ 4 (with ∞), and f has no rational periodic point of exact period > 1.
hypotheses: d odd, d ≥ 3; c ∈ ℚ.
x is preperiodic for f when some iterate fᵐ(x) is periodic (Mathlib: ∃ m, f^[m] x ∈ Function.periodicPts f); equivalently its forward orbit is finite.
proofSteps: f is strictly increasing on ℚ (odd d), hence injective; if f^{m+n}(x) = fᵐ(x) then fⁿ(x) = x, so preperiodic points are periodic.
A periodic point x of a strictly increasing map is fixed: if x < f(x) then x < f(x) < f²(x) < ⋯ never returns to x (and symmetrically).
Fixed points are rational roots of z^d − z + c, whose derivative d·z^{d−1} − 1 has exactly two real zeros (d − 1 even), so there are at most three real roots (Rolle).
acceptance: z³ has the rational preperiodic points −1, 0, 1 (all fixed) and ∞ (Hutz 2015, table: max 4 for z³ + c).

nodes.title: The orbit-repetition check
nodes.statement: For a type α with decidable equality, a self-map f, a finite set S ⊆ α, a fuel bound N and a start x, the check iterates x, f(x), f²(x), … for at most N steps, keeping the list of values seen: it returns true as soon as a value repeats, false as soon as a value lies outside S, and false when the fuel runs out. It is sound (true implies x preperiodic) and, when S contains every preperiodic point of f and N ≥ |S| + 1, complete (x preperiodic implies true).
hypotheses: α has decidable equality (for number fields this is the exact carrier of ComputationalNumberTheory:CN.0; for ℚ Mathlib's DecidableEq ℚ).
x is preperiodic for f when ∃ m, f^[m] x ∈ Function.periodicPts f.
proofSteps: Define by recursion on the fuel: check 0 _ _ = false; check (N + 1) seen x = true if x ∈ seen, else if x ∈ S then check N (x :: seen) (f x) else false.
Soundness: if the check returns true at a value y = fʲ(x) already seen as fⁱ(x), i < j, then fⁱ(x) is periodic (mathlib:Function.periodicPts), so x is preperiodic.
Completeness: see ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/preperiodic-filter-correct.
acceptance: For f = (n ↦ (n + 1) mod 3) on ℕ, S = {0, 1, 2}, fuel 4, start 0: the values 0, 1, 2 are seen and the fourth value 0 repeats: true.

nodes.title: Filtering a candidate set for preperiodic points
nodes.statement: For f : α → α with decidable equality and a finite candidate set S, preperiodicFilter f S is the subset of S of the x for which the orbit-repetition check with fuel |S| + 1 returns true. It is always a subset of S consisting of preperiodic points; if S contains all preperiodic points it is exactly the set of preperiodic points.
hypotheses: α with decidable equality; S a Finset.
x is preperiodic for f when ∃ m, f^[m] x ∈ Function.periodicPts f.
proofSteps: Define preperiodicFilter f S := S.filter (orbitRepeatsWithin f S (|S| + 1) []) (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/orbit-repetition-check).

nodes.title: Correctness of the preperiodic filter
nodes.statement: Let f : α → α with decidable equality and S a finite set containing every preperiodic point of f. Then for every x: x ∈ preperiodicFilter f S if and only if x is preperiodic for f.

nodes.title: The points of ℙ¹(ℚ) of height at most H
nodes.statement: For H ∈ ℕ, the finite set of points [a : b] ∈ ℙ¹(ℚ) with a, b ∈ ℤ, |a|, |b| ≤ H, (a, b) ≠ (0, 0). A point [v] lies in it if and only if its multiplicative height H(v) = Height.mulHeight v (Mathlib, relative to ℚ) is at most H.
hypotheses: H ∈ ℕ; heights are Mathlib's (scaling invariant), so the condition is on points of ℙ¹(ℚ).
proofSteps: Take the image of the pairs in [−H, H]² ∖ {0} under Projectivization.mk (mathlib:Projectivization.mk; classical decidable equality on ℙ¹(ℚ) for the image; the concrete carrier of ComputationalNumberTheory:CN.0 represents a point by a primitive integer pair).

Compatibility: a primitive integer vector (a, b) has H = max(|a|, |b|) (mathlib:Height.mulHeight at the archimedean place, all nonarchimedean factors 1), and every point has a primitive representative; H is scaling invariant (mathlib:Height.mulHeight₁_div_eq_mulHeight).

sources.excerpt: It is not hard to see that points in ℙᴺ(ℚ) of height < B map injectively into ℙᴺ(ℤ/p^ℓℤ) for p^ℓ > 2B².

nodes.title: Certified enumeration of PrePer(φ, ℙ¹(ℚ))
nodes.statement: Let φ = (F₀, F₁) be binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over ℚ with a Nullstellensatz certificate q (Σⱼ q(k, j)Fⱼ = X_k^{M+d}), f the induced map of ℙ¹(ℚ), and H ∈ ℕ with H ≥ exp(log(2·max(H(q), 1))/(d − 1)). Then the set of preperiodic points of f equals preperiodicFilter f (ratPointsOfHeightLE H).
hypotheses: Over ℚ, [ℚ : ℚ] = 1 so the constant of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/height-bound-for-preperiodic-points is log(2·max(H(q), 1)).
x is preperiodic for f when ∃ m, f^[m] x ∈ Function.periodicPts f.
proofSteps: Every preperiodic point has log-height ≤ log(2·max(H(q), 1))/(d − 1), hence multiplicative height ≤ H (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/height-bound-for-preperiodic-points).
So ratPointsOfHeightLE H contains all preperiodic points (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/rational-points-of-bounded-height), and ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/preperiodic-filter-correct gives the equality.
acceptance: Hutz 2015, Example 1: for z² − 7/4 the rational preperiodic points are ∞, 1/2, −3/2 (the 2-cycle) and their rational preimages; the certified enumeration returns this set.

nodes.title: Certified enumeration over a number field from a height enumeration
nodes.statement: Let L be a number field presented exactly (ComputationalNumberTheory:CN.0), φ binary forms of degree d ≥ 2 over L with a Nullstellensatz certificate, f the induced map of ℙ¹(L), B = C/(d − 1) the bound of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/height-bound-for-preperiodic-points, and S a finite set of points of ℙ¹(L) certified to contain every point of logarithmic height ≤ B (EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.0). Then PrePer(f, ℙ¹(L)) = preperiodicFilter f S.
hypotheses: L a number field with an exact presentation and decidable equality (CN.0); S a certified bounded-height enumeration (ED.0).
x is preperiodic for f when ∃ m, f^[m] x ∈ Function.periodicPts f.
proofSteps: Preperiodic points have h ≤ B (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/height-bound-for-preperiodic-points), so S contains them.
Apply ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/preperiodic-filter-correct, using the decidable equality of the exact carrier (ComputationalNumberTheory:CN.0).
acceptance: For L = ℚ this is ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/rational-preperiodic-enumeration-over-Q with S = ratPointsOfHeightLE H.

nodes.title: Rational points of period 1, 2, 3 for z² + c
nodes.statement: Let c ∈ ℚ and f = z² + c. (1) f has a rational fixed point iff c = 1/4 − ρ² for some ρ ∈ ℚ; the fixed points are 1/2 ± ρ. (2) f has a rational point of exact period 2 iff c = −3/4 − σ² for some σ ∈ ℚ, σ ≠ 0; they are −1/2 ± σ and form a 2-cycle. (3) f has a rational point of exact period 3 iff c = −(τ⁶ + 2τ⁵ + 4τ⁴ + 8τ³ + 9τ² + 4τ + 1)/(4τ²(τ + 1)²) for some τ ∈ ℚ ∖ {0, −1}; the cycle is x₁ = (τ³ + 2τ² + τ + 1)/(2τ(τ + 1)) ↦ x₂ = (τ³ − τ − 1)/(2τ(τ + 1)) ↦ x₃ = −(τ³ + 2τ² + 3τ + 1)/(2τ(τ + 1)) ↦ x₁, and τ = x₁ + x₂. There is at most one rational 3-cycle.
hypotheses: f_c(z) = z² + c with c ∈ ℚ; exact period is Mathlib's Function.minimalPeriod of f_c on ℚ (0 for non-periodic points).
proofSteps: (2) A point of exact period 2 is a root of Φ*₂ = x² + x + c + 1 that is not fixed (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/exact-period-is-formal-period, API of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-polynomial-of-a-polynomial-map); x = −1/2 ± σ with σ² = −3/4 − c, and σ = 0 is exactly the fixed point −1/2 of formal period 2 (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/lower-period-root-of-a-dynatomic-polynomial).

(3) Parametrisation: substituting shows x₁ ↦ x₂ ↦ x₃ ↦ x₁ under z² + c(τ) (checked by computer algebra). Converse: for a rational point x of exact period 3, Φ*₃(x, c) = 0; put τ := x + f(x) ∈ ℚ. Modulo Φ*₃(x, c), 2τ(τ + 1)·x = τ³ + 2τ² + τ + 1 and 4τ²(τ + 1)²·c = −(τ⁶ + ⋯ + 1) (identities verified by reduction modulo the monic Φ*₃ in ℚ[c][x]); the first identity forces τ ∉ {0, −1}, so c = c(τ) and x = x₁(τ).

At most one rational 3-cycle: Morton 1992, Theorem 3 (Φ₃ never splits completely over ℚ), proved through the ℚ-points of the elliptic curve Y² = 4X³ − 11X² + 8X (Morton 1992, Lemma 6), requested from EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3.

nodes.title: No rational 4-cycles for z² + c (Morton)
nodes.statement: There are no c, x ∈ ℚ such that x has exact period 4 for z² + c; equivalently Φ*₄(x, c) = 0 has no rational points.
hypotheses: f_c(z) = z² + c with c ∈ ℚ; exact period is Mathlib's Function.minimalPeriod of f_c on ℚ (0 for non-periodic points).
proofSteps: A rational point of exact period 4 is a rational point of Φ*₄(x, c) = 0 (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/exact-period-is-formal-period; Φ*₄ = Morton's degree-12 Φ₄, ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/unicritical-dynatomic-polynomial).

Put w = x + f²(x) = x⁴ + 2cx² + x + c + c² ∈ ℚ; the function field of Φ₄ = 0 is ℚ(w, Δ) with Δ² = (w⁴ − 1)(w² + 2w − 1) and x = w/2 ± Δ/(2(w³ − w)) (Morton 1998, Proposition 2); with u = −(w + 1)/(w − 1) and v = (u + 1)³Δ/4 one gets the curve v² = u(u² + 1)(1 + 2u − u²) (Proposition 3), a model of X₁(16).
Request to EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3: the rational points of v² = u(u² + 1)(1 + 2u − u²) are exactly (0, 0), (±1, ±2) and the point at infinity (Morton cites Washington; J₁(16)(ℚ) is finite).

The affine curve Φ₄(x, c) = 0 is nonsingular: the ideal (Φ₄, ∂Φ₄/∂x, ∂Φ₄/∂c) is the unit ideal of ℚ[x, c] (a Gröbner-basis certificate, verified by computer algebra). Hence every rational point (x, c) is a degree-one place of the function field ℚ(x, c) = ℚ(w, Δ), and Morton's divisor computation (proof of Theorem 4) shows that the six degree-one places are poles of x or c, so no finite (x, c) is rational.
acceptance: For every c tested by Hutz 2015 (heights up to 10⁶) no rational 4-cycle occurs.

nodes.title: No rational 5-cycles for z² + c (Flynn–Poonen–Schaefer)
nodes.statement: There are no c, x ∈ ℚ such that x has exact period 5 for z² + c.
hypotheses: f_c(z) = z² + c with c ∈ ℚ; exact period is Mathlib's Function.minimalPeriod of f_c on ℚ (0 for non-periodic points).
proofSteps: A rational 5-cycle gives a rational point (t, c) of the trace curve τ₅(t, c) = 0 with t = x + f(x) + ⋯ + f⁴(x) (FPS §3; τ₅ displayed there). The affine curve τ₅ = 0 has a single singular point (−1, −4/3), a node.

FPS's substitutions (z = r − 1, c = s − 4/3; s = rt; r = q − t; completing the square in t; p = 192y, q = −1 − 4x/3) map every rational point with r ≠ 0 and 216 + 144q − 72q² ≠ 0 to a rational point of C : y² = x⁶ + 8x⁵ + 22x⁴ + 22x³ + 5x² + 6x + 1. From the displayed models, the excluded rational points have r = 0 (c ∈ {−4/3, −2}) or q ∈ {3, −1}, where the equation is linear in t with solutions (q, t) = (3, −4/3) and (−1, 1/3), i.e. c = −64/9 and c = −16/9.

Requests: EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3 (J(C)(ℚ) ≅ ℤ by a 2-descent, FPS Theorem 3) and EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.4 (Chabauty–Coleman at p = 3 shows C(ℚ) = {(0, ±1), (−3, ±1), ∞±}, FPS Theorem 6).

The six points have c ∈ {∞, −16/9, −64/9, −2} (FPS Table 2). So c ∈ {−2, −16/9, −64/9, −4/3}; for these, ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/unicritical-rational-preperiodic-enumeration-correct returns {−2, −1, 0, 1, 2} (c = −2) and ∅ (the others), with no point of exact period 5.
acceptance: The three Galois-stable 5-cycles at c = −2, −16/9, −64/9 generate cyclic quintic fields of conductors 11, 41, 275 (FPS Table 2); none is pointwise rational.

nodes.title: No rational 6-cycles for z² + c, conditionally (Stoll)
nodes.statement: Let J be the Jacobian of the genus-4 curve X₀^dyn(6) = X₁^dyn(6)/⟨σ⟩ for z² + c. If the Mordell–Weil rank of J(ℚ) is 3, then X₀^dyn(6) has exactly ten rational points and there are no c, x ∈ ℚ with x of exact period 6 for z² + c. (Stoll deduces rank J(ℚ) ≤ 3, hence = 3, from the weak Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture for J together with analytic continuation and the functional equation of L(J, s); that hypothesis is not consumed here.)
hypotheses: f_c(z) = z² + c with c ∈ ℚ; exact period is Mathlib's Function.minimalPeriod of f_c on ℚ (0 for non-periodic points).

Explicit hypothesis: rank J(ℚ) = 3. The Jacobian, its Mordell–Weil group and its rank are supplied through EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3; the statement is not formalisable in Mathlib at the pinned commit, so no Lean form is suggested.
proofSteps: Ten known rational points of X₀^dyn(6) generate a torsion-free subgroup G of rank 3 of J(ℚ) (Stoll §3); if rank J(ℚ) = 3 then G has finite index and J(ℚ) is the saturation of G (request EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3: saturation at the required primes).

A Chabauty argument at p = 5 with a differential annihilating G shows that no further rational point maps into the saturation of G (request EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.4, Stoll's lemma before Theorem 6).

None of the non-cuspidal points among the ten lifts to a rational point of X₁^dyn(6), and a rational 6-cycle gives a non-cuspidal rational point of X₁^dyn(6) (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/dynatomic-curve, ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/exact-period-is-formal-period).
acceptance: Hutz 2015 and FPS §10 find no rational 6-cycles in their searches, consistent with the theorem.

nodes.title: Which combinations of periods ≤ 3 occur for z² + c over ℚ
nodes.statement: Let c ∈ ℚ. (1) z² + c has rational points of period 1 and of period 2 iff c = −(3µ⁴ + 10µ² + 3)/(4(µ² − 1)²) for some µ ∈ ℚ ∖ {−1, 0, 1}. (2) If z² + c has a rational point of period 3, it has no rational point of period 1 or 2.
hypotheses: f_c(z) = z² + c with c ∈ ℚ; exact period is Mathlib's Function.minimalPeriod of f_c on ℚ (0 for non-periodic points).
proofSteps: (1) By ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/quadratic-rational-cycles-of-length-at-most-three, c = 1/4 − ρ² = −3/4 − σ² with σ ≠ 0; this conic has the rational point (ρ, σ) = (1, 0), and µ = (1 − ρ)/σ parametrises it: ρ = −(µ² + 1)/(µ² − 1), σ = 2µ/(µ² − 1).

(2) With period 1 and 3: (τ, 2τ(τ + 1)ρ) lies on y² = x⁶ + 2x⁵ + 5x⁴ + 10x³ + 10x² + 4x + 1 (a model of X₁(18)); with period 2 and 3: (τ, 2τ(τ + 1)σ) lies on y² = x⁶ + 2x⁵ + x⁴ + 2x³ + 6x² + 4x + 1 (X₁(13)).
Request to EffectiveDiophantineMethods:ED.3: each of these genus-2 curves has exactly six rational points: the two at infinity and (−1, ±1), (0, ±1). These have τ ∈ {0, −1}, excluded.
acceptance: c = −29/16 has a 3-cycle and no rational fixed point or 2-cycle (Figure 1 of Poonen 1995).

nodes.title: Points of type (m, 1) are negatives of periodic points
nodes.statement: Let c ∈ ℚ and m ≥ 1. A rational x is of type (m, 1) for z² + c iff −x is a nonzero rational point of exact period m. The number of rational points of type (m, 1) equals the number of rational points of period m, except for (c, m) = (−1, 2) and (0, 1), where there is one fewer.
hypotheses: f_c(z) = z² + c with c ∈ ℚ; exact period is Mathlib's Function.minimalPeriod of f_c on ℚ (0 for non-periodic points).
A point of type (m, n) (n ≥ 1) enters an m-cycle after exactly n steps: minimalPeriod(fⁿ(x)) = m and f^{n−1}(x) is not periodic (Poonen 1995, §3).
proofSteps: If x is of type (m, 1) then f(fᵐ(x)) = f(x) but fᵐ(x) ≠ x, so fᵐ(x) = −x; −x is periodic of period m and nonzero.
Conversely if −x ≠ 0 has period m then f(x) = f(−x) is periodic of period m and fᵐ(x) = −x ≠ x.

0 is preperiodic only for c ∈ {−2, −1, 0} (c ∈ ℤ by ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/unicritical-preperiodic-valuation-lemma and |c| ≤ 2 by ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/unicritical-preperiodic-archimedean-bound), periodic only for c = −1 (period 2) and c = 0 (period 1).
acceptance: c = −29/16: the points of type (3, 1) are 1/4, 7/4, −5/4, the negatives of the 3-cycle.

nodes.title: Poonen's conjecture: no rational cycles of length ≥ 4
nodes.statement: Poonen's conjecture is the proposition: for all c, x ∈ ℚ and N ≥ 4, x does not have exact period N for z² + c. It is recorded as a statement, used only as an explicit hypothesis. It is proved for N = 4 (Morton) and N = 5 (Flynn–Poonen–Schaefer), and for N = 6 under the hypothesis of ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/stoll-conditional-no-rational-six-cycles.
hypotheses: An open conjecture: no theorem consumes it except as an explicit hypothesis (roadmap acceptance).
proofSteps: Define PoonenConjecture : Prop := ∀ c x : ℚ, ∀ N ≥ 4, minimalPeriod (z ↦ z² + c) x ≠ N (mathlib:Function.minimalPeriod).
Projections: the N = 4 and N = 5 instances are ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/morton-no-rational-four-cycles and ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/flynn-poonen-schaefer-no-rational-five-cycles (unconditional).
acceptance: Sharpness of the bound 4: z² − 29/16 has the rational 3-cycle −1/4 ↦ −7/4 ↦ 5/4.

nodes.title: The Morton–Silverman uniform boundedness conjecture
nodes.statement: For integers N ≥ 1, d ≥ 2 and D ≥ 1, the uniform boundedness conjecture UBC(N, d, D) is the proposition: there is a constant C(N, d, D) such that for every number field K with [K : ℚ] ≤ D and every morphism φ : ℙᴺ → ℙᴺ of degree d defined over K, #PrePer(φ, ℙᴺ(K)) ≤ C(N, d, D). It is recorded as a statement (the Lean prototype states N = 1, with Set.encard), used only as an explicit hypothesis; for each fixed φ the set is finite (Northcott), and uniformity across all maps of fixed degree is the open content.
hypotheses: An open conjecture; no theorem of this roadmap consumes it except as an explicit hypothesis (DY.6 acceptance).
d ≥ 2 is essential: in degree 1 the identity has every point preperiodic.
proofSteps: Define UniformBoundednessConjecture d D : Prop := ∃ C, ∀ number fields L with [L : ℚ] ≤ D, ∀ lifts φ of morphisms of ℙ¹ of degree d over L, #{preperiodic points of the induced map} ≤ C (Set.encard, so infinite sets are not bounded).
Monotonicity in D, the trivial case D = 0, and the necessity of d ≥ 2 are API/tests; the per-map finiteness is ArithmeticDynamics:DY.3/finiteness-of-rational-preperiodic-points.
acceptance: Any constant for (N, d, D) = (1, 2, 1) is ≥ 9, by z² − 29/16.

nodes.title: The analytic projective line at a place of a number field, with its kernel, circle measures and weight
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field and v a place of K. Fix a complete algebraically closed field C_v containing the completion K_v, with the absolute value |·|_v extending the standard absolute value of ℚ (|p|_v = 1/p when v lies over the prime p; the usual absolute value when v is infinite, where C_v = ℂ), and fix an embedding ι_v : K̄ → C_v extending K → K_v; put |x|_v := |ι_v(x)|_v, an absolute value on K̄ extending v. The analytic line at v is the compact Hausdorff space P¹_v^an equal to the Riemann sphere P¹(ℂ) when v is infinite and to the Berkovich projective line over C_v when v is finite, together with: (i) the inclusion P¹(K̄) → P¹_v^an of type I points, x ↦ ι_v(x), ∞ ↦ ∞; (ii) the kernel δ_v on A¹_v^an × A¹_v^an, equal to |x − y| on ℂ at an infinite place and to the Hsia kernel relative to ∞ at a finite place (δ_v(x, y) = diam(x ∨ y), the diameter of the smallest disc point above x and y; Favre–Rivera-Letelier's sup{x, y}), so that δ_v(ι_v x, ι_v y) = |x − y|_v for x, y ∈ K̄; (iii) for a ∈ K̄ and r > 0 the circle measure m_{a,r,v}, the normalised arc-length probability measure on {z : |z − ι_v a| = r} at an infinite place and the Dirac mass at the point ζ_{ι_v a, r} (the sup-norm on the disc D(ι_v a, r)) at a finite place; (iv) the weight r_v = [K_v : ℚ_v]/[K : ℚ].
hypotheses: K is a number field; v ranges over its places (Mathlib's NumberField.InfinitePlace K ⊔ NumberField.FinitePlace K).
At a finite place the Berkovich projective line over C_v and its points ζ_{a,r} are imported from TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic TB.1.
proofSteps: Choose C_v: ℂ at an infinite place; at a finite place over p the completion of an algebraic closure of K_v (isometric to Mathlib's PadicComplex p). Extend K → K_v ⊂ C_v to ι_v : K̄ → C_v, which exists because C_v is algebraically closed (IsAlgClosed.lift).

At a finite place take the Berkovich projective line over C_v, with its type I–IV points, the points ζ_{a,r}, compactness and the Hsia kernel relative to ∞, from TB.1 (request). At an infinite place take OnePoint ℂ with its compact Hausdorff topology.

Define δ_v, the circle measures m_{a,r,v} and the weight r_v as in the statement. At an infinite place w the weight is mult(w)/[K : ℚ] (NumberField.InfinitePlace.mult); at a finite place it is [K_v : ℚ_p]/[K : ℚ].

With these weights r_v log|a|_v = [K : ℚ]^{-1} log ‖a‖_v, where ‖·‖_v is Mathlib's normalised place value (w(a)^{mult w} at infinite w, the FinitePlace value at finite v), so the product formula of Mathlib (NumberField.prod_abs_eq_one) reads Σ_v r_v log|a|_v = 0 for a ∈ K^×.
Another embedding ι'_v differs from ι_v by an element of Gal(K̄/K), so every construction below made from Galois-stable data is independent of the choice (see DY.4/galois-orbit-measure).
acceptance: At the finite place 2 of ℚ: δ(ι 1, ι 3) = |2|_2 = 1/2 and δ(ζ_{0,1}, ζ_{0,1}) = 1.
∫ log δ_v(ι z, w) dm_{0,1,v}(w) = log⁺|z|_v at every place (Jensen's formula at infinite places, the value of the Gauss norm at finite places).
For K = ℚ all weights equal 1, and for any K the infinite weights sum to 1.

nodes.title: The standard measure λ_v at a place
nodes.statement: The standard measure at a place v of K is λ_v := m_{0,1,v}: the normalised Haar (arc-length) probability measure on the unit circle {|z| = 1} ⊂ ℂ when v is infinite, and the Dirac mass at the Gauss point ζ_{0,1} when v is finite. Its logarithmic potential is ∫ log δ_v(z, w) dλ_v(w) = log⁺|z|_v for z ∈ P¹(C_v) ∖ {∞}, extended continuously to A¹_v^an.
hypotheses: v is a place of the number field K; P¹_v^an is DY.4/analytic-line-at-a-place.
proofSteps: Define λ_v as the circle measure m_{0,1,v} of DY.4/analytic-line-at-a-place.

Its potential is log max(|z|_v, 1) = log⁺|z|_v by the circle-measure potential formula (Jensen's formula at infinite places, Mathlib circleAverage_log_norm_sub_const_eq_log_radius_add_posLog; the Gauss norm at finite places).
(λ_v, λ_v)_v = −∫ log⁺|z|_v dλ_v = 0 and ([x]_v, λ_v)_v = −log⁺|x|_v follow from the Fubini formula for the mutual energy supplied by TB.6.
acceptance: (λ_v, λ_v)_v = 0 at every place.
([2], λ_v)_v = −log 2 at an infinite place and ([p^{-1}], λ_v)_v = −log p at the place p of ℚ.

nodes.title: Galois-stable finite sets and their probability measures [F]_v
nodes.statement: A finite set F ⊂ P¹(K̄) is Galois-stable if σ(F) = F for every σ ∈ Gal(K̄/K); the Galois orbit Gal(K̄/K)·x of x ∈ P¹(K̄) is the smallest Galois-stable set containing x, of cardinality [K(x) : K] (1 for x = ∞). For a nonempty finite F ⊂ P¹(K̄) and a place v, [F]_v := |F|^{-1} Σ_{x∈F} δ_{ι_v x} is the equidistributed probability measure on the image of F in P¹_v^an. If F is Galois-stable, [F]_v does not depend on the embedding ι_v.
hypotheses: F finite; for independence of ι_v, F Galois-stable.
proofSteps: The orbit of x ∈ K̄ is the set of roots of its minimal polynomial over K, finite of size [K(x) : K] (minpoly).

Any two embeddings ι_v, ι'_v : K̄ → C_v over K_v satisfy ι'_v = τ ∘ ι_v ∘ σ with σ ∈ Gal(K̄/K) and τ a continuous automorphism of C_v over K_v fixing |·|_v; a Galois-stable F is mapped onto the same finite set, so [F]_v is unchanged (as a measure on the analytic line built from the chosen ι_v).
Under a finite extension L/K and a place w of L above v, a Galois-stable set over K is Galois-stable over L and [F]_w = [F]_v on P¹_w^an = P¹_v^an.
acceptance: [{0}]_v = δ_{ι 0}; for F the primitive cube roots of unity over ℚ, [F]_∞ is the average of the Dirac masses at e^{±2πi/3}.
{√2} is not Galois-stable over ℚ, and {√2, −√2} is.

nodes.title: Regularisation of a finite set by circles of radius r
nodes.statement: For a place v, a nonempty finite set F ⊂ K̄ and r > 0, the regularised measure is [F]_{v,r} := |F|^{-1} Σ_{x∈F} m_{x,r,v}: the average of the normalised arc-length measures on the circles |z − x| = r (v infinite) or of the Dirac masses at the points ζ_{x,r} (v finite). Its potential is ∫ log δ_v(z, w) d[F]_{v,r}(w) = |F|^{-1} Σ_{x∈F} log max(|z − x|_v, r) for z ∈ K̄, it has a continuous potential in the sense of TB.6, and for x, y ∈ K̄ the mutual energy is (m_{x,r,v}, m_{y,r,v})_v = −log max(|x − y|_v, r).
hypotheses: F ⊂ K̄ finite nonempty (∞ ∉ F); r > 0.
proofSteps: The potential formula for one circle measure is AnalyticLine.potential_circle; average over F.

At an infinite place the potential z ↦ |F|^{-1}Σ log max(|z − x|, r) is continuous on ℂ and log|z| + o(1) at ∞, so [F]_{v,r} − λ_v has a continuous potential on P¹(ℂ); at a finite place [F]_{v,r} is a finite combination of Dirac masses at type II/III points, which has continuous potential (FRL §4.3; TB.6).

The energy of two circle measures: (m_{x,r}, m_{y,r})_v = −∫ log max(|z − x|_v, r) dm_{y,r}(z) = −log max(|x − y|_v, r), by applying the potential formula twice (for x = y the value is −log r: at an infinite place the circle average of log max(|z − x|, r) over |z − x| = r; at a finite place −log diam(ζ_{x,r}) = −log r).
As r → 0, m_{x,r,v} → δ_{ι_v x} weakly, hence [F]_{v,r} → [F]_v.
acceptance: (m_{x,r}, m_{x,r})_v = −log r; for r = 1/2 at an infinite place this is log 2.

nodes.title: The self-energy bound for regularised finite sets
nodes.statement: For every place v, every nonempty finite F ⊂ K̄ and every r > 0: ([F]_{v,r}, [F]_{v,r})_v ≤ ([F]_v, [F]_v)_v + (−log r)/|F|, where ([F], [F])_v = −|F|^{-2} Σ_{x≠y∈F} log|x − y|_v (the diagonal omitted).
hypotheses: F ⊂ K̄ finite nonempty, r > 0.
proofSteps: Expand bilinearly: ([F]_r, [F]_r)_v = |F|^{-2} Σ_{x,y∈F} (m_{x,r}, m_{y,r})_v.
For x ≠ y, (m_{x,r}, m_{y,r})_v = −log max(|x − y|_v, r) ≤ −log|x − y|_v (DY.4/regularised-measure-of-a-finite-set).
For x = y, (m_{x,r}, m_{x,r})_v = −log r; there are |F| diagonal terms, contributing |F|^{-2}·|F|·(−log r) = (−log r)/|F|.
acceptance: Equality holds when |x − y|_v ≥ r for all x ≠ y in F.
For F = {0, 1} at an infinite place and r = 1/4: ([F]_r, [F]_r) = (log 4)/2 = ([F], [F]) + (log 4)/2.

sources.excerpt: Pour tout ε > 0 et tout sous-ensemble ﬁni F de A¹(C_p), on a ([F]_ε, [F]_ε) ≤ ([F], [F]) + |F|^{−1} log ε^{−1} .

nodes.title: Continuous functions are uniformly approximated by their circle averages
nodes.statement: For every place v and every continuous g : P¹_v^an → ℝ, the regularisation modulus ω_g(r) := sup_{x∈K̄} |∫ g dm_{x,r,v} − g(ι_v x)| tends to 0 as r → 0⁺. If g is κ-Hölder for the chordal metric (0 < κ ≤ 1), then ω_g(r) ≤ C r^κ.
hypotheses: g continuous on the compact space P¹_v^an.
proofSteps: Infinite place: P¹(ℂ) is a compact metric space for the chordal metric, g is uniformly continuous, and every point of the circle |z − x| = r is within chordal distance ≤ r of x; so ω_g(r) ≤ sup_{d(z,z')≤r} |g(z) − g(z')| → 0.

Finite place: m_{x,r} = δ_{ζ_{x,r}}. Suppose there are ε > 0, x_n ∈ K̄ and r_n → 0 with |g(ζ_{x_n,r_n}) − g(ι x_n)| ≥ ε. By compactness pass to a subsequence with ι x_n → S weakly. For every polynomial P = c Π(T − a_i), ζ_{x_n,r_n}(P) = |c| Π max(|x_n − a_i|_v, r_n) and ι x_n(P) = |c| Π |x_n − a_i|_v have the same limit S(P); so ζ_{x_n,r_n} → S weakly too (TB.1: the weak topology is generated by S ↦ S(P)), and continuity of g gives a contradiction.
The Hölder bound: the chordal distance between ι x and ζ_{x,r} (FRL §4.7) is at most r.
acceptance: For g(z) = min(log⁺|z|_v, 1): ω_g(r) ≤ r at an infinite place (g is 1-Lipschitz in |z|) and ω_g(r) = 0 for r < 1 at a finite place (log⁺|ζ_{x,r}|_v = log⁺|x|_v).
For g constant, ω_g ≡ 0.

nodes.title: Regularising a finite set changes its energy against a measure with continuous potential by little
nodes.statement: Let v be a place, ρ a probability measure on P¹_v^an with continuous potential, and g the continuous function with g(z) = ∫ log δ_v(z, w) dρ(w) − log⁺|z|_v off ∞ (a potential of ρ − λ_v). For every nonempty finite F ⊂ K̄ and 0 < r < 1: |([F]_v, ρ)_v − ([F]_{v,r}, ρ)_v| ≤ ω_g(r) + ε_v(r), with ε_v(r) = r if v is infinite and ε_v(r) = 0 if v is finite.
hypotheses: ρ a probability measure with continuous potential (TB.6); 0 < r < 1.
proofSteps: By the Fubini formula for the energy (TB.6; FRL Lemmas 2.5 and 4.4), (µ, ρ)_v = −∫ g_ρ dµ for µ = [F]_v and µ = [F]_{v,r}, where g_ρ(z) = ∫ log δ_v(z, w) dρ(w) = log⁺|z|_v + g(z).
The g-part is bounded by ω_g(r) (DY.4/regularisation-modulus-tends-to-zero).
The log⁺-part: at an infinite place |log⁺|x + re^{it}| − log⁺|x|| ≤ r since log⁺ is 1-Lipschitz; at a finite place log⁺|ζ_{x,r}| = log⁺ max(|x|_v, r) = log⁺|x|_v because r < 1.
acceptance: For ρ = λ_v at a finite place and r < 1 the difference is 0.
For ρ = λ_v at an infinite place and F = {0}: ([0], λ) = 0 and ([0]_r, λ) = 0 for r < 1, so the difference is 0 ≤ r.

nodes.title: Lower bound for the local energy of [F] − ρ
nodes.statement: Let v, ρ and g be as in DY.4/regularised-pairing-estimate. For every nonempty finite F ⊂ K̄ and 0 < r < 1: ([F]_v − ρ, [F]_v − ρ)_v ≥ ([F]_{v,r} − ρ, [F]_{v,r} − ρ)_v − 2(ω_g(r) + ε_v(r)) − (−log r)/|F| ≥ −2(ω_g(r) + ε_v(r)) − (−log r)/|F|.
hypotheses: ρ a probability measure with continuous potential; 0 < r < 1.
proofSteps: Expand both energies bilinearly (TB.6): (µ − ρ, µ − ρ) = (µ, µ) − 2(µ, ρ) + (ρ, ρ) for µ = [F]_v and µ = [F]_{v,r}.
Compare the (µ, µ) terms by DY.4/regularised-self-energy-bound and the (µ, ρ) terms by DY.4/regularised-pairing-estimate.
The second inequality: [F]_{v,r} − ρ has total mass 0 and continuous potential, so its energy is ≥ 0 by the positivity of TB.6 (FRL Propositions 2.6 and 4.5).
acceptance: The unregularised energy can be negative: for P(T) = T² + C with |C|_v > 1 at a finite v ∤ 2 and F_n the fixed points of Pⁿ, ([F_n] − µ_{P,v}, [F_n] − µ_{P,v})_v = −n2^{−n} log √|C|_v (FRL §6.7, corrected in sourceIssues E504), consistent with the bound as r → 0 only through the −log r/|F| term.

sources.match: The infinite-place statement (the constant C disappears with circle regularisation, Fili Lemma 12).
The finite-place statement.

nodes.title: Local energy criterion for weak convergence of [F_n]
nodes.statement: Let v be a place and ρ a probability measure on P¹_v^an with continuous potential. Let F_n ⊂ P¹(K̄) be nonempty finite sets with |F_n| → ∞ and limsup_n ([F_n ∖ {∞}]_v − ρ, [F_n ∖ {∞}]_v − ρ)_v ≤ 0. Then [F_n]_v → ρ weakly: ∫ f d[F_n]_v → ∫ f dρ for every continuous f : P¹_v^an → ℝ.
hypotheses: ρ probability with continuous potential; |F_n| → ∞.
proofSteps: Removing ∞ from F_n changes [F_n]_v by a measure of total variation ≤ 2/|F_n| → 0, so assume ∞ ∉ F_n.

Let ν_{n,r} := [F_n]_{v,r} − ρ, of mass 0 with continuous potential. By DY.4/energy-lower-bound-after-regularisation, (ν_{n,r}, ν_{n,r})_v ≤ ([F_n] − ρ, [F_n] − ρ)_v + 2(ω_g(r) + ε_v(r)) + (−log r)/|F_n|, so limsup_n (ν_{n,r}, ν_{n,r})_v ≤ 2(ω_g(r) + ε_v(r)), which tends to 0 as r → 0.

For a test function φ in the dense class D_v of TB.6 (smooth at infinite places; locally constant off a finite subtree and C¹ on its edges at finite places) the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality |∫ φ dν|² ≤ ⟨φ, φ⟩_v (ν, ν)_v (TB.6; FRL (32)–(33) with the squares restored, sourceIssues E501) gives limsup_n |∫ φ dν_{n,r}| ≤ (⟨φ, φ⟩_v · 2(ω_g(r) + ε_v(r)))^{1/2}.
|∫ φ d([F_n]_{v,r} − [F_n]_v)| ≤ ω_φ(r) uniformly in n (DY.4/regularisation-modulus-tends-to-zero); letting n → ∞ then r → 0 gives ∫ φ d[F_n]_v → ∫ φ dρ for φ ∈ D_v.

D_v is dense in C(P¹_v^an) for the sup norm and all measures involved are probability measures, so the convergence holds for every continuous f (MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_iff_forall_integral_tendsto).
acceptance: For ρ = λ_v at an infinite place and F_n the n-th roots of unity, ([F_n] − λ, [F_n] − λ) = −(log n)/n → 0 (since Π_{y≠x}(x − y) = n x^{n−1}), and [F_n] → λ, the Haar measure on the circle.
The hypothesis |F_n| → ∞ is needed: F_n = {0} for all n has ([F_n] − λ, [F_n] − λ) = 0 at a finite place but [F_n] = δ_0 ≠ λ_v.

nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the local energy against the standard measure at finite places
nodes.statement: Let v be a finite place and F ⊂ K̄ a nonempty finite set. Then (λ_v − [F]_v, λ_v − [F]_v)_v = (2/|F|) Σ_{x∈F} log⁺|x|_v − |F|^{-2} Σ_{x≠y∈F} log|x − y|_v ≥ (2/|F|²) Σ_{x∈F} log⁺|x|_v ≥ 0.
hypotheses: v finite (the ultrametric inequality is used).
proofSteps: Expand: (λ, λ) = 0, ([F], λ) = −|F|^{-1} Σ log⁺|x|_v (DY.4/standard-measure-at-a-place), ([F], [F]) = −|F|^{-2} Σ_{x≠y} log|x − y|_v.
Ultrametric inequality: log|x − y|_v ≤ log⁺|x|_v + log⁺|y|_v; summing over ordered pairs x ≠ y gives Σ_{x≠y} log|x − y| ≤ 2(|F| − 1) Σ_x log⁺|x|_v.
Hence the energy is ≥ (2/|F| − 2(|F| − 1)/|F|²) Σ log⁺|x|_v = (2/|F|²) Σ log⁺|x|_v ≥ 0.
acceptance: For F a set of v-adic units with pairwise differences units, the energy is exactly 0.
At an infinite place the statement fails: F = {1, −1} gives (λ − [F], λ − [F]) = −(1/2) log 2 < 0.

nodes.title: Adelic measures on the projective line
nodes.statement: An adelic measure ρ over the number field K is a family (ρ_v)_{v∈M_K} of probability measures ρ_v on P¹_v^an such that (i) ρ_v = λ_v for all but finitely many places v, and (ii) each ρ_v has a continuous potential: there is a continuous g_{ρ,v} : P¹_v^an → ℝ with g_{ρ,v}(z) = ∫ log δ_v(z, w) dρ_v(w) − log⁺|z|_v for z ∈ A¹_v^an (equivalently ρ_v − λ_v = Δ g_{ρ,v} for the Laplacian of TB.6, normalised by Δ log⁺|z|_v = λ_v − δ_∞); the continuous extension satisfies g_{ρ,v}(∞) = 0. N(ρ) denotes the finite set of places with ρ_v ≠ λ_v. For a finite extension L/K an adelic measure over K defines one over L by ρ_w := ρ_v for w | v.
hypotheses: K a number field; P¹_v^an, δ_v and λ_v as in DY.4/analytic-line-at-a-place and DY.4/standard-measure-at-a-place.
The Laplacian, potentials and the class of measures with continuous potential are those of TB.6 (request).
proofSteps: The data are the measures ρ_v; condition (ii) is stated through the logarithmic potential, which needs only the kernel δ_v.

A measure with continuous potential charges no type I point (the potential of a point mass at a type I point is −∞ there), in particular not ∞; hence g_{ρ,v}(z) → 0 as z → ∞ (FRL, proof of Proposition 2.6), which is the normalisation g_{ρ,v}(∞) = 0.
Base change: for L/K and w | v, P¹_w^an = P¹_v^an (the same C_v) and λ_w = λ_v, so (ρ_v)_{w|v} is an adelic measure over L.
acceptance: The standard family λ = (λ_v) is an adelic measure with N(λ) = ∅.
Over ℚ, ρ_p := δ_{ζ_{0,p}} at one prime p and ρ_v := λ_v elsewhere is an adelic measure: g_{ρ,p}(z) = log max(|z|_p, p) − log⁺|z|_p is continuous.
ρ_v := δ_{ι_v 0} at one place is not an adelic measure: its potential log|z|_v − log⁺|z|_v tends to −∞ at 0.

sources.excerpt: Une mesure adélique ρ est la donnée en chaque place d'une mesure de probabilité ρ_v supportée dans P¹(C_v), telle que ρ_v = λ_v hors d'un nombre ﬁni de places, et telle que ρ_v admette un potentiel continu en toutes les places, i.e. ρ_v = λ_v + ∆g avec g continue.
sources.match: The definition.

sources.excerpt: We call ρ = (ρ_v)_{v∈M_K} an adelic measure if for each v ∈ M_K, ρ_v is a Borel probability measure on P¹(C_v) which is equal to λ_v for all but ﬁnitely many v and admits a continuous potential with respect to λ_v at the remaining places

nodes.title: The height h_ρ attached to an adelic measure
nodes.statement: For an adelic measure ρ over K and a finite Galois-stable set F ⊂ P¹(K̄), h_ρ(F) := ½ Σ_{v∈M_K} r_v ([F]_v − ρ_v, [F]_v − ρ_v)_v, where (·,·)_v is the mutual energy of TB.6 (the diagonal of type I points omitted, so ([F]_v, [F]_v)_v = −|F|^{-2} Σ_{x≠y∈F∖{∞}} log|x − y|_v); for x ∈ P¹(K̄), h_ρ(x) := h_ρ(Gal(K̄/K)·x). Only finitely many terms are nonzero, and h_ρ does not depend on K, on the embeddings ι_v, or on replacing K by a finite extension.
hypotheses: ρ adelic over K; F Galois-stable finite.
proofSteps: Finiteness: for v ∉ N(ρ) finite such that every x ∈ F ∖ {∞} is a v-adic unit or v-integral with all pairwise differences v-adic units, ([F] − λ_v, [F] − λ_v)_v = 0; all but finitely many places are of this kind (FRL §5.2).
Independence of ι_v: DY.4/galois-orbit-measure. Independence of K: base change of ρ, the formula Σ_{w|v} r_w = r_v and the equality of the local terms at all w | v.
Galois invariance: Gal·(σx) = Gal·x.
acceptance: h_λ(2) = log 2, h_λ(ζ) = 0 for a root of unity ζ, and h_λ(∞) = 0 (DY.4/standard-adelic-height-is-the-weil-height).
For the adelic measure over ℚ with ρ_p = δ_{ζ_{0,p}}: h_ρ(∞) = −½ log p and h_ρ(0) = ½ log p.

nodes.title: Product formula for the energy of a Galois-stable finite set
nodes.statement: For every finite Galois-stable F ⊂ P¹(K̄), Σ_{v∈M_K} r_v ([F]_v, [F]_v)_v = 0, where ([F]_v, [F]_v)_v = −|F|^{-2} Σ_{x≠y∈F∖{∞}} log|x − y|_v.
hypotheses: F Galois-stable and finite.
proofSteps: Let F′ = F ∖ {∞}; then ([F], [F])_v = −|F|^{-2} log|Δ_{F′}|_v with Δ_{F′} = Π_{x≠y∈F′} (x − y), a nonzero element of K̄.
Every σ ∈ Gal(K̄/K) permutes the ordered pairs of F′, so σ(Δ_{F′}) = Δ_{F′}; hence Δ_{F′} ∈ K^× (the fixed field of Gal(K̄/K) in characteristic 0 is K).
The product formula Σ_v r_v log|a|_v = 0 for a ∈ K^× (NumberFieldPlace.sum_weight_mul_log_eq_zero, from NumberField.prod_abs_eq_one) gives the claim.
acceptance: F = {√2, −√2} over ℚ: Δ = −8, and Σ_v r_v log|−8|_v = log 8 − log 8 = 0.
The corrected sign: DKY (2.16) prints the middle expression without the minus sign (sourceIssues E507); the value 0 is unaffected.

nodes.title: Decomposition of the adelic height into local potentials
nodes.statement: For an adelic measure ρ over K: h_ρ(∞) = ½ Σ_v r_v (ρ_v, ρ_v)_v, and for every finite Galois-stable F ⊂ K̄ (∞ ∉ F), h_ρ(F) = h_ρ(∞) − Σ_v r_v (ρ_v, [F]_v)_v = h_ρ(∞) + Σ_v r_v |F|^{-1} Σ_{x∈F} ∫ log δ_v(ι_v x, w) dρ_v(w). These two identities determine h_ρ; consequently h_ρ(F) = |F|^{-1} Σ_{x∈F} h_ρ(x) for every Galois-stable finite F ⊂ P¹(K̄).
hypotheses: ρ adelic; F Galois-stable finite.
proofSteps: [∞]_v pairs to 0 with every measure (pairs involving ∞ are excluded from the energy), so ([∞] − ρ, [∞] − ρ)_v = (ρ_v, ρ_v)_v.
Expand ([F] − ρ, [F] − ρ)_v = (ρ, ρ)_v − 2(ρ, [F])_v + ([F], [F])_v (bilinearity, TB.6) and sum with weights; the last terms sum to 0 by DY.4/product-formula-for-the-energy-of-a-finite-set.
(ρ_v, [F]_v)_v = −|F|^{-1} Σ_{x∈F} ∫ log δ_v(ι_v x, w) dρ_v(w) by the Fubini formula for the energy (TB.6).
The right-hand side is affine in [F]_v, so for F a disjoint union of Galois orbits O_i, h_ρ(F) = Σ_i (|O_i|/|F|) h_ρ(O_i); for ∞ ∈ F use the first identity for the orbit {∞}.
acceptance: For ρ = λ: h_λ(∞) = 0 and h_λ(F) = Σ_v r_v |F|^{-1} Σ_{x∈F} log⁺|x|_v.
For the Gauss-radius measure over ℚ at p: h_ρ(0) = −½ log p − (−log p) = ½ log p.

sources.excerpt: Pour chaque mesure adélique ρ = {ρ_v}_{v∈M_K} on a h_ρ(∞) = ½ Σ_{v∈M_K} (( ρ_v, ρ_v ))_v et h_ρ(F) = h_ρ(∞) − Σ_{v∈M_K} (( ρ_v, [F] ))_v. De plus, ces propriétés déterminent la hauteur h_ρ.

nodes.title: The standard adelic measure gives Mathlib's absolute logarithmic Weil height
nodes.statement: For every x ∈ K̄, h_λ(x) = NumberField.absLogHeight₁ x, and h_λ(∞) = 0; that is, h_λ is the absolute logarithmic Weil height on P¹(K̄) with the convention h(∞) = 0.
hypotheses: λ the standard adelic measure over K.
proofSteps: By DY.4/adelic-height-decomposition and DY.4/standard-measure-at-a-place, h_λ(∞) = ½ Σ r_v (λ_v, λ_v) = 0 and h_λ(x) = Σ_v r_v |O|^{-1} Σ_{y∈O} log⁺|y|_v with O = Gal·x.

Let L = K(x). The embeddings of L into C_v over K correspond to the places w | v of L, each counted [L_w : K_v] times; hence Σ_v r_v |O|^{-1} Σ_{y∈O} log⁺|y|_v = Σ_{w∈M_L} r_w log⁺|x|_w (r_w = [L_w : ℚ_w]/[L : ℚ]).

By AnalyticLine.weight_mul_log_eq over L this is [L : ℚ]^{-1} logHeight₁ x computed in L (NumberField.logHeight₁_eq), which equals absLogHeight₁ x (DT.0/abs-mul-height-eq-rpow: the absolute height may be computed in any number field containing x).
acceptance: h_λ(2) = log 2, h_λ(1/2) = log 2, h_λ(√2) = ½ log 2 over ℚ.
h_λ(ζ) = 0 for every root of unity ζ, and h_λ(0) = 0.

nodes.title: Adelic heights differ from the Weil height by a bounded function
nodes.statement: For an adelic measure ρ over K and every x ∈ K̄: |h_ρ(x) − h_ρ(∞) − absLogHeight₁(x)| ≤ Σ_{v∈N(ρ)} r_v sup|g_{ρ,v}|; hence h_ρ − h is bounded on P¹(K̄) (with h(∞) = 0).
hypotheses: ρ adelic over K.
proofSteps: By DY.4/adelic-height-decomposition for ρ and for λ, h_ρ(x) − h_ρ(∞) − h_λ(x) = −Σ_v r_v (ρ_v − λ_v, [O]_v)_v with O = Gal·x.
For v ∉ N(ρ) the term vanishes; for v ∈ N(ρ), −(ρ_v − λ_v, [O]_v)_v = |O|^{-1} Σ_{y∈O} g_{ρ,v}(ι_v y) (Fubini, TB.6), bounded by sup|g_{ρ,v}| (continuous on a compact space).
Conclude with DY.4/standard-adelic-height-is-the-weil-height.
acceptance: For the Gauss-radius measure at p: h_ρ(x) − h(x) = −½ log p + log max(|x|_p, p) − log⁺|x|_p ∈ [−½ log p, ½ log p].

sources.excerpt: Pour toute mesure adélique ρ, la fonction h_ρ est une hauteur de Weil. En d'autres termes, la différence h_ρ − h_nv est uniformément bornée sur K̄.

nodes.title: Mahler formula for adelic heights
nodes.statement: Let ρ be an adelic measure over K and α ∈ K̄ with monic minimal polynomial P ∈ K[T]. Then h_ρ(α) = h_ρ(∞) + deg(α)^{-1} Σ_v r_v ∫ log|P|_v dρ_v, where |P|_v(S) := S(P) on A¹_v^an (the value of the multiplicative seminorm S at P at a finite place; |P(z)| at an infinite place). At a finite place with ρ_v = λ_v the integral is log of the Gauss norm max_i |a_i|_v of P = Σ a_i T^i, so the sum is finite; for ρ = λ it is the classical Mahler-measure formula for the Weil height.
hypotheses: ρ adelic; α ∈ K̄, P = minpoly_K(α).
proofSteps: DY.4/adelic-height-decomposition with F = Gal·α, the set of roots of P: h_ρ(α) = h_ρ(∞) + Σ_v r_v deg(α)^{-1} Σ_{β: P(β)=0} ∫ log δ_v(ι_v β, S) dρ_v(S).

For S ∈ A¹_v^an, Σ_β log δ_v(ι_v β, S) = log S(P): at an infinite place |P(z)| = Π|z − β|; at a finite place δ_v(β, S) = S(T − β) (the Hsia kernel relative to ∞ against a type I point, TB.1) and the seminorm S is multiplicative.
At a finite place with ρ_v = λ_v = δ_{ζ_{0,1}}, ζ_{0,1}(P) is the Gauss norm.
acceptance: ρ = λ, K = ℚ, α = 1/2: P = T − 1/2; the place 2 contributes log|1/2|_2 = log 2 and the infinite place contributes ∫ log|z − 1/2| dλ = log⁺(1/2) = 0, so h(1/2) = log 2.
ρ = λ, α = √2 over ℚ: P = T² − 2, the infinite integral is ∫ log|z² − 2| dλ = log 2, finite places give 0, so h(√2) = ½ log 2.

sources.excerpt: Soit α ∈ K̄ et soit P ∈ K[T] le polynôme (unitaire) minimal de α sur K. Alors on a h_ρ(α) = h_ρ(∞) + 1/deg(α) Σ_{v∈M_K} ∫_{P¹(C_v)} log ∥P∥_v dρ_v .

nodes.title: Galois-stable sets of bounded height and bounded size are finite in number
nodes.statement: Let ρ be an adelic measure over K and (F_n) a sequence of finite Galois-stable subsets of P¹(K̄) in which every finite set occurs for only finitely many n, with sup_n h_ρ(F_n) < ∞. Then |F_n| → ∞.
hypotheses: Each finite set occurs finitely often in (F_n); h_ρ(F_n) bounded above.
proofSteps: Suppose |F_n| ≤ M along a subsequence. By DY.4/adelic-height-decomposition h_ρ(F_n) = |F_n|^{-1} Σ_{x∈F_n} h_ρ(x), and by DY.4/adelic-height-is-a-weil-height h_ρ(x) ≥ h(x) + h_ρ(∞) − C ≥ h_ρ(∞) − C for every x; so every x ∈ F_n has h(x) ≤ M(H + C + |h_ρ(∞)|) + C =: B, where H bounds h_ρ(F_n).

Every x ∈ F_n ∖ {∞} has degree [ℚ(x) : ℚ] ≤ M[K : ℚ]; by Northcott over ℚ̄ (DT.0/northcott-absolute-height) there are finitely many such x, so finitely many possible sets F_n — contradicting that each set occurs finitely often.
acceptance: For F_n = {x_n} with pairwise distinct x_n ∈ K of bounded height the hypothesis fails only if the x_n repeat; e.g. the Galois orbits of the n-th roots of unity have h_λ = 0 and |F_n| = n → ∞.

sources.excerpt: Tout élément de F_n est alors de degré au plus M et de hauteur (naïve) au plus H. Mais la propriété de Northcott afﬁrme que l'ensemble de ces points est ﬁni, voir par exemple [HS, Theorem B.2.3].
sources.match: The argument (here with the hypothesis 'each set occurs finitely often' in place of 'pairwise distinct').

nodes.title: Equidistribution of small points for adelic measures on P¹
nodes.statement: Let ρ be an adelic measure over K and (F_n) a sequence of finite Galois-stable subsets of P¹(K̄) in which every finite set occurs for only finitely many n, with limsup_n h_ρ(F_n) ≤ 0. Then h_ρ(F_n) → 0 and, for every place v, [F_n]_v → ρ_v weakly on P¹_v^an. In particular, for every sequence of pairwise distinct x_n ∈ P¹(K̄) with h_ρ(x_n) → 0, the Galois-orbit measures [Gal·x_n]_v converge weakly to ρ_v at every place.
hypotheses: ρ adelic over K.
F_n Galois-stable, each finite set occurring finitely often (in particular pairwise distinct sets, or Galois orbits of pairwise distinct points).
proofSteps: |F_n| → ∞ by DY.4/small-galois-stable-sets-grow.
Let N be N(ρ) together with the infinite places. For v ∉ N, ρ_v = λ_v at a finite place and ([F_n] − λ_v, [F_n] − λ_v)_v ≥ 0 (DY.4/nonnegative-local-energy-at-standard-places, applied to F_n ∖ {∞}).

For v ∈ N and every 0 < r < 1, ([F_n] − ρ_v, [F_n] − ρ_v)_v ≥ −2(ω_{g,v}(r) + ε_v(r)) − (−log r)/|F_n| (DY.4/energy-lower-bound-after-regularisation); letting n → ∞ then r → 0 (DY.4/regularisation-modulus-tends-to-zero) gives liminf_n ([F_n] − ρ_v, [F_n] − ρ_v)_v ≥ 0. Removing ∞ from F_n changes these energies by o(1).
Hence liminf h_ρ(F_n) ≥ 0, and with limsup ≤ 0, h_ρ(F_n) → 0.

Fix v₀. r_{v₀} ([F_n] − ρ_{v₀}, [F_n] − ρ_{v₀})_{v₀} ≤ 2h_ρ(F_n) − Σ_{v∈N∖{v₀}} r_v ([F_n] − ρ_v, [F_n] − ρ_v)_v − (nonnegative terms), so limsup_n ([F_n] − ρ_{v₀}, [F_n] − ρ_{v₀})_{v₀} ≤ 0; conclude with DY.4/local-equidistribution-criterion.
For points: the Galois orbits of pairwise distinct x_n form a sequence in which each finite set occurs at most |set| times.
acceptance: ρ = λ, F_n = the primitive n-th roots of unity over ℚ: h_λ = 0, and [F_n]_∞ converges to the Haar measure on the unit circle (Bilu).
The hypothesis on repetitions is needed: F_n = {0} for all n has h_λ = 0, but [F_n]_∞ = δ_0 does not converge to λ_∞.
Regularisation is needed in the proof: the individual local terms can be negative (FRL §6.7; sourceIssues E504).

nodes.title: The essential minimum of an adelic height is nonnegative
nodes.statement: For every adelic measure ρ over K and every ε > 0, the set {x ∈ P¹(K̄) : h_ρ(x) < −ε} is finite; equivalently, liminf_n h_ρ(x_n) ≥ 0 along every sequence of pairwise distinct points of P¹(K̄).
hypotheses: ρ adelic over K.
proofSteps: If the set were infinite, choose pairwise distinct x_n in it; their Galois orbits F_n satisfy limsup h_ρ(F_n) ≤ −ε ≤ 0 and each finite set occurs finitely often, so h_ρ(F_n) → 0 by DY.4/equidistribution-of-small-points-on-p1, a contradiction.
The two formulations are equivalent by extracting subsequences.
acceptance: For ρ = λ the height is ≥ 0 everywhere, and the essential minimum 0 is attained on the roots of unity.
For the Gauss-radius measure at p, h_ρ(∞) = −½ log p < 0 at the single point ∞, consistent with finiteness of {h_ρ < −ε}.

sources.excerpt: Pour toute mesure adélique ρ, la fonction h_ρ est une hauteur de Weil dont le minimum essentiel est non-négatif. En d'autres termes, la différence h_ρ − h_nv est uniformément bornée sur P¹(K̄), et pour tout ε > 0, l'ensemble {α ∈ P¹(K̄); h_ρ(α) < −ε} est ﬁni.

nodes.title: Quantitative equidistribution for adelic measures with Hölder potentials
nodes.statement: Let ρ be an adelic measure over K whose potentials are Hölder in the sense that ω_{g_{ρ,v}}(r) ≤ C₀ r^κ for 0 < r < 1 and all v ∈ N(ρ), for some C₀ > 0 and 0 < κ ≤ 1. There is C > 0 depending only on ρ such that for every place v, every test function φ ∈ D_v (TB.6) with Dirichlet norm ⟨φ, φ⟩_v and regularisation constant Lip_v(φ) (|∫ φ dm_{x,r,v} − φ(ι_v x)| ≤ Lip_v(φ) r), and every Galois-stable finite F ⊂ K̄ with |F| ≥ 2: |∫ φ d[F]_v − ∫ φ dρ_v| ≤ Lip_v(φ) |F|^{−1/κ} + (⟨φ, φ⟩_v r_v^{−1} (2h_ρ(F) + C log|F| / |F|))^{1/2}.
hypotheses: ρ adelic with Hölder potentials at the places of N(ρ).
The square root and the factor 2/r_v correct FRL Theorem 7 (sourceIssues E501, E502).
proofSteps: Put r := |F|^{−1/κ} ≤ |F|^{−1}. Summing DY.4/energy-lower-bound-after-regularisation over N ∪ {v} and using DY.4/nonnegative-local-energy-at-standard-places at the other places: Σ_{w∈N∪{v}} r_w ([F]_r − ρ_w, [F]_r − ρ_w)_w ≤ 2h_ρ(F) + (|N| + 1) max_w r_w (2C₀|F|^{−1} + 2r + log|F|/(κ|F|)).
Each regularised term is ≥ 0 (TB.6 positivity), so r_v ([F]_r − ρ_v, [F]_r − ρ_v)_v ≤ 2h_ρ(F) + C log|F|/|F|.
Cauchy–Schwarz for the Dirichlet form (TB.6): |∫ φ d([F]_r − ρ_v)| ≤ ⟨φ, φ⟩_v^{1/2} ([F]_r − ρ_v, [F]_r − ρ_v)_v^{1/2}.

The bound is quadratic-homogeneous-correct: replacing φ by tφ multiplies both sides by |t|, which fails for FRL's printed (34).
