nodes.title: Adelic metrics on O_{P¹}(1)
nodes.statement: An adelic metric on O_{P¹}(1) over K is a family φ = (φ_v)_{v∈M_K} of continuous functions φ_v : P¹_v^an → ℝ with φ_v = 0 for all but finitely many v. It defines at each place the continuous metric ‖·‖_v := ‖·‖_{st,v} e^{−φ_v} on O(1) over P¹_v^an, where the standard metric is ‖s(x)‖_{st,v} = |s(x₀, x₁)|_v / max(|x₀|_v, |x₁|_v) for a linear form s, extended continuously to P¹_v^an. With affine coordinate z = x₀/x₁ and ∞ = (1 : 0): −log‖x₁‖_v(z) = log⁺|z|_v + φ_v(z) (the section x₁ has divisor ∞) and −log‖x₀‖_v(z) = log⁺|z^{-1}|_v + φ_v(z) (divisor 0). The pair Ō = (O(1), (‖·‖_v)_v) is an adelically metrized line bundle on P¹ in the sense of Zhang, and φ ↦ Ō is a bijection onto continuous adelic metrics on O(1).
hypotheses: K a number field; the metrics on O(1)^an over P¹_v^an are those of TB.6 (request), described on P¹ by the function φ_v.
proofSteps: The standard metric is continuous on P¹_v^an: at a finite place −log‖x₁‖_st(S) = log⁺|S| is continuous on the Berkovich line (TB.1).

Two continuous metrics on the same line bundle differ by e^{−φ} with φ continuous (the ratio of norms of a nowhere-vanishing local section), so every continuous metric has the stated form; this is the P¹ case of the correspondence of TB.6.
The finiteness condition is Zhang's adelic condition: at all but finitely many places the metric is the model metric of the standard model P¹_{O_K}.
acceptance: The standard metric φ = 0 gives −log‖x₁‖_v(z) = log⁺|z|_v.
At a place v and R ≥ 1, φ_v(z) = log max(|z|_v, R) − log⁺|z|_v extends continuously to P¹_v^an with φ_v(∞) = 0; with φ_w = 0 elsewhere it is an adelic metric.

nodes.title: Curvature measures and semipositivity of an adelic metric on O(1)
nodes.statement: For an adelic metric φ on O(1) over K, the curvature at v is the signed measure µ_{φ,v} := λ_v + Δφ_v of total mass 1 = deg O(1) (Laplacian of TB.6, Δ log⁺|z|_v = λ_v − δ_∞), characterised by Δ(−log‖s‖_v) = µ_{φ,v} − δ_{div s} for every linear form s; φ is semipositive if every µ_{φ,v} is a positive measure. For semipositive φ, µ_φ = (µ_{φ,v})_v is an adelic measure: µ_{φ,v} = λ_v when φ_v = 0, and ∫ log δ_v(z, w) dµ_{φ,v}(w) − log⁺|z|_v = φ_v(z) − φ_v(∞), so the potential of µ_{φ,v} is g_{µ_φ,v} = φ_v − φ_v(∞). This is the P¹ case of the Chambert-Loir measure c₁(Ō_v) of TB.6.
hypotheses: φ an adelic metric on O(1) over K.
proofSteps: Δ(−log‖x₁‖_v) = Δ log⁺|z|_v + Δφ_v = λ_v + Δφ_v − δ_∞ (TB.6 normalisation), so µ_{φ,v} := λ_v + Δφ_v; total mass: Δφ_v has mass 0.
For another linear form s = a x₀ + b x₁, −log‖s‖_v − (−log‖x₁‖_v) = −log|a z + b|_v + (log of the constant part), whose Laplacian is δ_∞ − δ_{div s}; this gives the characterisation for every s.

For semipositive φ, µ_{φ,v} is a probability measure; its potential g(z) = ∫ log δ_v(z, w) dµ(w) − log⁺|z|_v satisfies Δg = µ − λ = Δφ_v, so g − φ_v is constant (Laplacian kernel = constants, TB.6), and g(∞) = 0 fixes the constant.
At the places with φ_v = 0, µ_{φ,v} = λ_v; these are all but finitely many.
acceptance: Standard metric: µ_v = λ_v at every place.
The metric φ_v(z) = log max(|z|_v, R) − log⁺|z|_v (R ≥ 1) has curvature m_{0,R,v} (the circle of radius R at an infinite place, δ_{ζ_{0,R}} at a finite place): semipositive.
The metric −φ_v with R > 1 has curvature 2λ_v − m_{0,R,v}, which is not positive: not semipositive.

nodes.title: The height of an adelic metric on O(1)
nodes.statement: For an adelic metric φ on O(1) over K and x ∈ P¹(K̄) with Galois orbit O, h_φ(x) := Σ_v r_v |O|^{-1} Σ_{y∈O} (−log‖s(y)‖_v) for any linear form s over K with s(y) ≠ 0 on O. Equivalently h_φ(x) = absLogHeight₁(x) + Σ_v r_v |O|^{-1} Σ_{y∈O} φ_v(ι_v y) for x ∈ K̄, and h_φ(∞) = Σ_v r_v φ_v(∞).
hypotheses: φ an adelic metric; s a linear form over K not vanishing on O.
proofSteps: Independence of s: two sections differ by a rational function in K(z) whose values on O multiply to an element of K^× (a norm), killed by the product formula (PST Proposition 8, proof).

With s = x₁ (for x ≠ ∞): −log‖x₁‖_v = log⁺|z|_v + φ_v, and Σ_v r_v |O|^{-1} Σ_y log⁺|y|_v = absLogHeight₁(x) (DY.4/standard-adelic-height-is-the-weil-height); with s = x₀ at ∞: −log‖x₀‖_v(∞) = φ_v(∞).
Independence of K and Galois invariance as for h_ρ.
acceptance: Standard metric: h_φ = absLogHeight₁ with h(∞) = 0.
Over ℚ with φ_p = log max(|z|_p, p) − log⁺|z|_p: h_φ(0) = log p ≠ h(0) = 0 and h_φ(∞) = 0.

nodes.title: The normalised adelic metric of an adelic measure
nodes.statement: For an adelic measure ρ over K, the normalised adelic metric Ō^ρ is φ^ρ_v := g_{ρ,v} + ½(ρ_v, ρ_v)_v, where g_{ρ,v} is the potential of ρ_v (normalised by g_{ρ,v}(∞) = 0). It is semipositive with curvature ρ, φ^ρ_v = 0 for v ∉ N(ρ) (since (λ_v, λ_v)_v = 0), and φ^ρ_v(∞) = ½(ρ_v, ρ_v)_v. Every semipositive adelic metric with curvature ρ is φ^ρ + c for a unique family of constants c = (c_v).
hypotheses: ρ an adelic measure over K.
proofSteps: φ^ρ_v is continuous (g_{ρ,v} is) and vanishes where ρ_v = λ_v.
Its curvature is λ_v + Δg_{ρ,v} = ρ_v (DY.4/curvature-measures-of-an-adelic-metric).
Two semipositive metrics with the same curvature differ at each place by a function with zero Laplacian, hence a constant (TB.6).
acceptance: φ^λ = 0, the standard metric.
For the Gauss-radius measure at p over ℚ: φ^ρ_p(z) = log max(|z|_p, p) − log⁺|z|_p − ½ log p.

nodes.title: The Arakelov–Zhang pairing of adelic metrics on O(1)
nodes.statement: For semipositive adelic metrics φ₁, φ₂ on O(1) over K with curvatures µ₁, µ₂, the Arakelov–Zhang pairing is Ō₁·Ō₂ := Σ_v r_v [φ_{2,v}(∞) + ∫ (log⁺|z|_v + φ_{1,v}(z)) dµ_{2,v}(z)], the value of Zhang's arithmetic intersection number h₁((u)) + h₂((s)) + Σ_v r_v ∫ log‖s‖_{1,v}^{-1} Δ(log‖u‖_{2,v}^{-1}) at the sections s = x₁ (divisor ∞) and u = x₀ (divisor 0). The sum is finite. For rational maps f, g of degree ≥ 2 over K, the pairing of their canonical adelic metrics is the dynamical Arakelov–Zhang pairing ⟨f, g⟩ (DY.4/dynamical-arakelov-zhang-pairing).
hypotheses: φ₁, φ₂ semipositive adelic metrics on O(1) over K.
proofSteps: The integral is finite: log⁺|z|_v + φ_{1,v} is µ_{2,v}-integrable because µ_{2,v} has continuous potential (TB.6; FRL Lemmas 2.4 and 4.3).
At the places where φ₁ = φ₂ = 0 the term is ∫ log⁺ dλ_v = 0.
The value at s = x₁, u = x₀: h₁(0) + h₂(∞) + Σ_v r_v [∫(log⁺|z| + φ₁) dµ₂ − φ_{1,v}(0)], and h₁(0) = Σ_v r_v φ_{1,v}(0) (DY.4/height-of-an-adelic-metrized-line-bundle), giving the formula.

For the Gauss-radius metric Ō_p over ℚ (φ_p = log max(|z|_p, p) − log⁺|z|_p): Ō_p·Ō_p = log p.

nodes.statement: For adelic measures ρ, σ over K, ⟨ρ, σ⟩ ≥ 0, with equality if and only if ρ = σ. Consequently, for semipositive adelic metrics φ₁, φ₂ on O(1) with Ō₁·Ō₁ = Ō₂·Ō₂ = 0: Ō₁·Ō₂ ≥ 0, with equality iff µ_{1,v} = µ_{2,v} for every v, in which case h_{φ₁} = h_{φ₂}.
hypotheses: ρ, σ adelic.
proofSteps: At each place ρ_v − σ_v has total mass 0 and a continuous potential, so (ρ_v − σ_v, ρ_v − σ_v)_v ≥ 0 with equality iff ρ_v = σ_v (TB.6; FRL Propositions 2.6 and 4.5); the weights r_v are positive.

For metrics use DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing-of-normalised-metrics; equal curvatures and vanishing self-pairings give φ₁ − φ₂ = c with Σ_v r_v c_v = 0 (DY.4/height-of-a-semipositive-metric-versus-its-curvature), hence equal heights (AdelicMetric.height_twist).

nodes.title: The square root of the Arakelov–Zhang pairing is a metric (Fili)
nodes.statement: d(ρ, σ) := ⟨ρ, σ⟩^{1/2} is a metric on the set of adelic measures (over K, compatibly with base change): d(ρ, σ) = 0 iff ρ = σ, d is symmetric, and d(ρ, τ) ≤ d(ρ, σ) + d(σ, τ). For normalised semipositive adelic metrics this reads (Ō₁·Ō₃)^{1/2} ≤ (Ō₁·Ō₂)^{1/2} + (Ō₂·Ō₃)^{1/2}.
hypotheses: Adelic measures over K.
proofSteps: At each place, (·,·)_v is a symmetric bilinear form on the real vector space X_v of signed measures of mass 0 with continuous potential, positive definite (TB.6); ‖ν‖_v := (ν, ν)_v^{1/2} is a norm on X_v.
On the finitely supported families ν = (ν_v) ∈ ⊕_v X_v, ‖ν‖ := (½ Σ_v r_v ‖ν_v‖_v²)^{1/2} is a norm (ℓ² sum of norms with positive weights), and d(ρ, σ) = ‖ρ − σ‖.
The triangle inequality for ‖·‖ gives the claim; nondegeneracy is DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing-nonnegative-and-nondegenerate; the metric version is DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing-of-normalised-metrics.
acceptance: d(λ, ρ_p) = (½ log p)^{1/2} for the Gauss-radius measure ρ_p, and d(ρ_p, ρ_q) = (½ log p + ½ log q)^{1/2} for distinct primes p, q (disjoint supports of the differences), consistent with the triangle inequality through λ.
DKY (7.3) is the case of the Lattès heights ĥ_{t₁}, ĥ_{t₂} and h_{F,η}.

sources.excerpt: Then d is a metric on the real vector space of all adelic measures, that is, for all adelic measures ρ, σ, τ, we have d(ρ, τ) ≤ d(ρ, σ) + d(σ, τ), and d(ρ, σ) = 0 if and only if ρ = σ as adelic measures.

nodes.title: Heights along small sequences converge to the Arakelov–Zhang pairing
nodes.statement: Let ρ, σ be adelic measures over K and (F_n) finite Galois-stable subsets of P¹(K̄), each finite set occurring for only finitely many n, with h_ρ(F_n) → 0. Then h_σ(F_n) → ⟨ρ, σ⟩. In particular, for pairwise distinct x_n ∈ P¹(K̄) with h_ρ(x_n) → 0, h_σ(x_n) → ⟨ρ, σ⟩; and for normalised semipositive adelic metrics Ō₁, Ō₂ on O(1), h_{Ō₁}(x_n) → 0 implies h_{Ō₂}(x_n) → Ō₁·Ō₂.
hypotheses: ρ, σ adelic; F_n as in DY.4/equidistribution-of-small-points-on-p1.
proofSteps: Expand h_σ(F_n) = ½Σ_v r_v [(σ, σ) − 2(σ − ρ, [F_n]) − 2(ρ, [F_n]) + ([F_n], [F_n])]_v.
Σ_v r_v ([F_n], [F_n])_v = 0 (DY.4/product-formula-for-the-energy-of-a-finite-set), and from h_ρ(F_n) → 0, Σ_v 2r_v(ρ, [F_n])_v → Σ_v r_v (ρ, ρ)_v.

σ_v − ρ_v vanishes outside the finite set N(ρ) ∪ N(σ) and has a continuous potential G_v; (σ − ρ, [F_n])_v = −∫ G_v d[F_n]_v → −∫ G_v dρ_v = (σ − ρ, ρ)_v by DY.4/equidistribution-of-small-points-on-p1 and the Fubini formula (TB.6).
Combine: h_σ(F_n) → ½Σ_v r_v [(σ,σ) − 2(σ − ρ, ρ) − (ρ, ρ)] = ½Σ_v r_v (σ − ρ, σ − ρ) = ⟨ρ, σ⟩.
The metric version follows from DY.4/height-of-the-metric-of-an-adelic-measure and DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing-of-normalised-metrics.

nodes.title: Adelic measures sharing infinitely many small points coincide (Fili)
nodes.statement: Let ρ, σ be adelic measures over K, Z(ρ) := {x ∈ P¹(K̄) : h_ρ(x) ≤ 0}, and assume Z(ρ) ∪ Z(σ) is infinite. The following are equivalent: (1) ⟨ρ, σ⟩ = 0; (2) ρ = σ; (3) h_ρ = h_σ; (4) Z(ρ) = Z(σ); (5) Z(ρ) ∩ Z(σ) is infinite; (6) there are pairwise distinct x_n ∈ P¹(K̄) with h_ρ(x_n) + h_σ(x_n) → 0.
hypotheses: Z(ρ) ∪ Z(σ) infinite.
proofSteps: (1) ⇔ (2): DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing-nonnegative-and-nondegenerate. (2) ⇒ (3) ⇒ (4): immediate.
(4) ⇒ (5): Z(ρ) = Z(σ) = Z(ρ) ∪ Z(σ) is infinite.
(5) ⇒ (6): take distinct x_n ∈ Z(ρ) ∩ Z(σ); then h_ρ(x_n), h_σ(x_n) ≤ 0 and liminf of each is ≥ 0 (DY.4/essential-minimum-of-an-adelic-height), so both tend to 0.
(6) ⇒ (1): liminf h_ρ(x_n) ≥ 0 and liminf h_σ(x_n) ≥ 0 force h_ρ(x_n) → 0 and h_σ(x_n) → 0; then h_σ(x_n) → ⟨ρ, σ⟩ (DY.4/limit-of-heights-along-small-sequences), so ⟨ρ, σ⟩ = 0.
acceptance: The hypothesis cannot be dropped: over ℚ, the adelic measures with ρ_∞ the equilibrium measure of [−1, 1] and σ_∞ that of [−1/2, 1/2] (standard at finite places) have Z(ρ) = Z(σ) = ∅ but ρ ≠ σ (Fili Remark 1).
For canonical measures of rational maps the hypothesis always holds (infinitely many preperiodic points).

nodes.statement: Let φ be a semipositive adelic metric on O(1) over K. For every sequence of pairwise distinct x_n ∈ P¹(K̄), liminf_n h_φ(x_n) ≥ ½ Ō·Ō; equivalently {x ∈ P¹(K̄) : h_φ(x) ≤ b} is finite for every b < ½ Ō·Ō. In particular, for normalised semipositive Ō₁, Ō₂ and b < ½ Ō₁·Ō₂, the set {x : h_{φ₁}(x) + h_{φ₂}(x) ≤ b} is finite.
hypotheses: φ semipositive (deg O(1) = 1, so Zhang's bound L̄·L̄/(2 deg L) is ½ Ō·Ō).
proofSteps: h_φ = h_µ + ½ Ō·Ō (DY.4/height-of-a-semipositive-metric-versus-its-curvature) and liminf h_µ(x_n) ≥ 0 (DY.4/essential-minimum-of-an-adelic-height).

For the last claim apply this to the average metric (φ₁ + φ₂)/2: its height is ½(h_{φ₁} + h_{φ₂}) (AdelicMetric.height_average) and its self-pairing is ¼·0 + ½ Ō₁·Ō₂ + ¼·0 = ½ Ō₁·Ō₂ (AdelicMetric.pairing_average); so liminf (h_{φ₁} + h_{φ₂})(x_n) ≥ ½ Ō₁·Ō₂ > b.
acceptance: For the Gauss-radius metric Ō_p (self-pairing log p): h_{Ō_p}(x) ≥ h_ρ(x) + ½ log p, and all but finitely many x have h_{Ō_p}(x) > ½ log p − ε.
DKY Proposition 1.8 is the case of two Lattès heights.

nodes.title: Equidistribution of small points for semipositive adelic metrics on O_{P¹}(1)
nodes.statement: Let φ be a semipositive adelic metric on O(1) over K with curvature µ_φ, and (x_n) a generic sequence in P¹(K̄) (every point occurs for only finitely many n) that is small: h_φ(x_n) → ½ Ō·Ō. Then for every place v the Galois-orbit measures [Gal·x_n]_v converge weakly to µ_{φ,v} = c₁(Ō_v)/deg O(1). This is Yuan's theorem (DY.4/equidistribution-for-semipositive-adelic-line-bundles) for (X, L̄) = (P¹, Ō), where h_L̄(P¹) = ½ Ō·Ō.
hypotheses: φ semipositive; (x_n) generic and small.
proofSteps: h_{µ_φ}(x_n) = h_φ(x_n) − ½ Ō·Ō → 0 (DY.4/height-of-a-semipositive-metric-versus-its-curvature).
The Galois orbits of a generic sequence form a sequence of Galois-stable sets in which each set occurs finitely often (DY.4/generic-sequence).
Apply DY.4/equidistribution-of-small-points-on-p1 to the adelic measure µ_φ.
acceptance: For the standard metric this is Bilu's theorem (DY.4/bilu-equidistribution-theorem).
The canonical metric of a rational map gives DY.4/dynamical-equidistribution.
A non-generic small sequence need not equidistribute: x_n = 0 for all n, standard metric: h(0) = 0 = ½·0 but [x_n] = δ_0.

nodes.title: The adelic measure m_{F,η} and height h_{F,η} of a regularised finite set
nodes.statement: Let F ⊂ K̄ be a nonempty Galois-stable finite set and η = (η_v) positive reals with η_v = 1 for all but finitely many v. Then m_{F,η} := ([F]_{v,η_v})_v is an adelic measure, and its normalised height h_{F,η} := h_{m_{F,η}} is the height of the adelic metric with −log‖x₁‖_v(z) = α_v + |F|^{-1} Σ_{x∈F} log max(|z − x|_v, η_v), α_v = ½(m_{F,η,v}, m_{F,η,v})_v; it satisfies h_{F,η}·h_{F,η} = 0 and (m_{F,η,v}, m_{F,η,v})_v ≤ ([F]_v, [F]_v)_v + (−log η_v)/|F|.
hypotheses: F Galois-stable, finite, nonempty, ∞ ∉ F; η_v > 0, η_v = 1 for almost all v.
proofSteps: At a finite place with η_v = 1 where every x ∈ F is v-integral, ζ_{x,1} = ζ_{0,1}, so m_{F,η,v} = λ_v; this holds at all but finitely many places.
Each [F]_{v,η_v} has continuous potential (DY.4/regularised-measure-of-a-finite-set), so m_{F,η} is adelic.
The local height: φ^m_v + log⁺|z|_v = ∫ log δ_v(z, w) dm_v(w) + ½(m_v, m_v)_v = |F|^{-1}Σ_x log max(|z − x|_v, η_v) + α_v (DY.4/adelic-metric-of-an-adelic-measure).
h·h = 0 by DY.4/height-of-a-semipositive-metric-versus-its-curvature (iii); the energy bound is DY.4/regularised-self-energy-bound.
acceptance: F = {0}, η ≡ 1: m_{F,η} = λ and h_{F,η} = h.
Remark 7.2 of DKY: when Σ_v r_v α_v ≠ 0, h_{F,η} has positive essential minimum.

sources.excerpt: Then m_{F,η} = {m_{F,η,v}}_{v∈M_K} is an adelic measure in the sense of [FRL1]. It gives rise to a unique height h_{F,η} on P¹(Q̄) associated to a continuous and semipositive adelic metric on O_{P¹}(1) with curvature distributions given by m_{F,η,v} and satisfying (7.2) h_{F,η} · h_{F,η} = 0.

nodes.title: Upper bound for the pairing with a regularised finite set
nodes.statement: Let ρ be an adelic measure over K, F ⊂ K̄ a nonempty Galois-stable finite set and η as in DY.4/regularised-adelic-measure-of-a-finite-set. Then ⟨ρ, m_{F,η}⟩ ≤ h_ρ(F) + Σ_v r_v [−(ρ_v, m_{F,η,v})_v + (ρ_v, [F]_v)_v + (−log η_v)/(2|F|)].
hypotheses: ρ adelic; F, η as stated.
proofSteps: ⟨ρ, m⟩ = ½Σ_v r_v [(ρ, ρ) − 2(m, ρ) + (m, m)]_v (definition).
(m_v, m_v)_v ≤ ([F]_v, [F]_v)_v + (−log η_v)/|F| (DY.4/regularised-self-energy-bound) and Σ_v r_v ([F], [F])_v = 0 (DY.4/product-formula-for-the-energy-of-a-finite-set).
½Σ_v r_v (ρ, ρ)_v = h_ρ(∞) = h_ρ(F) + Σ_v r_v (ρ_v, [F]_v)_v (DY.4/adelic-height-decomposition).
acceptance: For ρ = m_{F,η} itself the left side is 0 and the right side is h_{F,η}(F) + Σ_v r_v [(m, [F]) − (m, m) + (−log η)/(2|F|)] ≥ 0 by the energy bound.

nodes.title: Generic sequences of algebraic points
nodes.statement: Let X be an integral scheme of finite type over K. A sequence (x_n) of points of X with values in K̄ (viewed as points of the underlying space of X) is generic if for every Zariski-closed Z ⊊ X only finitely many n satisfy x_n ∈ Z; equivalently, no infinite subsequence is contained in a proper closed subvariety of X. On a curve (in particular on P¹) a sequence is generic iff every point occurs for only finitely many n. A sequence (x_n) is small for a height h with target c if h(x_n) → c; for an adelic metrized line bundle the target is h_L̄(X).
hypotheses: X integral of finite type over K; points with values in K̄.
proofSteps: The proper closed subsets of an integral curve are the finite sets of closed points, which gives the curve criterion.
If f : X → Y is a dominant morphism and x_n ∈ X generic, then f(x_n) is generic: f(x_n) ∈ Z ⊊ Y infinitely often would put x_n in the proper closed subset f^{-1}(Z).
A subsequence of a generic sequence is generic.
acceptance: On P¹ the sequence of primitive n-th roots of unity is generic; the constant sequence 0 is not.
For f(z) = z^d the exceptional set {0, ∞} is a proper subvariety; the sequence x_n = 0 is small (ĥ_f(0) = 0) but not generic, and [x_n]_v = δ_0 does not converge to λ_v.

sources.excerpt: A sequence {x_m}_{m≥1} of algebraic points is generic if no inﬁnite subsequence of {x_m} is contained in a proper closed subvariety of P^n.
sources.match: The definition.

sources.excerpt: A sequence {x_m}_{m≥1} of algebraic points in X(K̄) is small if h_L(x_m) → h_L(X) as m → ∞.

nodes.title: Equidistribution of small points for semipositive adelic line bundles (Yuan)
nodes.statement: Let X be a projective variety of dimension n ≥ 1 over a number field K and L̄ = (L, (‖·‖_v)_v) an ample line bundle with a semipositive adelic metric (at every place a uniform limit of semipositive model metrics, and the model metric of one integral model at almost all places; TB.6). Put h_L̄(X) := ĉ₁(L̄)^{n+1}/((n + 1) deg_L X) and h_L̄(x) := ĉ₁(L̄|_x̄)/deg x. If (x_m) is a generic sequence in X(K̄) with h_L̄(x_m) → h_L̄(X), then for every place v the Galois-orbit probability measures µ_{v,x_m} converge weakly on X_v^an to c₁(L̄_v)^n / deg_L(X), a probability measure because c₁(L̄_v)^n has total mass deg_L X.
hypotheses: X projective, dim X = n ≥ 1; L ample with semipositive adelic metric; (x_m) generic and small.
proofSteps: Reduce to the geometric case over X_{C_v}^an and to test functions f that are smooth (infinite v) or model functions (finite v; Gubler's density theorem, TB.6), by Stone–Weierstrass (Yuan §3.1–3.3).
Variational principle: for ε > 0 twist the metric at v by e^{−εf}, L̄(εf); then h_{L̄(εf)}(x_m) = h_L̄(x_m) + ε ∫ f dµ_{v,x_m}.

Write O(f) as a difference of two ample metrized line bundles and apply Yuan's arithmetic Siu inequality (Theorem 2.2; Lemma 3.3) to obtain small sections of N·L̄(εf), hence liminf_m h_{L̄(εf)}(x_m) ≥ ĉ₁(L̄(εf))^{n+1}/((n+1)deg_L X) + O(ε²) for the generic sequence (Zhang's successive-minima inequality).
Expand ĉ₁(L̄(εf))^{n+1} = ĉ₁(L̄)^{n+1} + (n+1)ε ∫ f c₁(L̄_v)^n + O(ε²); divide by ε and let ε → 0⁺, then replace f by −f.

The global inputs (adelic intersection numbers, heights of subvarieties, arithmetic Siu, successive minima) are gaps G1–G2 of this packet; the local measures and model approximation come from TB.6, the analytification X_v^an from TB.0 and deg_L X from SF.5.
acceptance: For (X, L̄) = (P¹, Ō(1)) with φ semipositive the theorem is DY.4/equidistribution-for-semipositive-adelic-metrics-on-p1 (h_L̄(P¹) = ½ Ō·Ō).
For an abelian variety with the Néron–Tate metric of a symmetric ample bundle it is the Szpiro–Ullmo–Zhang theorem consumed by HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions RP.5.
Genericity cannot be dropped: torsion points of an abelian subvariety B ⊊ A equidistribute to the Haar measure of B(ℂ), not of A(ℂ).

nodes.title: The canonical adelic measure of a rational map
nodes.statement: Let f : P¹ → P¹ be a rational map of degree d ≥ 2 over K. Its canonical adelic measure is ρ_f := (µ_{f,v})_{v∈M_K}, where µ_{f,v} is the canonical measure of f on P¹_v^an (DY.2/canonical-measure). It is an adelic measure: µ_{f,v} has a continuous potential, and µ_{f,v} = λ_v at every finite place where f has good reduction, hence at all but finitely many places.
hypotheses: f of degree d ≥ 2 over K.
proofSteps: Continuous potential: µ_{f,v} = λ_v + Δ(λ_{f,v} − log⁺|z|_v) with λ_{f,v} the local canonical height and λ_{f,v} − log⁺|z|_v continuous on P¹_v^an (DY.2/canonical-measure, DY.2/local-canonical-height; FRL §6.1).

Good reduction: if a homogeneous lift F of f has v-integral coefficients and unit resultant, then max(|F₀|, |F₁|) = max(|x₀|, |x₁|)^d, the escape rate is log max(|x₀|, |x₁|), and µ_{f,v} = λ_v (PST Proposition 6; FRL §6.2).
f has good reduction at all but finitely many places (DY.0/good-reduction-of-a-rational-map).
acceptance: ρ_{z^d} = λ for every d ≥ 2.
For f(z) = (z² − z)/p over ℚ, µ_{f,p} is supported on a Cantor set of type I points in ℤ_p, so ρ_{f,p} ≠ λ_p.

sources.excerpt: Alors ρ_R = {ρ_{R,v}}_{v∈M_K} est une mesure adélique et la hauteur normalisée h_R coïncide avec la hauteur h_{ρ_R} déﬁnie par la mesure adélique ρ_R.

nodes.title: The canonical adelic metric of a rational map
nodes.statement: Let f be a rational map of degree d ≥ 2 over K with a homogeneous lift F = (F₀, F₁) over K (DY.0). Its canonical adelic metric is φ^{f,F}_v(z) := G_{F,v}(z, 1) − log⁺|z|_v, extended continuously to P¹_v^an with φ^{f,F}_v(∞) = G_{F,v}(1, 0), where G_{F,v} is the homogeneous escape rate (DY.2/escape-rate); equivalently −log‖x₁‖_{f,v}(z) = λ_{F,v}(z) = G_{F,v}(z, 1) (DY.2/local-canonical-height). It is an adelic metric (φ^{f,F}_v = 0 where F has good reduction), semipositive with curvature ρ_f, and its height is ĥ_f. Replacing F by aF (a ∈ K^×) replaces φ_v by φ_v + log|a|_v/(d − 1), a twist with Σ_v r_v log|a|_v/(d − 1) = 0.
hypotheses: f of degree d ≥ 2 over K; F a homogeneous lift over K.
proofSteps: G_{F,v}(z, w) − log max(|z|_v, |w|_v) is bounded and continuous (DY.2/escape-rate), so φ^{f,F}_v is continuous on P¹(C_v) and extends to P¹_v^an (DY.2).
At a place of good reduction of F, G_{F,v} = log max(|z|, |w|), so φ_v = 0.
Curvature: Δ(−log‖x₁‖_{f,v}) = Δλ_{F,v} = µ_{f,v} − δ_∞ (DY.2/canonical-measure), so the curvature is ρ_f (DY.4/curvature-measures-of-an-adelic-metric).
Height: ĥ_f(x) = Σ_v r_v |O|^{-1} Σ_{y∈O} G_{F,v}(ỹ) for lifts ỹ (DY.2/local-canonical-height; PST Proposition 8), which is h_{φ^{f,F}}(x) (DY.4/height-of-an-adelic-metrized-line-bundle).
Scaling: G_{aF,v} = G_{F,v} + log|a|_v/(d − 1).
acceptance: f = z^d with F = (x₀^d, x₁^d): φ = 0 and h = absLogHeight₁ = ĥ_f (ClassicalArithmeticCompletion CA.6/canonical-height-power-map).
f = z² + c, F = (x₀² + c x₁², x₁²), finite place with |c|_v > 1: φ_v(0) = G_{F,v}(0, 1) = ½ log|c|_v ≠ 0.

nodes.title: The canonical adelic metric of a rational map has self-intersection zero
nodes.statement: For a rational map f of degree d ≥ 2 over K and any lift F, Ō_{f,F}·Ō_{f,F} = 0.
hypotheses: f of degree ≥ 2 over K.
proofSteps: Choose a linear form s over K and factor F*s := s(F₀, F₁) = Π_{j=1}^d s_j into linear forms (after a finite extension of K; the pairing is unchanged). The metric identity ‖s(f(x))‖_{f,v} = Π_j ‖s_j(x)‖_{f,v} holds (RationalMap.canonicalMetric_functional_equation).

Invariance ∫ g∘f dµ_{f,v} = ∫ g dµ_{f,v} (DY.2/canonical-measure) applied to g = log‖s‖_{f,v} gives, with a second section t, ⟨f, f⟩_{s,t,v} − log‖s(div t)‖_{f,v} = Σ_j (⟨f, f⟩_{s_j,t,v} − log‖s_j(div t)‖_{f,v}) (PST Proposition 10).

Summing over places with DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing-independent-of-sections: Ō·Ō − ĥ_f(div s) = d·Ō·Ō − Σ_j ĥ_f(div s_j); since f(div s_j) = div s, ĥ_f(div s) = d ĥ_f(div s_j) (DY.1), so Ō·Ō = d·Ō·Ō, i.e. Ō·Ō = 0.
acceptance: f = z^d: the standard metric has self-intersection 0.

For f = z² + c the identity gives Σ_v r_v [2φ_v(∞) − (µ_{f,v}, µ_{f,v})_v] = 0 with φ_v(∞) = 0 (∞ is fixed with G_F(1, 0) = 0), so Σ_v r_v (µ_{f,v}, µ_{f,v})_v = 0: the adelic filled Julia set has capacity 1.

sources.match: The statement.

sources.excerpt: Since h_ϕ(div(s)) = h_ϕ(ϕ(div(s_j))) = dh_ϕ(div(s_j)) for each j, we deduce that ⟨ϕ, ϕ⟩ = d⟨ϕ, ϕ⟩, whereby ⟨ϕ, ϕ⟩ = 0.
sources.match: The conclusion.

nodes.title: The canonical height of a rational map is the adelic height of its canonical measures
nodes.statement: For a rational map f of degree d ≥ 2 over K, ĥ_f = h_{ρ_f} on P¹(K̄); equivalently ĥ_f is the height of the normalised adelic metric Ō^{ρ_f}, and Ō_{f,F} = Ō^{ρ_f} + c with Σ_v r_v c_v = 0 for every lift F.
hypotheses: f of degree ≥ 2 over K.
proofSteps: The canonical metric Ō_{f,F} is semipositive with curvature ρ_f and height ĥ_f (DY.4/canonical-adelic-metric-of-a-rational-map), and Ō_{f,F}·Ō_{f,F} = 0 (DY.4/canonical-metric-self-intersection-zero).
By DY.4/height-of-a-semipositive-metric-versus-its-curvature, ĥ_f = h_{Ō_{f,F}} = h_{ρ_f} + ½ Ō_{f,F}·Ō_{f,F} = h_{ρ_f}, and φ^{f,F} = φ^{ρ_f} + c with Σ_v r_v c_v = ½·0 = 0.
acceptance: f = z^d: ρ_f = λ and ĥ_f = h (Bilu's setting).
Consequence: h_{ρ_f}(∞) = ĥ_f(∞) = ½Σ_v r_v (µ_{f,v}, µ_{f,v})_v; for a polynomial this is 0.

sources.excerpt: Soit R une fraction rationnelle de degré au moins 2 et à coefﬁcients dans K. Pour chaque place v de K soit ρ_{R,v} la mesure d'équilibre de R correspondante. Alors ρ_R = {ρ_{R,v}}_{v∈M_K} est une mesure adélique et la hauteur normalisée h_R coïncide avec la hauteur h_{ρ_R}

sources.excerpt: When ρ = (ρ_{φ,v})_{v∈M_K} is the adelic set of canonical measures associated to iteration of a rational map φ, then by [9, Thm. 4] we have h_ρ = h_φ is the usual Call-Silverman dynamical height [7].

nodes.title: Equidistribution of dynamically small points
nodes.statement: Let f be a rational map of degree d ≥ 2 over K and (x_n) a sequence of pairwise distinct points of P¹(K̄) with ĥ_f(x_n) → 0. Then for every place v the Galois-orbit measures [Gal·x_n]_v converge weakly to the canonical measure µ_{f,v} on P¹_v^an. More generally the same holds for finite Galois-stable F_n ⊂ P¹(K̄), each set occurring finitely often, with |F_n|^{-1} Σ_{x∈F_n} ĥ_f(x) → 0.
hypotheses: f of degree ≥ 2 over K; x_n pairwise distinct (a generic sequence on P¹).
proofSteps: ĥ_f = h_{ρ_f} (DY.4/canonical-height-is-an-adelic-height), and h_{ρ_f}(F) is the average of h_{ρ_f} over F (AdelicMeasure.height_eq_average).
Apply DY.4/equidistribution-of-small-points-on-p1 to ρ_f.
acceptance: Any sequence of distinct preperiodic points (ĥ_f = 0) equidistributes to µ_{f,v}; for f = z² the roots of unity equidistribute on the unit circle and to the Gauss point at finite places.

For a Lattès map f_E of an elliptic curve E/K, the x-coordinates of torsion points of E (preperiodic for f_E; ĥ_E = ½ĥ_{f_E}∘x with Tau Ceti's WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.canonicalHeight) equidistribute to the pushforward of Haar measure at every infinite place (the Lattès map itself is built in DY.6/lattes-map).
The exceptional-set test: for f = z^d the constant sequence x_n = 0 is small but not generic, and [x_n]_v = δ_0 ≠ µ_{f,v} = λ_v.

sources.excerpt: Suppose z_n is a sequence of distinct points of P¹(k̄) with ĥ_ϕ(z_n) → 0. For v ∈ M_k, let δ_n be the discrete probability measure on the Berkovich space P¹_{Berk,v}/C_v supported equally on the Galois conjugates of z_n. Then the sequence of measures δ_n converges weakly to µ_{ϕ,v} for all v ∈ M_k.

nodes.title: Equidistribution of iterated preimages
nodes.statement: Let f be a rational map of degree d ≥ 2 over K and z₀ ∈ P¹(K̄) with infinite backward orbit ⋃_n f^{-n}(Gal·z₀) (z₀ not exceptional). Then the sets F_n := f^{-n}(Gal·z₀) are Galois-stable and pairwise distinct, and [F_n]_v → µ_{f,v} weakly at every place v.
hypotheses: z₀ non-exceptional; F_n taken as sets (without multiplicity).
proofSteps: F_n is Galois-stable because f is defined over K; every y ∈ F_n has ĥ_f(y) = d^{-n} ĥ_f(z₀) (DY.1), so ĥ_f-averages tend to 0.
If F_n = F_m for some n < m, then F_n = f^{-(m−n)}(F_n) is a finite totally invariant set for f^{m−n}, so the backward orbit of z₀ would be finite; hence the F_n are pairwise distinct.
Apply DY.4/dynamical-equidistribution.
acceptance: f = z², z₀ = 2: the 2ⁿ-th roots of 2 equidistribute on the unit circle.
f = z^d, z₀ = 0 is exceptional (f^{-n}(0) = {0}) and the conclusion fails.

sources.excerpt: Pour n ≥ 1, notons F_n le sous-ensemble des solutions dans K̄ à l'équation R^n = S. Si pour n grand les ensembles F_n sont distincts deux à deux, alors pour toute place v ∈ M_K, on a lim_{n→∞} [F_n] = ρ_{R,v} .
sources.match: The statement (S constant).

sources.excerpt: Lorsque z₀ ∈ K n'est pas exceptionnel pour R et lorsque la fraction rationnelle S est constante égale à z₀, on sait que les ensembles F_n sont distincts deux à deux.

nodes.title: Equidistribution of periodic points
nodes.statement: Let f be a rational map of degree d ≥ 2 over K and Fix(f^n) ⊂ P¹(K̄) the set of solutions of f^n(z) = z. For every strictly increasing sequence (n_k) along which the sets Fix(f^{n_k}) are pairwise distinct, [Fix(f^{n_k})]_v → µ_{f,v} weakly at every place v. Such sequences exist (for instance a subsequence of n_k = k! along which Fix(f^{k!}) strictly increases), because f has infinitely many periodic points.
hypotheses: f of degree ≥ 2; (n_k) with pairwise distinct sets.
proofSteps: Fix(f^n) is Galois-stable and its points are preperiodic, so ĥ_f = 0 on it (DY.1/zero-canonical-height-iff-preperiodic).
Apply DY.4/dynamical-equidistribution.
Existence: Fix(f^{k!}) ⊆ Fix(f^{(k+1)!}) and the union is the infinite set of periodic points (DY.3: infinitely many periodic points), so the chain increases strictly infinitely often.
acceptance: f = z²: Fix(f^n) = {0, ∞} ∪ μ_{2ⁿ−1}; along n_k = k these sets are pairwise distinct and equidistribute on the unit circle.
FRL assert pairwise distinctness for all large n; that needs I. N. Baker's theorem on exact periods (sourceIssues E505).

sources.excerpt: Lorsque S(z) = z, l'ensemble F_n est égal à l'ensemble des points périodiques de R dans K̄, de période n. Dans ce cas les ensembles F_n sont distincts deux à deux (pour n grand) et on obtient l'équidistribution des points périodiques de R selon la mesure d'équilibre.

nodes.title: The Arakelov–Zhang pairing of two rational maps
nodes.statement: For rational maps f, g of degrees ≥ 2 over K, ⟨f, g⟩ := ⟨ρ_f, ρ_g⟩ = ½ Σ_v r_v (µ_{f,v} − µ_{g,v}, µ_{f,v} − µ_{g,v})_v, which equals the Arakelov–Zhang pairing Ō_{f,F}·Ō_{g,G} of the canonical adelic metrics for any lifts F, G (Petsche–Szpiro–Tucker). The local terms E_v(f, g) := ½(µ_{f,v} − µ_{g,v}, µ_{f,v} − µ_{g,v})_v are the local dynamical energies of DY.4/local-dynamical-energy.
hypotheses: f, g of degree ≥ 2 over K.
proofSteps: The canonical metrics have self-intersection 0 and curvatures ρ_f, ρ_g (DY.4/canonical-metric-self-intersection-zero, DY.4/canonical-adelic-metric-of-a-rational-map), so Ō_f·Ō_g = ⟨ρ_f, ρ_g⟩ by DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing-of-normalised-metrics.
The value does not depend on K or on the lifts (twists with Σ r_v c_v = 0).
acceptance: ⟨z², z³⟩ = 0 (both canonical adelic measures are λ).

nodes.title: The local dynamical energy of two rational maps
nodes.statement: For rational maps f, g of degree ≥ 2 over K and a place v, E_v(f, g) := ½(µ_{f,v} − µ_{g,v}, µ_{f,v} − µ_{g,v})_v. Equivalently E_v(f, g) = ½(∫ (λ_{f,v} − λ_{g,v}) dµ_{g,v} + ∫ (λ_{g,v} − λ_{f,v}) dµ_{f,v}) for local canonical heights λ_{f,v}, λ_{g,v} (any normalisation). E_v(f, g) ≥ 0 with equality iff µ_{f,v} = µ_{g,v}, E_v = 0 for all but finitely many v, and ⟨f, g⟩ = Σ_v r_v E_v(f, g).
hypotheses: f, g of degree ≥ 2 over K; v a place.
proofSteps: λ_{f,v} − λ_{g,v} is a continuous potential of µ_{f,v} − µ_{g,v} up to an additive constant (DY.2/canonical-measure), so (µ_f − µ_g, µ_f − µ_g)_v = −∫ (λ_f − λ_g) d(µ_f − µ_g) (Fubini, TB.6), which is the displayed formula; constants integrate to 0 against a mass-zero measure.
Positivity and nondegeneracy: TB.6 (FRL Propositions 2.6, 4.5).
Where both maps have good reduction, µ_f = µ_g = λ_v.
acceptance: E_v(z², z³) = 0 at every place.

For σ_α(z) = α − (α − z)²: E_v(z², σ_α) = log⁺|α|_v at a finite place (the hyperbolic distance from ζ_{0,1} to ζ_{α,1} is 2 log⁺|α|_v) and log⁺|α|_v + I(|α|_v) at an infinite place, I as in PST Lemma 17.

nodes.title: Vanishing criterion for the dynamical Arakelov–Zhang pairing
nodes.statement: For rational maps f, g of degree ≥ 2 over K, ⟨f, g⟩ ≥ 0, and the following are equivalent: (a) ⟨f, g⟩ = 0; (b) ĥ_f = ĥ_g on P¹(K̄); (c) Preper(f) = Preper(g); (d) Preper(f) ∩ Preper(g) is infinite; (e) there are pairwise distinct x_n ∈ P¹(K̄) with ĥ_f(x_n) + ĥ_g(x_n) → 0; (f) µ_{f,v} = µ_{g,v} for every place v.
hypotheses: f, g of degree ≥ 2 over K.
proofSteps: Nonnegativity and (a) ⇔ (f): DY.4/arakelov-zhang-pairing-nonnegative-and-nondegenerate for ρ_f, ρ_g.
(f) ⇒ (b): ĥ_f = h_{ρ_f} = h_{ρ_g} = ĥ_g (DY.4/canonical-height-is-an-adelic-height).
(b) ⇒ (c): preperiodic points are exactly the zeros of the canonical height (DY.1/zero-canonical-height-iff-preperiodic).
(c) ⇒ (d): Preper(f) is infinite (DY.3: infinitely many periodic points). (d) ⇒ (e): take distinct common preperiodic points.
(e) ⇒ (a): ĥ_f, ĥ_g ≥ 0, so both tend to 0, and ĥ_f(x_n) → ⟨f, g⟩ (DY.4/heights-of-small-points-of-another-map).
acceptance: f = z², g = z³: all conditions hold (Preper = {0, ∞} ∪ roots of unity).
f = z², g = z² − 2 (Chebyshev): µ_{g,∞} is the arcsine measure on [−2, 2], so ⟨f, g⟩ > 0, and Preper(f) ∩ Preper(g) = {∞, 0, 1, −1} (the real numbers ζ + ζ^{-1} that are 0 or roots of unity).

nodes.title: Periodic-point averages counted with multiplicity (Petsche–Szpiro–Tucker Theorem 2)
nodes.statement: For rational maps f, g of degree ≥ 2 over K with d = deg g, Σ(f, g) := lim_{n→∞} (dⁿ + 1)^{-1} Σ_{g^n(x)=x} ĥ_f(x), the sum over the dⁿ + 1 solutions counted with multiplicity, exists and equals ⟨f, g⟩.
hypotheses: Solutions of g^n(x) = x counted with multiplicity.
proofSteps: Let e_n := dⁿ + 1 − |Fix(gⁿ)| be the multiplicity excess. A solution has multiplicity > 1 only if it lies on a periodic cycle whose multiplier λ satisfies λ^{n/k} = 1 (k the exact period; DY.2/multiplier-of-a-periodic-cycle), and its multiplicity as a fixed point of gⁿ is bounded independently of n.

nodes.title: Upper bound for ĥ_ψ − h through the pairing with the squaring map
nodes.statement: For a rational map ψ of degree ≥ 2 over K and every x ∈ P¹(K̄): ĥ_ψ(x) − h(x) ≤ ⟨z², ψ⟩ + log 2. In particular ĥ_ψ(x) − h(x) ≤ ⟨z², ψ⟩ + ĥ_ψ(∞) + log 2 (Petsche–Szpiro–Tucker Theorem 15, whose bound is weaker by ĥ_ψ(∞) ≥ 0).
hypotheses: ψ of degree ≥ 2 over K; h the Weil height with h(∞) = 0.
proofSteps: For x ∈ K̄ with orbit O: ĥ_ψ(x) − h(x) = h_{ρ_ψ}(∞) + Σ_v r_v |O|^{-1} Σ_{y∈O} [∫ log δ_v(y, w) dµ_{ψ,v}(w) − log⁺|y|_v] (DY.4/canonical-height-is-an-adelic-height, DY.4/adelic-height-decomposition, DY.4/standard-adelic-height-is-the-weil-height).
log δ_v(y, w) ≤ log⁺|y|_v + log⁺|w|_v + θ_v with θ_v = log 2 at infinite places and 0 at finite places (triangle, resp. ultrametric, inequality for the kernel).
Hence ĥ_ψ(x) − h(x) ≤ h_{ρ_ψ}(∞) + Σ_v r_v ∫ log⁺|w|_v dµ_{ψ,v} + log 2 = ⟨λ, ρ_ψ⟩ + log 2 (DY.4/pairing-with-the-standard-measure; Σ_{v|∞} r_v = 1), and ⟨λ, ρ_ψ⟩ = ⟨z², ψ⟩.
At x = ∞: ĥ_ψ(∞) = h_{ρ_ψ}(∞) ≤ ⟨λ, ρ_ψ⟩ since the log⁺ integrals are ≥ 0.

nodes.title: Hölder continuity of the potential of a canonical measure
nodes.statement: Let f be a rational map of degree d ≥ 2 over C_v (any place v) with lift F, and g_{f,v} the continuous potential of µ_{f,v} − λ_v (g_{f,v}(z) = G_{F,v}(z, 1) − log⁺|z|_v up to an additive constant). Then g_{f,v} is κ-Hölder for the chordal metric of P¹_v^an with κ = log d / log M, where M > d is a Lipschitz constant of f for that metric; consequently ω_{g_{f,v}}(r) ≤ C r^κ.
hypotheses: d ≥ 2; M > d a Lipschitz constant of f for the chordal metric (TB.1 at finite places).
proofSteps: g₁ := the potential of d^{−1} f^*λ_v − λ_v, i.e. g₁(x) = d^{−1} log‖F(x)‖_v − log‖x‖_v on lifts, is Lipschitz for the chordal metric (smooth on the Riemann sphere; at finite places by the explicit form of ‖F(x)‖ on the Berkovich line, TB.1).
g_{f,v} = Σ_{k≥0} d^{−k} g₁∘f^k up to a constant (telescoping the escape rate, DY.2/escape-rate), the series converging uniformly.
For N ≥ 0: |g(z) − g(w)| ≤ Σ_{k<N} d^{−k} Lip(g₁) M^k d(z, w) + 2 sup|g₁| Σ_{k≥N} d^{−k} ≤ C₁ (M/d)^N d(z, w) + C₂ d^{−N}; choose N with (M/d)^N d(z, w) ≈ d^{−N} to get C d(z, w)^κ.
The chordal distance between ι x and a point of the circle measure m_{x,r} is at most r, so ω_g(r) ≤ C r^κ.
acceptance: f = z^d: g = 0.
For f = z² + c at a finite place with |c|_v > 1 the potential is locally constant off the Julia set and the bound holds with κ = log 2/log M.

nodes.title: The adelic Multibrot measure
nodes.statement: Fix D ≥ 2 and put P_c(z) = z^D + c. For a place v of ℚ (or of K ⊇ ℚ) let G_{M,v}(c) := lim_{n→∞} D^{−(n−1)} log⁺|P_cⁿ(0)|_v. At a finite place G_{M,v}(c) = log⁺|c|_v; at the infinite place G_M is continuous on ℂ, harmonic off the Multibrot set M_D = {c : (P_cⁿ(0))_n bounded}, zero on M_D, and G_M(c) = log|c| + o(1) as c → ∞ (M_D has logarithmic capacity 1). The family µ_{M_D} := (λ_v + Δ(G_{M,v} − log⁺|c|_v))_v — the harmonic (equilibrium) measure of M_D at the infinite place and λ_v at finite places — is an adelic measure with Hölder potentials, and ∫ log|c − w| dµ_{M_D,∞}(w) = G_M(c).
hypotheses: D ≥ 2; the normalisation D^{−(n−1)} corrects FRL Lemma 6.3 (sourceIssues E503).
proofSteps: Finite place: if |c|_v ≤ 1 all P_cⁿ(0) are v-integral; if |c|_v > 1, |P_cⁿ(0)|_v = |c|_v^{D^{n−1}} by induction, so G_{M,v}(c) = log⁺|c|_v and µ_{M,v} = λ_v.

Infinite place: G_M(c) = G_{P_c}(c) = D·G_{P_c}(0) for the escape rate of P_c (DY.2/escape-rate); the telescoping estimate |D^{-n} log⁺|P_c^{n+1}(0)| − D^{−(n−1)} log⁺|P_cⁿ(0)|| ≤ D^{-n} log(1 + |c|) gives locally uniform convergence and continuity.
G_M = 0 on M_D, G_M > 0 and harmonic off M_D (a locally uniform limit of harmonic functions where P_cⁿ(0) → ∞), and G_M(c) − log|c| → 0 at ∞ (|P_cⁿ(0)| = |c|^{D^{n−1}}(1 + o(1))).

Hence ΔG_M = µ_{M,∞} − δ_∞ with µ_{M,∞} a probability measure on ∂M_D (TB.6, archimedean Laplacian); the potential u(c) = ∫ log|c − w| dµ_{M,∞}(w) has the same Laplacian, so u − G_M is constant, and the constant is 0 because both are log|c| + o(1) at ∞: µ_{M,∞} is the equilibrium measure of M_D and M_D has capacity 1.

Hölder continuity of G_M: G_M(c) = D·G_{P_c}(0) and the escape rate is jointly Hölder in (c, z) on compact sets by the argument of FRL Proposition 6.5 (Lipschitz one-step estimate for (c, z) ↦ z^D + c, then optimisation of the truncation).
acceptance: G_{M,p}(c) = log⁺|c|_p at every prime p.

nodes.title: Critical height as an adelic height and equidistribution of PCF maps in moduli (Gauthier; Yuan–Zhang)
nodes.statement: Let d ≥ 2, M_d^cm the critically marked moduli space with its family f of degree-d maps and marked critical points c₁, …, c_{2d−2} (DY.0/moduli-space-of-rational-maps), and ĥ_crit([f]) := Σ_{i=1}^{2d−2} ĥ_f(c_i(f)) for [f] ∈ M_d^cm(ℚ̄) (DY.1 canonical heights; the critical height of DY.6). (a) ĥ_crit is the height of a nondegenerate nef adelic line bundle on the quasi-projective variety M_d^cm over ℚ̄ in the sense of Yuan–Zhang, the restriction to the ramification divisor of the f-invariant extension of O(1) on M_d^cm × P¹, with archimedean curvature the bifurcation current T_bif. (b) For every generic sequence of postcritically finite parameters in M_d^cm(ℚ̄), the Galois-orbit measures at the infinite place converge to the normalised bifurcation measure T_bif^{∧(2d−2)}/mass.
hypotheses: d ≥ 2; generic sequences in the sense of DY.4/generic-sequence on M_d^cm.
proofSteps: (a) Construct the invariant extension of O(1) on M_d^cm × P¹ and restrict to the graphs of the critical points (Yuan–Zhang §6.3): gap G3.
Its archimedean curvature is T_bif = Σ_i π_*(T̂_f ∧ [Γ_{c_i}]) and T_bif^{∧(2d−2)} ≠ 0 (Bassanelli–Berteloot), which gives nondegeneracy: gap G4.

(b) Apply the Yuan–Zhang equidistribution theorem for nondegenerate nef adelic line bundles on quasi-projective varieties [YZ, Theorem 5.4.3] (gap G3) to PCF parameters, which have ĥ_crit = 0 (DY.1/zero-canonical-height-iff-preperiodic).
The polynomial one-parameter slice z^D + c is DY.4/equidistribution-of-pcf-parameters, proved without these inputs.

nodes.title: Level towers and rooted trees
nodes.statement: A level tower T is a sequence of sets (V_n)_{n≥0} (the vertices at level n) with parent maps π_n : V_{n+1} → V_n. The ancestor map at level k of a vertex at level k + j is π_k ∘ ⋯ ∘ π_{k+j−1} (the identity for j = 0); the children of v ∈ V_n are the elements of π_n^{-1}(v). T is a rooted tree when V_0 is a single point; its vertices are ⊔_n V_n and its edges join x ∈ V_{n+1} to π_n(x). T is d-regular (d ∈ ℕ) when V_0 has exactly one element, every V_n is finite, and every vertex has exactly d children. A morphism T → T' is a family of maps V_n → V'_n commuting with the parent maps; an isomorphism is a family of bijections commuting with the parent maps.
hypotheses: No hypotheses: any family of types and maps is a level tower. Regularity is a separate predicate.
Pinned convention: levels are indexed from the root, V_0 being the root level; the parent map goes down one level.
proofSteps: Structure with two fields (V, parent); ancestor by recursion on j; children as a fibre; IsRegular as the conjunction of the three conditions; Hom and Iso as structures of levelwise maps with the commutation field.
card_level_of_isRegular: induction on n, V_{n+1} is the disjoint union over v ∈ V_n of the children of v (the fibres of π_n), each of cardinality d, so Nat.card V_{n+1} = d · Nat.card V_n.
parent_surjective_of_isRegular: a fibre of cardinality d ≥ 1 is nonempty.
acceptance: A 2-regular tower has 8 vertices at level 3; a 1-regular tower has one vertex at each level.
The tower with levels Fin (n + 1) and every vertex sent to the last vertex below is regular of no degree.

uses.how: the preimage tree T_∞(α) with vertex set ⊔ φ^{-n}(α) and edges given by φ is a rooted tree graded by level; Aut(T_n) and Aut(T_∞) are automorphisms of such trees
rooted forests graded by the distance to a root carry the Galois action; a level tower with arbitrary V_0 is exactly a graded rooted forest

nodes.title: The automorphism group Aut(T) of a level tower and its profinite topology

planet.name: Automorphism group of a rooted tree

nodes.statement: For a level tower T, Aut(T) is the group of families (σ_n)_{n≥0} with σ_n a permutation of V_n and π_n ∘ σ_{n+1} = σ_n ∘ π_n for all n, under levelwise composition; it is a subgroup of ∏_n Perm(V_n). It acts on each level through levelHom n : Aut(T) → Perm(V_n). Its topology is the subspace topology from the product ∏_n Perm(V_n) with each factor discrete (the topology of pointwise convergence on the vertex set). When every V_n is finite, Aut(T) is a compact, Hausdorff, totally disconnected topological group, i.e. a profinite group, and the kernels of the levelHom n form a basis of open neighbourhoods of 1.
hypotheses: Profiniteness (compactness) needs every level finite; the topological group structure, Hausdorffness and total disconnectedness hold for every T.
proofSteps: autSubgroup: the compatibility condition is closed under composition, identity and inverses (for inverses apply σ_n^{-1} to both sides).
Topological group: induced from the product of discrete groups, a topological group (Pi.topologicalSpace with the discrete topology on each Perm(V_n)).
Hausdorff and totally disconnected: the product of discrete spaces is, and so is any subspace.

Compactness for finite levels: the compatibility conditions are closed (each is an equality of values in a discrete space depending on finitely many coordinates), and ∏_n Perm(V_n) is compact by Tychonoff (finite discrete factors).
Aut.ext_iff': equality of families is levelwise equality.
Iso.autCongr: conjugation by the levelwise bijections of an isomorphism.
acceptance: Aut(T¹) is trivial; Aut(T²) → Perm(V_1) is onto Perm(V_1) ≅ S_2; the transposition of the leaves (0,0), (0,1) of T², which have different parents, is not in the image of levelHom 2.

nodes.title: The automorphism group Aut(T_n) of the tree truncated at level n
nodes.statement: For a level tower T and n ∈ ℕ, Aut(T_n) is the subgroup of ∏_{k=0}^{n} Perm(V_k) of families (σ_0, …, σ_n) with π_k ∘ σ_{k+1} = σ_k ∘ π_k for k < n. It comes with: restriction Aut(T_{n+1}) → Aut(T_n) (forget σ_{n+1}); truncation Aut(T) → Aut(T_n); the action toLevelPerm on the top level V_n, which is injective when every parent map is surjective; and, for finite levels, the level signs χ_k = sign ∘ (k-th component) : Aut(T_n) → {±1}, k = 0, …, n.
hypotheses: Injectivity of toLevelPerm needs surjective parent maps (true for d-regular towers with d ≥ 1).
Surjectivity of restriction and of truncation needs regularity (every automorphism of the truncated tree extends).
proofSteps: truncAut: subgroup, as for autSubgroup, with the finitely many conditions k < n.
restrict: σ ↦ (σ_0, …, σ_n); the conditions for k < n are among those for k < n + 1.
toLevelPerm_injective: if σ_n = τ_n then σ_k = τ_k for k < n, because π_k ∘ ⋯ is surjective onto V_k and σ_k ∘ ancestor = ancestor ∘ σ_n.
Aut.truncate: σ ↦ (σ_0, …, σ_n).

For the binary tree, Aut(T_n) ≅ IteratedWreathProduct (Multiplicative (ZMod 2)) n (Mathlib), of order 2^{2ⁿ−1}.

nodes.title: Every d-regular level tower is isomorphic to T^d
nodes.statement: If T is a d-regular level tower then there is an isomorphism of level towers T ≅ T^d. Consequently Aut(T) ≃* Aut(T^d) and Aut(T_n) ≃* Aut(T^d_n) for every n, compatibly with restriction and truncation; the isomorphisms are unique up to conjugation by Aut(T^d).

Commutation: Fin.tail (e_{n+1} x) = e_n (π x) by construction; bijectivity from the fibrewise bijections.

nodes.title: Aut(T) is the inverse limit of the finite groups Aut(T_n)
nodes.statement: Let T be d-regular. For every family (s_n)_{n≥0} with s_n ∈ Aut(T_n) and restrict(s_{n+1}) = s_n there is a unique σ ∈ Aut(T) with truncate_n(σ) = s_n for all n. Together with the profinite topology of Aut(T), this identifies Aut(T) with lim_n Aut(T_n) as a topological group (each Aut(T_n) finite discrete). In particular a closed subgroup H ≤ Aut(T) whose truncations are all of Aut(T_n) is Aut(T).
hypotheses: T is d-regular (finite levels).
proofSteps: Existence: σ_n := (s_n)_n (the top component); compatibility π_n ∘ σ_{n+1} = σ_n ∘ π_n holds in s_{n+1}. Uniqueness: an element of Aut(T) is determined by its levelwise components (Aut.ext_iff').

Topology: the map Aut(T) → ∏_n Aut(T_n) is a continuous injective group homomorphism from a compact space (Aut.compactSpace) to a Hausdorff space, with image the compatible families, hence a homeomorphism onto the inverse limit.
Closed subgroups: if H is closed and truncate_n(H) = Aut(T_n) for all n, every σ is a limit of elements of H (agree with σ on levels ≤ n), so σ ∈ H.
acceptance: For T¹ both sides are trivial.

nodes.title: The characters of Aut(T_n) for binary trees are products of level signs
nodes.statement: Let T be 2-regular and n ∈ ℕ. For every homomorphism χ : Aut(T_n) → {±1} there is a unique subset S ⊆ {1, …, n} with χ = ∏_{k∈S} χ_k, where χ_k is the sign of the permutation induced on level k. Equivalently Hom(Aut(T_n), {±1}) has exactly 2ⁿ elements and the level signs χ_1, …, χ_n form an F_2-basis of it; the largest elementary abelian 2-quotient of Aut(T_n) ≅ [C_2]^n is C_2^n.
hypotheses: T is binary (2-regular). The levels are finite, so the signs are defined.
proofSteps: Transport to T² along regular-tower-isomorphism (signs are invariant under relabelling).

Count: for a regular wreath product D ≀ Q and abelian A, a homomorphism D ≀ Q → A is determined by a pair of homomorphisms D → A, Q → A (on the base D^Q it takes equal values on conjugate coordinates); by the wreath recursion Aut(T²_{n+1}) ≅ Aut(T²_n) ≀ C_2, #Hom(Aut(T²_{n+1}), ±1) = 2 · #Hom(Aut(T²_n), ±1), so the count is 2ⁿ.

Independence: for each 1 ≤ k ≤ n let σ_k swap the two subtrees below one vertex at level k − 1 (fixing everything else); it acts trivially on the levels j < k, by one transposition on level k and by 2^{j−k} disjoint transpositions on each level j > k, so χ_k(σ_k) = −1 and χ_j(σ_k) = 1 for j ≠ k.
An independent family of n elements in an F_2-space of cardinality 2ⁿ is a basis; uniqueness of S follows.

nodes.title: The preimage tree T_∞(g, α) of a point under a self-map
nodes.statement: For a set X, a map g : X → X and α ∈ X, the preimage tree T(g, α) is the level tower with V_n = g^{-n}(α) = {x ∈ X : g^n(x) = α} and parent map x ↦ g(x) (which sends V_{n+1} to V_n). Its root level V_0 is {α}. For a field K, f ∈ K[x], α ∈ K and a field L ⊇ K, the polynomial preimage tree T(f, α; L) is T(g, α) with X = L and g(y) = f(y) (evaluation); its level n is the root set of fⁿ(x) − α in L, where fⁿ is the n-fold composite f.comp^[n] X. The arboreal tree of the sources is T(f, α; K^sep) under the non-collision condition (DY.5/preimage-tree-regular).
hypotheses: No hypotheses for the definition; regularity is the theorem DY.5/preimage-tree-regular.
Pinned convention: fⁿ denotes composition iterates (f.comp^[n] X, with f⁰ = X), never powers.
proofSteps: Level n is the subtype {x // g^[n] x = α}; parent x := g x, with g^[n] (g x) = g^[n+1] x = α (Function.iterate_succ_apply).

nodes.title: The chain rule for polynomial iterates
nodes.statement: For a commutative semiring R, f ∈ R[x] and n ∈ ℕ: (fⁿ)' = ∏_{i=0}^{n−1} f'(fⁱ(x)), where fⁿ = f.comp^[n] X.
hypotheses: None.
proofSteps: Induction on n. n = 0: (X)' = 1 = empty product.
Step: f^{n+1} = f.comp (fⁿ) (Function.iterate_succ_apply'), so (f^{n+1})' = (fⁿ)' · f'.comp (fⁿ) by Polynomial.derivative_comp; apply the induction hypothesis and Finset.prod_range_succ.

nodes.title: Non-collision: fⁿ − α is separable iff no critical point reaches α
nodes.statement: Let K be a field, f ∈ K[x] with deg f ≥ 1, α ∈ K and n ≥ 1. Then fⁿ(x) − α is separable if and only if for every c ∈ K̄ with f'(c) = 0 and every 1 ≤ k ≤ n, f^k(c) ≠ α. Hence fⁿ − α is separable for all n ≥ 1 iff α does not lie in the forward orbit {f^k(c) : k ≥ 1, f'(c) = 0} of the critical points (the non-collision condition). If f' = 0 (f inseparable) every c ∈ K̄ is critical and both sides fail.
hypotheses: deg f ≥ 1.
Critical points are the roots of f' in an algebraic closure, with the convention that every point is a root of the zero polynomial.
proofSteps: fⁿ − α splits over K̄ with roots z (f^n(z) = α); it is separable iff its roots are simple (Polynomial.nodup_roots_iff_of_splits), iff no root z has (fⁿ)'(z) = 0.
By derivative-of-iterate, (fⁿ)'(z) = ∏_{i<n} f'(fⁱ(z)); it vanishes iff c := fⁱ(z) is critical for some i < n, and then f^{n−i}(c) = α with 1 ≤ n − i ≤ n.
Conversely if f'(c) = 0 and f^k(c) = α with 1 ≤ k ≤ n, choose z ∈ K̄ with f^{n−k}(z) = c (K̄ algebraically closed, deg f ≥ 1); z is a multiple root.
acceptance: f = x² + 1 over ℚ, α = 0: the critical point 0 has orbit 1, 2, 5, 26, …, never 0, so every fⁿ is separable.
f = x² − 2 over ℚ, α = 2: f(0) = −2, f²(0) = 2 = α, so f² − 2 is inseparable (it equals x²(x² − 4)).

sources.excerpt: One consequence of Lemma 2.8 is that g ◦f n is separable for all n if and only if g is separable and 0 is not contained in the forward orbit of any critical point of f.

nodes.title: Under non-collision the preimage tree is the complete d-ary tree
nodes.statement: Let K be a field, f ∈ K[x] of degree d ≥ 1 and α ∈ K with fⁿ(x) − α separable for every n. Then for every field L ⊇ K over which every fⁿ − α splits (for example L = K^sep or L = K̄), the preimage tree T(f, α; L) is d-regular: level n has dⁿ elements and every vertex has exactly d children. Hence T(f, α; L) ≅ T^d.
hypotheses: fⁿ − α separable for all n (equivalently the non-collision condition of DY.5/separable-iterates-criterion).
Every fⁿ − α splits over L.
proofSteps: |V_n| = |rootSet (fⁿ − α) L| = deg(fⁿ − α) = dⁿ (Polynomial.card_rootSet_eq_natDegree, separability and splitting; Polynomial.natDegree_iterate_comp).

Children of β ∈ V_n: the roots of f(x) − β in L. Over L, f^{n+1} − α = (fⁿ − α) ∘ f = c ∏_{β ∈ V_n} (f(x) − β); since f^{n+1} − α is separable and splits, so does each factor f − β (Polynomial.Separable.of_dvd), which has degree d, hence exactly d roots.
The isomorphism with T^d is regular-tower-isomorphism.

f = x² over ℚ, α = 0: fⁿ = x^{2ⁿ} is inseparable and level n is {0}, so the hypothesis fails and so does the conclusion.

nodes.title: Affine conjugation does not change the preimage tree or its Galois action
nodes.statement: Let K ⊆ L be fields, f ∈ K[x], α ∈ K and h(x) = ux + v with u, v ∈ K, u ≠ 0. Put ψ = h^{-1} ∘ f ∘ h = u^{-1}(f(ux + v) − v) and α' = h^{-1}(α) = u^{-1}(α − v). Then y ↦ h^{-1}(y) is an isomorphism of level towers T(f, α; L) ≅ T(ψ, α'; L) commuting with the action of Gal(L/K); consequently the fields K(f^{-n}(α)) and K(ψ^{-n}(α')) coincide for every n, the level images G_n(f, α) and G_n(ψ, α') correspond, and (f, α) is stable iff (ψ, α') is. In particular every quadratic f = ax² + bx + c over a field of characteristic ≠ 2 is conjugate over K to a monic quadratic (x − γ)² + δ (take u = a^{-1}), and α can be moved to 0 (take v = α).
hypotheses: h is affine and defined over K (u ∈ Kˣ, v ∈ K).
proofSteps: ψⁿ = h^{-1} ∘ fⁿ ∘ h by induction, so fⁿ(y) = α iff ψⁿ(h^{-1}(y)) = α'; apply preimageTree.iso with the bijection h^{-1} of L.
Galois equivariance: σ(h^{-1}(y)) = h^{-1}(σ y) because u, v ∈ K.
Fields: h^{-1}(y) ∈ K(y) and y ∈ K(h^{-1}(y)).

nodes.title: The Galois action on the preimage tree
nodes.statement: Let K ⊆ L be fields, f ∈ K[x] and α ∈ K. Every σ ∈ Gal(L/K) = (L ≃ₐ[K] L) maps level n of T(f, α; L) to itself by x ↦ σ(x) and commutes with the parent maps, because σ(f(x)) = f(σ(x)) and σ(α) = α. This defines a group homomorphism galoisTreeAction : Gal(L/K) → Aut(T(f, α; L)). On level n it agrees with Mathlib's Polynomial.Gal.galActionHom of fⁿ − α composed with the restriction Polynomial.Gal.restrict, when fⁿ − α splits over L.
hypotheses: None for the construction.
The comparison with galActionHom needs fⁿ − α to split over L.
proofSteps: σ(aeval x f) = aeval (σ x) f (Polynomial.aeval_algHom_apply), so σ commutes with y ↦ f(y) and fixes algebraMap α; hence σ^[n]-compatibility and σ maps g^{-n}(α) to itself. Levelwise permutations with inverse σ^{-1}.
Homomorphism: levelwise, (στ)(x) = σ(τ(x)).
levelHom_galoisTreeAction_coe: by construction the level-n action is σ on the underlying element of L.
Comparison: Polynomial.Gal.galActionHom_restrict gives galActionHom (fⁿ − α) L (restrict σ) x = σ x; both sides are σ x.

nodes.title: Preimage trees of rational maps of P¹ and their Galois action
nodes.statement: Let φ : P¹ → P¹ be a rational map of degree d ≥ 2 defined over a field K (ArithmeticDynamics:DY.0/rational-map-of-the-projective-line) and α ∈ P¹(K). The preimage tree T(φ, α) := preimageTree applied to the action of φ on P¹(K^sep) and the point α carries an action of Gal(K^sep/K) by tree automorphisms, and it is d-regular with dⁿ vertices at level n exactly when φⁿ(x) = α has dⁿ distinct solutions in P¹(K̄) for every n ≥ 1 (and these then lie in P¹(K^sep)). For a polynomial φ = f and α ∈ K (α ≠ ∞) it is T(f, α; K^sep) of DY.5/preimage-tree, since ∞ is totally invariant.
hypotheses: φ of degree d ≥ 2 over K; the regularity clause assumes dⁿ distinct solutions of φⁿ(x) = α for every n.
proofSteps: φ commutes with σ ∈ Gal(K^sep/K) acting on P¹(K^sep) coordinatewise, because the coefficients of the two defining forms of φ lie in K; so galois equivariance gives a homomorphism to Aut(T(φ, α)) exactly as in galois-action-on-preimage-tree.

If φⁿ(x) = α has dⁿ distinct solutions in P¹(K̄), each is separable over K (a simple root of the numerator of φⁿ − α) and so lies in P¹(K^sep); every vertex at level n has d children because level n + 1 has dⁿ⁺¹ elements and each fibre has at most d.
For polynomials the point ∞ is fixed with φ^{-1}(∞) = {∞}, so α ≠ ∞ has no preimage at ∞ and T(φ, α) = T(f, α; K^sep).
acceptance: φ(x) = (x² + 1)/x (the survey's example (d), commuting with x ↦ −x): the tree over α = 0 is defined and its level 1 is {±i}.
For a polynomial, the tree agrees with the polynomial preimage tree.

nodes.title: The arboreal Galois representation ρ : Gal(K^sep/K) → Aut(T_∞(f, α))
nodes.statement: For a field K, f ∈ K[x] and α ∈ K, the arboreal Galois representation is ρ = arborealRep K f α := galoisTreeAction for L = K^sep (Mathlib's SeparableClosure K), a homomorphism Gal(K^sep/K) → Aut(T(f, α; K^sep)); its source is TauCeti.AbsoluteGaloisGroup K = Gal(SeparableClosure K/K) by definition, identified with Mathlib's Field.absoluteGaloisGroup K by TauCeti.absoluteGaloisGroupRestrictEquiv. Its image is the arboreal image G_∞(f, α) := im ρ ≤ Aut(T_∞), and its level-n image is G_n(f, α) := im(truncate_n ∘ ρ) ≤ Aut(T_n). Under the non-collision condition T_∞ ≅ T^d (DY.5/preimage-tree-regular), so G_∞(f, α) is a subgroup of Aut(T^d_∞) determined up to conjugacy.
hypotheses: No hypotheses for the definition; the comparison statements assume fⁿ − α separable (so that the whole level lies in K^sep).
proofSteps: Definition: arborealRep := galoisTreeAction K (SeparableClosure K) f α; arborealImage := range; levelImage n := range of (Aut.truncate n) ∘ arborealRep.

nodes.title: The fields K_n = K(f^{-n}(α)) and K_∞
nodes.statement: For a field K, f ∈ K[x] and α ∈ K, K_n = preimageField K f α n is the intermediate field of K^sep/K generated by the roots of fⁿ(x) − α in K^sep, and K_∞ = ⨆_n K_n. If fⁿ − α is separable, K_n is a splitting field of fⁿ − α over K, finite and Galois, and its fixing subgroup in Gal(K^sep/K) is the kernel of the action on level n. Under separability for all n (and deg f ≥ 1), K_n ⊆ K_{n+1} and [K_{n+1} : K_n] ≤ (d!)^{dⁿ}.
hypotheses: Splitting-field, Galois and tower statements assume the relevant fⁿ − α separable; the fixing-subgroup statement assumes deg f ≥ 1.
proofSteps: preimageField := IntermediateField.adjoin K (rootSet (fⁿ − α) K^sep).
IsSplittingField: IntermediateField.adjoin_rootSet_isSplittingField, since a separable polynomial splits over K^sep.
IsGalois: IsGalois.of_separable_splitting_field.
Monotonicity: every β ∈ V_n is f(y) for some y ∈ V_{n+1} (separability of f − β, DY.5/preimage-tree-regular), so β ∈ K_{n+1}.
Degree bound: K_{n+1} = K_n(roots of f(x) − β : β ∈ V_n); each adjunction of the d roots of f − β has degree ≤ d! over the previous field, and |V_n| ≤ dⁿ.
fixingSubgroup: σ fixes K_n iff σ fixes every root at level n iff σ acts trivially on V_n.
acceptance: K_0 = K; for z ↦ z² over ℚ at 1, K_2 = ℚ(i) of degree 2.
For z ↦ z³ over ℚ at 2, K_1 is the splitting field of x³ − 2, of degree 6, not ℚ(∛2).

nodes.title: G_∞ is closed, equals Gal(K_∞/K), and is the inverse limit of the G_n
nodes.statement: Assume deg f ≥ 1 and fⁿ − α separable for all n. Then: (i) ker ρ is the fixing subgroup of K_∞; (ii) G_∞(f, α) is a closed subgroup of Aut(T), and ρ induces an isomorphism of topological groups Gal(K_∞/K) ≃ₜ* G_∞(f, α); (iii) G_∞ = {σ ∈ Aut(T) : truncate_n(σ) ∈ G_n for all n} = lim_n G_n. In particular ρ is surjective iff G_n = Aut(T_n) for every n.
hypotheses: deg f ≥ 1; fⁿ − α separable for all n.
proofSteps: (i): σ ∈ ker ρ iff σ fixes every level iff σ fixes every K_n iff σ fixes K_∞.

(ii): Gal(K^sep/K) is compact (Mathlib's CompactSpace instance for Galois extensions, found by instance inference) and Aut(T) is Hausdorff, so the image of the continuous map ρ (arboreal-representation-continuous) is compact, hence closed; ρ factors through Gal(K^sep/K)/ker ρ ≅ Gal(K_∞/K) (InfiniteGalois.normalAutEquivQuotient, K_∞/K normal), giving a continuous bijection from a compact to a Hausdorff space, a homeomorphism.
(iii): ⊆ is clear; for ⊇, a closed subgroup is the inverse limit of its truncations (tree-automorphism-inverse-limit), and the truncations of G_∞ are the G_n.
Surjectivity: if every G_n = Aut(T_n) then (iii) gives G_∞ = Aut(T).
acceptance: For x² + 1 over ℚ at 0, G_∞ = Aut(T_∞) (worked example).
For x² − 2 over ℚ at 0, G_∞ is procyclic (≅ ℤ_2), of infinite index.

nodes.title: Finite levels as finite étale K-schemes
nodes.statement: Let K be a field, f ∈ K[x] of degree ≥ 1 and α ∈ K with fⁿ − α separable. Under the field-case equivalence between finite étale K-schemes and finite continuous Gal(K^sep/K)-sets (Tau Ceti ModularCurves layer 0D), the finite étale K-scheme X_n := Spec K[x]/(fⁿ(x) − α) (the fibre over α of the iterate fⁿ : A¹_K → A¹_K) corresponds to level n of the preimage tree with the action levelHom n ∘ ρ, and the K-morphism X_{n+1} → X_n induced by x ↦ f(x) corresponds to the parent map. The tower (X_n) is thus the finite étale incarnation of T(f, α; K^sep), and ρ is the action of π₁(Spec K) = Gal(K^sep/K) on it.
hypotheses: fⁿ − α (and f^{n+1} − α for the morphism) separable, so that X_n is finite étale over K.
proofSteps: X_n is finite étale because K[x]/(fⁿ − α) is a finite product of finite separable field extensions (separability).

Its K^sep-points are the K-algebra maps K[x]/(fⁿ − α) → K^sep, i.e. the roots of fⁿ − α in K^sep, with the Galois action by composition: this is level n with levelHom n ∘ ρ (DY.5/arboreal-image-finite-level).
The ring map K[x]/(fⁿ − α) → K[x]/(f^{n+1} − α), x ↦ f(x), is well defined since f^{n+1} − α = (fⁿ − α) ∘ f; on K^sep-points it is β ↦ f(β), the parent map.
Functoriality of the ModularCurves 0D equivalence.
acceptance: n = 0: X_0 = Spec K, the one-point Galois set (the root).
f = x², α = 1, K = ℚ: X_2 = Spec ℚ[x]/(x⁴ − 1) = Spec(ℚ × ℚ × ℚ(i)), with Galois set {1, −1, i, −i}.

nodes.title: Capelli's lemma
nodes.statement: Let K be a field, g, h ∈ K[x] with g ≠ 0 and deg h ≥ 1, and let β be a root of g in some field extension L of K. Then g(h(x)) is irreducible over K if and only if g is irreducible over K and h(x) − β is irreducible over K(β).
hypotheses: deg h ≥ 1 (if h is constant, g ∘ h is constant and the statement degenerates).
β is any root of g in any extension; when g is irreducible all roots are conjugate, so the condition does not depend on the choice.
proofSteps: ⇐: for monic g, h this is Mathlib's Polynomial.irreducible_comp; the general case follows by scaling g and h to monic polynomials (irreducibility is invariant under units and under the substitution x ↦ ux).
⇒, g irreducible: a factorization g = g₁g₂ into non-units gives g ∘ h = (g₁ ∘ h)(g₂ ∘ h) into non-units since deg h ≥ 1.

⇒, h − β irreducible: let γ be a root of h(x) − β in an extension; then γ is a root of g ∘ h, so [K(γ) : K] = deg g · deg h (g ∘ h irreducible), while K(β) ⊆ K(γ) because β = h(γ), [K(β) : K] = deg g (g irreducible) and [K(γ) : K(β)] ≤ deg h (IntermediateField.adjoin.finrank, Module.finrank_mul_finrank). Equality forces [K(γ) : K(β)] = deg h, so h − β, of degree deg h with root γ, is the minimal polynomial of γ over K(β) up to a unit, hence irreducible.
acceptance: g = x² + 1, h = x² over ℚ: g ∘ h = x⁴ + 1 is irreducible, and x² − i is irreducible over ℚ(i).
g = x² − 2, h = x² over ℚ: x⁴ − 2 irreducible, and x² − √2 irreducible over ℚ(√2).

nodes.title: Stable pairs: all iterates fⁿ − α irreducible
nodes.statement: Let K be a field, f ∈ K[x] and α ∈ K. The pair (f, α) is stable over K (IsStableAt f α) if fⁿ(x) − α is irreducible over K for every n ≥ 1. For α = 0 this is Jones's 'f is stable'; in Jones's terminology (f, α) is stable iff x − α is f-stable. By Capelli's lemma irreducibility of f^N − α implies irreducibility of fⁿ − α for all 1 ≤ n ≤ N, so stability is the irreducibility of a cofinal set of iterates.
hypotheses: No hypotheses.
proofSteps: Definition: ∀ n ≥ 1, Irreducible (fⁿ − C α).

nodes.title: The adjusted critical orbit of a quadratic polynomial
nodes.statement: For a commutative ring R, f ∈ R[x], γ, α ∈ R and n ∈ ℕ, adjustedCriticalOrbit f γ α n is c_1 := α − f(γ) for n = 1 and c_n := fⁿ(γ) − α for n ≠ 1 (so c_0 = γ − α is a junk value). For a monic quadratic f = (x − γ)² + δ over a field, γ is the critical point, c_1 = α − δ and c_n = fⁿ(γ) − α for n ≥ 2; for α = 0 the sequence is Jones's adjusted critical orbit −f(γ), f²(γ), f³(γ), …, and for f = x² + a, γ = α = 0 it is Stoll's sequence c_1 = −a, c_{n+1} = c_n² + a (with c_0 = 0).
hypotheses: Pinned sign: c_1 = −(f(γ) − α), so that c_1 is a square in K_1 (Stoll's remark after Lemma 1.5).
proofSteps: Definition by cases on n = 1.
adjustedCriticalOrbit_ne_zero_iff: for char K ≠ 2 the only critical point of (x − γ)² + δ is γ, and f^k(γ) = α iff c_k = 0 (c_1 = α − f(γ)); apply DY.5/separable-iterates-criterion.

nodes.title: Jones's stability step for quadratic iterates
nodes.statement: Let K be a field of characteristic ≠ 2, f = (x − γ)² + δ ∈ K[x], α ∈ K and n ≥ 0. If fⁿ − α is irreducible over K and c_{n+1} is not a square in K, then f^{n+1} − α is irreducible over K. (For n = 0 this says: f − α is irreducible if α − δ is not a square; the converse also holds there.)
hypotheses: char K ≠ 2; f monic quadratic.
Only monic f is covered: for a non-monic quadratic the correct condition involves the leading coefficient (see ArithmeticDynamics/E603); reduce to the monic case by affine-conjugation-invariance.
proofSteps: By Capelli's lemma with g = fⁿ − α and h = f: f^{n+1} − α = g ∘ f is irreducible if g is irreducible and f(x) − β = (x − γ)² − (β − δ) is irreducible over K(β) for a root β of g.
x² − a is irreducible over a field iff a is not a square (X_pow_sub_C_irreducible_iff_of_prime with p = 2), and the substitution x ↦ x − γ preserves irreducibility.
If β − δ = s² in K(β) then c_{n+1} = N_{K(β)/K}(β − δ) = N(s)² is a square in K (shifted-root-product); contradiction.
acceptance: x² + 1 over ℚ at 0: every c_n is a non-square, so every iterate is irreducible.
x² + 3 over ℚ at 0: c_3 = 147 = 7²·3 is not a square, so f³ is irreducible (while G_3 ≠ Aut(T_3)).

nodes.title: K_{n+1} is a 2-Kummer extension of K_n
nodes.statement: Let K be a field of characteristic ≠ 2, f = (x − γ)² + δ ∈ K[x], α ∈ K, and assume f^{n+1} − α separable. Then K_{n+1} = K_n(y_β − γ : β ∈ V_n), where for each root β of fⁿ − α, y_β is a root of f(x) − β (so (y_β − γ)² = β − δ). Hence K_{n+1}/K_n is generated by the square roots of the 2ⁿ elements β − δ ∈ K_n, [K_{n+1} : K_n] ≤ 2^{2ⁿ}, and Gal(K_{n+1}/K_n) is an elementary abelian 2-group, equal to the kernel of G_{n+1} → G_n.
hypotheses: char K ≠ 2; f monic quadratic; f^{n+1} − α separable.
proofSteps: The roots of f^{n+1} − α are the y with f(y) ∈ V_n, i.e. (y − γ)² = β − δ; K_{n+1} is generated over K by these, and contains K_n since β = f(y).
Multiquadratic degree bound: adjoining r square roots has degree ≤ 2^r (TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_adjoin_range_eq_two_pow_finrank_span_squareClass, with r = 2ⁿ).
Each element of Gal(K_{n+1}/K_n) sends y_β − γ to ±(y_β − γ), hence has order ≤ 2; commutativity follows.

nodes.title: Invariant vectors of 2-groups in permutation modules
nodes.statement: Let G be a finite 2-group acting transitively on a finite set X, and let W ⊆ (X → F_2) be a nonzero F_2-subspace stable under the permutation action (w ↦ w ∘ g^{-1}). Then the constant function 1 lies in W.

proofSteps: W is a finite set of cardinality a power of 2 with a G-action; |W| ≡ |W^G| (mod 2) (IsPGroup.card_modEq_card_fixedPoints), and 0 ∈ W^G, so W^G contains a nonzero w (IsPGroup.exists_fixed_point_of_prime_dvd_card_of_fixed_point).
A G-invariant function on X is constant on G-orbits; X is one orbit, so w is constant and nonzero, i.e. w = 1.

nodes.title: The Kummer step: [K_{n+1} : K_n] is maximal iff c_{n+1} is not a square in K_n
nodes.statement: Let K be a field of characteristic ≠ 2, f = (x − γ)² + δ ∈ K[x], α ∈ K and n ≥ 0. Assume fⁿ − α is irreducible over K and c_{n+1} ≠ 0. Then [K_{n+1} : K_n] = 2^{2ⁿ} (equivalently Gal(K_{n+1}/K_n) is the whole kernel of Aut(T_{n+1}) → Aut(T_n), 'H_{n+1} maximal') if and only if c_{n+1} is not a square in K_n.
hypotheses: char K ≠ 2; fⁿ − α irreducible (so G_n acts transitively on V_n); c_{n+1} ≠ 0 (so f^{n+1} − α is separable).
proofSteps: By quadratic-level-kummer-generation and the multiquadratic degree formula, [K_{n+1} : K_n] = 2^{2ⁿ − dim R}, where R ⊆ F_2^{V_n} is the space of relations: ε with ∏_β (β − δ)^{ε_β} a square in K_n (TauCeti.Multiquadratic.finrank_adjoin_range_eq_two_pow_finrank_span_squareClass, TauCeti.linearIndependent_squareClass_iff).

R is stable under G_n = Gal(K_n/K), which permutes the β − δ; fⁿ − α is separable (an irreducible polynomial of degree 2ⁿ is separable in characteristic ≠ 2), so G_n ≤ Aut(T_n) is a 2-group (tree-automorphism-order) acting transitively on V_n (level-transitivity-iff-irreducible).

nodes.title: A square root of c_n in K_n, transformed by the level-n sign
nodes.statement: Let K be a field of characteristic ≠ 2, f = (x − γ)² + δ ∈ K[x], α ∈ K, n ≥ 1, with fⁿ − α separable. Choose for each β ∈ V_{n−1} a child y_β ∈ V_n and put s_n := ∏_{β ∈ V_{n−1}} (y_β − γ) ∈ K_n. Then s_n² = c_n, and for every σ ∈ Gal(K^sep/K), σ(s_n) = sign(σ|V_n) · s_n, where sign(σ|V_n) is the sign of the permutation of level n induced by ρ(σ). In particular c_n is a square in K_n, and K(√c_n) ⊆ K_n is the fixed field of the kernel of χ_n ∘ ρ.
hypotheses: char K ≠ 2; f monic quadratic; n ≥ 1; fⁿ − α separable.
proofSteps: s_n² = ∏_β (y_β − γ)² = ∏_β (β − δ) = c_n (shifted-root-product).
The two children of β are γ ± (y_β − γ). σ sends y_β to a child of σβ, so σ(y_β − γ) = ε_β (y_{σβ} − γ) with ε_β = ±1, and σ(s_n) = (∏_β ε_β) s_n.

The permutation of V_n induced by σ is the composite of the 'label-preserving' permutation y_β ↦ y_{σβ}, 2γ − y_β ↦ 2γ − y_{σβ} (two copies of the permutation of V_{n−1}, hence even) with the transpositions {y_β, 2γ − y_β} for ε_β = −1; its sign is ∏ ε_β.
acceptance: n = 1: s_1 = y − γ with (y − γ)² = α − δ = c_1, and σ(s_1) = −s_1 iff σ swaps the two level-1 vertices.

nodes.title: Stoll's maximality criterion
nodes.statement: Let K be a field of characteristic ≠ 2, f = (x − γ)² + δ ∈ K[x], α ∈ K and n ≥ 0 with fⁿ − α separable. Then G_n(f, α) = Aut(T_n) (equivalently [K_n : K] = 2^{2ⁿ−1}) if and only if c_1, …, c_n are 2-independent in K: no nonempty subproduct ∏_{i∈S} c_i, S ⊆ {1, …, n}, is a square in K (equivalently, the classes of c_1, …, c_n in Kˣ/Kˣ² are F_2-linearly independent: TauCeti.linearIndependent_squareClass_iff).
hypotheses: char K ≠ 2; f monic quadratic (any quadratic reduces to this by affine-conjugation-invariance); fⁿ − α separable.
proofSteps: Induction on n; n = 0 is trivial. Assume the equivalence at n.

(Stoll Lemma 1.4) G_{n+1} = Aut(T_{n+1}) iff G_n = Aut(T_n) and [K_{n+1} : K_n] = 2^{2ⁿ}, since |Aut(T_{n+1})| = |Aut(T_n)| · 2^{2ⁿ} (tree-automorphism-order), |G_{n+1}| = |G_n| [K_{n+1} : K_n] (arboreal-image-finite-level) and [K_{n+1} : K_n] ≤ 2^{2ⁿ}.

If c_1, …, c_{n+1} are independent, each c_i is a non-square, so (f, α) is stable up to n + 1 (quadratic-stability-criterion) and stoll-kummer-step applies: [K_{n+1}:K_n] = 2^{2ⁿ} iff c_{n+1} is not a square in K_n.

(Stoll Lemma 1.5) If G_n = Aut(T_n) and c_1, …, c_n are independent then for c ∈ Kˣ: c is a square in K_n iff c_1, …, c_n, c are dependent. ⇐: c ≡ ∏_{i∈S} c_i mod squares and each c_i is a square in K_n (square-root-of-adjusted-critical-value). ⇒: K(√c_1, …, √c_n) ⊆ K_n has degree 2ⁿ (independence, multiquadratic degree formula), and every subfield of K_n generated by square roots of elements of K has degree ≤ #Hom(Gal(K_n/K), ±1) = 2ⁿ (binary-tree-sign-characters, as G_n = Aut(T_n)); so √c ∈ K(√c_1, …, √c_n) and square descent (TauCeti.Multiquadratic.squareClass_of_sq_mem_fintype) gives c ∏_{i∈S} c_i ∈ Kˣ².
Combine: G_{n+1} maximal iff c_1..c_n independent and c_{n+1} not a square in K_n iff c_1, …, c_{n+1} independent.
The equivalence of square-free subproducts with linear independence of square classes is TauCeti.linearIndependent_squareClass_iff.

nodes.statement: Let a ∈ ℤ with −a not a square and c the critical orbit of x² + a. More precisely, for each prime p dividing some c_n, with m = min{n : p ∣ c_n} and e = v_p(c_m): v_p(c_n) = e if m ∣ n and 0 otherwise, so p divides b_m and no other b_n.

Then v_p(b_n) = Σ_{d∣n} μ(n/d) v_p(c_d) = e Σ_{t ∣ n/m} μ(n/(mt)) = e·[n = m]; so each prime divides exactly one b_n.

nodes.title: Stoll's Theorem (Section 1): maximality from non-square Möbius factors
nodes.statement: Let a ∈ ℤ with −a not a square, f = x² + a over ℚ, α = 0 and n ≥ 1. (1) G_n(f, 0) = Aut(T_n) iff b_1, …, b_n are 2-independent in ℚ. (2) If none of |b_2|, …, |b_n| is a square in ℚ, then G_n(f, 0) = Aut(T_n).
hypotheses: a ∈ ℤ, −a not a square (this is also the irreducibility of every f_n with n ≥ 1).
proofSteps: (1): by stoll-maximality-criterion, G_n maximal iff c_1, …, c_n are 2-independent; the classes of c_1, …, c_n and of b_1, …, b_n in ℚˣ/ℚˣ² span the same F_2-subspace (c_m = ∏_{d∣m} b_d and b_m = ∏ c_d^{μ(m/d)}), so one family is independent iff the other is.

(2): the b_m are pairwise coprime integers (critical-orbit-mobius-factors), and a square product of pairwise coprime integers has every factor a square up to sign; so b_1, …, b_n are 2-independent iff none of the b_m is a square and at most one of the −b_m is a square. Here b_1 = −a is not a square; if moreover no |b_m| with m ≥ 2 is a square then no b_m and no −b_m with m ≥ 2 is a square, and the family is 2-independent.
Pass from (1).

a = 3: b_2 = c_2/c_1 = 12/(−3) = −4 has |b_2| = 4 a square; the criterion (2) does not apply at n = 2, although G_2 is maximal by (1) (b_1 = −3, b_2 = −4: −3, −4, 12 are non-squares).

nodes.title: Stoll's Lemma 2.1: a congruence criterion for non-square Möbius quotients
nodes.statement: Let g ∈ ℤ[x] be even (g(−x) = g(x)), and let (γ_n)_{n≥1} be integers with γ_1 = ±g(0), γ_{n+1} = g(γ_n) and all γ_n ≠ 0; put β_n = ∏_{d∣n} γ_d^{μ(n/d)}. Suppose that for every n ≥ 1 there is m ∈ ℕ with m ∣ γ_n + γ_{2n}, m coprime to γ_n, and −1 not a square in ℤ/mℤ. Then β_n is not a square in ℚ for every n ≥ 2.
hypotheses: g even; the recursion; γ_n ≠ 0; the existence of the moduli m.
proofSteps: Write n = n'k with n' = rad(n) > 1; take m for the index k and put A = γ_{2k}. Then γ_k ≡ −A (mod m); since the k-fold iterate g_k of g is even, γ_{3k} = g_k(γ_{2k}) ≡ g_k(−γ_k) = g_k(γ_k) = γ_{2k} = A (mod m), and by induction γ_{tk} ≡ A (mod m) for t ≥ 2.

β_n = ∏_{t ∣ n'} γ_{kt}^{μ(n'/t)} (only squarefree quotients n/d contribute). Modulo m the factor with t = 1 is γ_k^{μ(n')} ≡ (−A)^{μ(n')} and every other factor is A^{μ(n'/t)}; since μ(n') = ±1 and Σ_{t∣n'} μ(n'/t) = 0, splitting the divisors of n' by the sign of μ(n'/t) (two sets of equal size) writes β_n = P/Q with P ≡ −Q (mod m) and Q a unit mod m.
If P/Q = (u/v)² in ℚ, clearing denominators and reducing modulo m (Q invertible, P ≡ −Q) makes −1 a square in ℤ/mℤ, a contradiction.

nodes.title: Stoll's Lemma 2.2: congruence conditions giving the moduli
nodes.statement: In the setting of even-sequence-nonsquare-criterion, suppose all γ_n > 0 and either (a) g(0) = 1 and g(1) ≡ 2 (mod 4), or (b) g(0) = ±1 and g(1) ≡ 3 (mod 4). Then β_n is not a square in ℚ for every n ≥ 2.

nodes.title: Stoll's theorem: surjective arboreal representations for x² + a over ℚ
nodes.statement: Let a ∈ ℤ with (a) a > 0 and a ≡ 1 (mod 4), or (b) a > 0 and a ≡ 2 (mod 4), or (c) a < 0, a ≡ 0 (mod 4) and −a not a square. Rescale: g := |a| x² + sgn(a), an even integer polynomial; with γ_1 := 1 its iteration sequence satisfies γ_n |a| = |c_n| for n ≥ 1 (induction), so γ_n > 0 (critical-orbit-positivity) and β_n = |b_n| for n ≥ 2 (the Möbius exponents sum to zero for n ≥ 2, so the factors |a| cancel).

nodes.title: The discriminant recursion for iterates
nodes.statement: Let K be a field, f ∈ K[x] of degree d with leading coefficient a and (d : K) ≠ 0, α ∈ K, and let R be the multiset of roots of f' in an algebraically closed L ⊇ K (the critical points with multiplicity). With Mathlib's discriminant Polynomial.discr and A = (−1)^{d(d−1)/2} d^d a^{d−1}: Disc(f^{n+1} − α) = A^{dⁿ} · a^{(dⁿ − 1)(dⁿ⁺¹ + 1)} · Disc(fⁿ − α)^d · ∏_{r ∈ R} (f^{n+1}(r) − α). For monic f (a = 1) this is Aitken–Hajir–Maire's Proposition 3.2 (specialized at t = α); for a ≠ 1 the factor a^{(dⁿ−1)(dⁿ⁺¹+1)} corrects it (ArithmeticDynamics/E601).
hypotheses: (d : K) ≠ 0, so that f' = d·a·∏_{r∈R}(x − r) has degree d − 1.
Mathlib's Polynomial.discr, equal to lc^{2m−2} ∏_{i<j} (ζ_i − ζ_j)² for degree m.
proofSteps: For a polynomial P of degree m, leading coefficient ℓ and roots ζ_i in L: Disc(P) = (−1)^{m(m−1)/2} ℓ^{m−2} ∏_i P'(ζ_i) (Polynomial.resultant_deriv and Polynomial.resultant_eq_prod_eval; for monic P, Polynomial.Monic.prod_roots_eval_derivative).

With h_n = fⁿ − α (degree dⁿ, leading coefficient ℓ_n = a^{(dⁿ−1)/(d−1)}, ℓ_{n+1} = a ℓ_n^d): h_{n+1}' = f' · (h_n' ∘ f) (derivative-of-iterate), and as ζ runs over the roots of h_{n+1}, f(ζ) runs over the roots of h_n, each d times; so ∏_ζ h_{n+1}'(ζ) = ∏_ζ f'(ζ) · (∏_β h_n'(β))^d.
Collect signs and leading coefficients; the power of a is (d−1)dⁿ (from A^{dⁿ}) plus (dⁿ−1)(dⁿ⁺¹+1).

nodes.title: Jones's ramification criterion for maximality
nodes.statement: Let f = x² + bx + c with b, c ∈ ℤ, γ = −b/2, α ∈ ℤ and n ≥ 1, with fⁿ − α irreducible over ℚ. If there is an odd prime p with v_p(c_{n+1}) odd and v_p(c_k) = 0 for 1 ≤ k ≤ n, then [K_{n+1} : K_n] = 2^{2ⁿ}, i.e. H_{n+1} = Gal(K_{n+1}/K_n) is maximal (the whole kernel of Aut(T_{n+1}) → Aut(T_n)). In words: a primitive prime divisor of the adjusted critical orbit appearing to odd multiplicity forces a new maximal Kummer layer.

nodes.title: The index recursion for level images

nodes.title: The index of G_∞ in Aut(T_∞)
nodes.statement: Assume deg f = d ≥ 1 and fⁿ − α separable for all n. Then G_∞(f, α) has finite index in Aut(T_∞) iff the sequence [Aut(T_n) : G_n] is bounded, iff [K_{n+1} : K_n] = (d!)^{dⁿ} for all sufficiently large n; and then [Aut(T_∞) : G_∞] = sup_n [Aut(T_n) : G_n] = lim_n [Aut(T_n) : G_n]. Boundedness of a non-decreasing integer sequence is eventual constancy; level-index-recursion translates constancy into maximal relative degrees.

nodes.title: Level images shrink under base extension
nodes.statement: Let E/K be a field extension, f ∈ K[x] and α ∈ K with fⁿ − α separable for all n. Then there is an isomorphism of level towers T(f, α; E^sep) ≅ T(f, α; K^sep) under which the level image G_N(f, α) over E is carried into G_N(f, α) over K, for every N; equivalently Gal(fᴺ − α / E) is a subgroup of Gal(fᴺ − α / K) compatibly with the root actions.

ι maps the roots of fⁿ − α in K^sep bijectively to those in E^sep (both have dⁿ elements, preimage-tree-regular) and commutes with f: a tree isomorphism (preimageTree.iso).
Every τ ∈ Gal(E^sep/E) stabilizes ι(K^sep) (normality of K^sep/K) and restricts to an element of Gal(K^sep/K) acting compatibly on the levels.

Then there is an isomorphism of level towers T(f̄, ᾱ; κ^sep) ≅ T(f, α; F^sep) carrying the level image G_N(f̄, ᾱ) over κ into G_N(f, α) over F, for every N.
